So how should i demonstrate the ai agent?

For the judges, the demo has to visibly hit the track's three 基础要求 — framework on hardware, custom Skill, proactive+execution — and it has to be *unfakeable*. Here's the run I'd record.

## The setup shot (30 s)

Board powered, LCD in frame showing the VelaPaw UI, serial console beside it. This matters: it establishes that the feeder app and the agent are the same device, not a PC pretending.

**On the board console** — reset, three Enters for `nsh>`, then:

```
ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1
ai_agent &
```

Then a host→board ping to prime ARP before anything hits the network, or the first request stalls with no timeout. Check the ping's **reply source**, not "0% loss" — a `Tentative` `Ethernet 2` silently routes it into the VPN and everything downstream fails confusingly.

Wait for the `vela>` prompt. Do **not** type `velapaw &` — it's already running from boot autostart, and a second instance wedges the console into a reset-tap recovery on camera.

## Act 1 — the Skill is real (1 min)

Point the camera at the console line **`Skills summary: NNN bytes`**. That's the load-bearing signal that your Skill file was read off `/data/ai_agent/skills/`. (`Skills system ready (N built-in)` looks better but is a compile-time constant — it prints whether or not your skill loaded.)

Then ask something whose answer only your device knows:

```
ask how much did bob eat today and is that normal for him
```

**Never demo with `ask hello`** — that one's cache-poisoned, and a judge who asks you to run it twice gets a byte-identical reply. Expect two `[Agent]:` lines: a placeholder, then the real answer 4–35 s later. Say that out loud in the video so the first line doesn't read as the answer.

## Act 2 — the proof it's not canned (2 min, and this is the one that wins it)

This is the strongest thing you have, so give it the most screen time:

1. **Feed a pet on the LCD** — on camera, with the stepper actually turning.
2. Show the number change on the Trends tab.
3. Wait for the next heartbeat firing (3 min in the flashed build).
4. The push comes back **with the new number in it.**

No cached reply and no hardcoded demo string can survive that, because the data didn't exist when the recording started. It simultaneously proves proactive firing, real device-data reading, and live LLM execution — all three requirements in one unbroken take.

## Act 3 — the offline claim (30 s)

Pull the network. Feed a pet — recognition, schedule, portion, dispense, history all still work. `ask` doesn't. This is exactly what §4 of the README now claims, demonstrated rather than asserted, and it turns "needs internet" from a weakness into a designed boundary.

## What to avoid

| Don't | Why |
|---|---|
| `ask hello` | cached — reproducibly identical, reads as fake |
| `velapaw &` | second instance wedges the console |
| Cutting between Act 2's steps | the unbroken take *is* the proof |
| Quoting the 30-minute interval | the build fires at 3 min; say so and explain why |

One caveat on Act 2: the heartbeat only pushes when a pet **crosses a concern threshold** — a quiet device means nothing is wrong. So pick the pet and portion deliberately so the feeding you do on camera actually trips it, or you'll be filming three minutes of silence. Bob at 20 g / 66 % of baseline has room; jay is already at 171 %.

Then Act 2 as I described it can't go in the video — the 3-minute heartbeat wait alone eats three times your budget. Here's how I'd spend the minute.

## First: check whether it really is only a minute

Most 4-minute hardware demos have 30–60 s of slack in them — boot sequences, repeated enrollment shots, a slow pan of the enclosure. Reclaiming 45 s there is usually easier than compressing the agent into 60, and it's the cheapest edit you can make. Worth one pass through the existing cut before you design around a hard 60 s.

## The 60-second cut

One unbroken take, board and console both in frame:

| Time | Shot | Requirement it satisfies |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:08 | Console already at `vela>`, `Skills summary: NNN bytes` visible | framework on hardware + custom Skill loaded |
| 0:08–0:22 | **Feed a pet on the LCD** — stepper turns, Trends number changes | creates data that didn't exist before the take |
| 0:22–0:38 | `ask how much did bob eat today` → answer quotes the number you just created | CLI channel, execution, reading real device data |
| 0:38–0:55 | Proactive digest fires, citing the same new number | proactive scenario |
| 0:55–1:00 | Caption: fires unattended on a timer — full logs in `docs/AI_AGENT.md` | — |

The reason to keep the feed-first structure even when compressed: **the number in the reply cannot have been pre-recorded**, because you created it fifteen seconds earlier on camera. That single property is what separates your submission from one that shows a chatbot answering with plausible text. Don't trade it away for time.

## The problem: making 0:38 arrive on schedule

You need the proactive push on demand, and I can see two routes — but I want to flag honestly that **I couldn't confirm either from the repo just now.** I searched `agent/` and there's no `heartbeat_trigger` in the contest-repo copy; my note about that CLI is from the VM-side framework tree, so I don't currently know whether the *flashed* build exposes a manual trigger.

- **If a trigger command exists** — call it at 0:38, and caption it plainly as a manual trigger for time, with the unattended firing evidenced in the doc. Judges accept that; an uncaptioned one they'd be right to distrust.
- **If not** — drop the interval to ~45 s in a demo build, start the take, feed at 0:08, and let the natural firing land inside the window. Costs a rebuild and reflash.

Either way there's a constraint you can't edit around: the push only fires when a pet **crosses a concern threshold**. Pick the pet and portion so the on-camera feeding actually trips it — bob has headroom at 66 % of baseline; jay is already at 171 %.

## What moves out of the video

Act 3 (pull the network, feeder keeps feeding) doesn't fit and doesn't need to — §4 of the README now states the offline boundary in words, and your existing 4 minutes already show the feeder working as a self-contained appliance. """Answer two questions for the 60-second demo cut:

  1. Does the FLASHED build expose a manual heartbeat trigger at the vela>
     prompt?  (If yes, the proactive push can be summoned on cue instead of
     waiting out the 3-minute interval.)
  2. How long does one `ask` round-trip actually take, wall-clock, from
     keypress to the real (second) [Agent]: line?

Launches ai_agent only if it is not already up.  Never launches velapaw --
it auto-starts at boot and a second instance wedges the console.
Every write has a timeout: on a wedged CDC ACM console ser.write() blocks
for ever, which is how an earlier harness hung with no output.
"""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import serial
import serial.tools.list_ports

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RAW = os.path.join(HERE, "agent_demo_probe_raw.log")
PORT = "COM8"
BOARD_IP = "192.168.137.2"

ports = [p.device for p in serial.tools.list_ports.comports()]
print(f">>> ports: {ports}", flush=True)
if PORT not in ports:
    sys.exit(f"!!! {PORT} absent. ABORTING.")

lines = []
lock = threading.Lock()
stop = False
t0 = time.time()
fh = open(RAW, "wb")


def reader(s):
    buf = b""
    while not stop:
        try:
            chunk = s.read(4096)
        except Exception:
            break
        if not chunk:
            continue
        fh.write(chunk)
        fh.flush()
        buf += chunk
        while b"\n" in buf:
            one, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
            txt = one.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r")
            with lock:
                lines.append((time.time() - t0, txt))
            print(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] {txt}", flush=True)


ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 115200, timeout=0.2, write_timeout=10)
threading.Thread(target=reader, args=(ser,), daemon=True).start()


def send(cmd):
    print(f"\n>>> {cmd!r}", flush=True)
    try:
        ser.write((cmd + "\r\n").encode())
        return True
    except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
        print("!!! write timed out -- console not draining.", flush=True)
        return False


def since(mark):
    with lock:
        return "\n".join(t for _, t in lines[mark:])


def mark():
    with lock:
        return len(lines)


def wait_for(pat, timeout, m):
    """Wait until pat appears in output after mark m."""
    end = time.time() + timeout
    rx = re.compile(pat)
    while time.time() < end:
        if rx.search(since(m)):
            return True
        time.sleep(0.4)
    return False


# ---- wake the console -------------------------------------------------
m = mark()
for _ in range(3):
    if not send(""):
        sys.exit("!!! console wedged on wake.")
    time.sleep(1.2)
time.sleep(3)
probe = since(m)

at_vela = "vela>" in probe
at_nsh = "nsh>" in probe
print(f"\n### prompt: vela>={at_vela}  nsh>={at_nsh}", flush=True)
if not (at_vela or at_nsh):
    stop = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
    ser.close()
    fh.close()
    sys.exit("!!! no prompt -- console wedged. Reset the board.")

# ---- bring up ai_agent if needed --------------------------------------
if not at_vela:
    m = mark()
    send("ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1")
    time.sleep(6)

    print("\n### priming ARP from the host ...", flush=True)
    subprocess.run(["ping", "-n", "3", BOARD_IP],
                   capture_output=True, text=True)

    m = mark()
    send("ai_agent &")
    print("### waiting for the vela> prompt (up to 300 s) ...", flush=True)
    if not wait_for(r"vela>", 300, m):
        stop = True
        time.sleep(0.5)
        ser.close()
        fh.close()
        sys.exit("!!! ai_agent never reached vela>.")
    print("### vela> reached.", flush=True)
    time.sleep(2)
else:
    print("### ai_agent already running.", flush=True)
    subprocess.run(["ping", "-n", "3", BOARD_IP], capture_output=True, text=True)

# ---- Q1: is there a manual heartbeat trigger? -------------------------
print("\n########## Q1: command list ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
send("help")
time.sleep(8)
helptext = since(m)
print("\n--- help ---\n" + helptext, flush=True)

cands = sorted(set(re.findall(
    r"\b(heartbeat\w*|trigger\w*|\w*_trigger|push\w*|digest\w*|proactive\w*)\b",
    helptext, re.I)))
print(f"\n### trigger-ish tokens in help: {cands}", flush=True)

# ---- Q2: time one ask round-trip --------------------------------------
print("\n########## Q2: ask round-trip ##########", flush=True)
PROMPT = "ask in one short sentence how is bob doing on food right now"
m = mark()
t_send = time.time()
send(PROMPT)

agent_hits = []
end = time.time() + 240
while time.time() < end:
    with lock:
        rows = lines[m:]
    agent_hits = [(ts, tx) for ts, tx in rows if "[Agent]" in tx]
    if len(agent_hits) >= 2:
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)

print("\n--- ask output ---\n" + since(m), flush=True)
print("\n########## RESULT ##########", flush=True)
if len(agent_hits) >= 2:
    first = agent_hits[0][0] - (t_send - t0)
    real = agent_hits[-1][0] - (t_send - t0)
    print(f"placeholder [Agent]: line at  {first:6.1f} s", flush=True)
    print(f"real        [Agent]: line at  {real:6.1f} s", flush=True)
elif len(agent_hits) == 1:
    only = agent_hits[0][0] - (t_send - t0)
    print(f"only ONE [Agent]: line, at {only:.1f} s "
          f"-- second never arrived in 240 s", flush=True)
else:
    print("no [Agent]: line at all within 240 s", flush=True)

time.sleep(2)
stop = True
time.sleep(0.5)
ser.close()
fh.close()
print(f"\n>>> raw: {RAW}", flush=True)

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**

- NuttX RTOS on ESP32-S3 (8 MB PSRAM, 16 MB flash), built in a VMware Linux VM (`king@king-VMware-Virtual-Platform`, `~/openvela`, VM IP `192.168.160.128`), flashed from Windows 11.
- **COM8** = NuttX CDCACM runtime console (`nsh>`/`vela>`). **COM3** = Espressif USB-Serial/JTAG ROM port. COM3-only = download mode; COM8-only = app booted. Re-enumeration after reset can take ~15 s.
- **esptool on Windows is `python -m esptool` (v5.3.1), NOT on PATH.** v5 uses hyphenated subcommands: `write-flash`, `flash-id`, `erase-region`, `read-flash`.
- `write-flash 0x0 nuttx.bin` writes 0x0–~0x17ec80, **below the littlefs `/data` partition at 0x180000**, so board-side session files, skills and feeding data survive a firmware flash.
- **`velapaw` auto-starts at boot.** Launching a second instance with `velapaw &` wedges the console (`mic: session belonged to pid 5, reopening` — the `-110` mic-reopen trap). Recovery is a physical RESET tap.
- **`ser.write()` on a wedged CDC ACM console blocks for ever** — fix is `serial.Serial(..., write_timeout=10)` plus catching `serial.SerialTimeoutException`.
- **`ask hello` is cache-poisoned** (RAM-only `llm_cache`) — always probe with a novel prompt. Every ask emits **two** `[Agent]:` lines (placeholder then real). Budget 3.6–35.6 s per LLM call after the 20-tool cut.
- **`Skills summary: NNN bytes` is the real signal that a Skill loaded**; `Skills system ready (N built-in)` is a compile-time constant and proves nothing.
- Proactive heartbeat: **3-minute interval in the flashed build** (was 30 min); pushes **only when a pet crosses a concern threshold**.
- ARP priming (host→board ping) is required before the first LLM request, or it stalls with no timeout. A `Tentative`/`Disconnected` `Ethernet 2` silently reroutes board traffic into the VPN — read the ping's **reply source**, not "0% loss".

```
>>> 'ask in one short sentence how is bob doing on food right now'

Two hard facts the boot log did settle, one of which contradicts my earlier note:

[heartbeat] Heartbeat started (every 30 min)

"""Probe round 2, this time following the pattern exactly.

Round 1's mistake: `ai_agent &` backgrounds the agent but nsh keeps the
console, so `help` and `ask` were both eaten by nsh.  `sleep 600` parks nsh
so the agent's own CLI thread owns stdin -- that is what lands you at vela>.

ai_agent is ALREADY RUNNING from round 1.  Do not launch it again, and
never launch velapaw.

Also: `ask` is limited by nsh's MAX_ARGS, so keep the prompt short.
"""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import serial
import serial.tools.list_ports

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RAW = os.path.join(HERE, "agent_demo_probe2_raw.log")
PORT = "COM8"

ports = [p.device for p in serial.tools.list_ports.comports()]
print(f">>> ports: {ports}", flush=True)
if PORT not in ports:
    sys.exit(f"!!! {PORT} absent. ABORTING.")

lines = []
lock = threading.Lock()
stop = False
t0 = time.time()
fh = open(RAW, "wb")


def reader(s):
    buf = b""
    while not stop:
        try:
            chunk = s.read(4096)
        except Exception:
            break
        if not chunk:
            continue
        fh.write(chunk)
        fh.flush()
        buf += chunk
        while b"\n" in buf:
            one, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
            txt = one.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r")
            with lock:
                lines.append((time.time() - t0, txt))
            print(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] {txt}", flush=True)


ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 115200, timeout=0.2, write_timeout=10)
threading.Thread(target=reader, args=(ser,), daemon=True).start()


def send(cmd):
    print(f"\n>>> {cmd!r}", flush=True)
    try:
        ser.write((cmd + "\r\n").encode())
        return True
    except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
        print("!!! write timed out -- console not draining.", flush=True)
        return False


def mark():
    with lock:
        return len(lines)


def since(m):
    with lock:
        return "\n".join(t for _, t in lines[m:])


# ---- wake -------------------------------------------------------------
m = mark()
for _ in range(3):
    if not send(""):
        sys.exit("!!! console wedged on wake.")
    time.sleep(1.2)
time.sleep(2)
if "nsh>" not in since(m) and "vela>" not in since(m):
    stop = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
    ser.close()
    fh.close()
    sys.exit("!!! no prompt.")

# ---- is the custom feeding Skill actually on disk? --------------------
print("\n########## Q0: skills on littlefs ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
send("ls -l /data/ai_agent/skills/")
time.sleep(5)
print("\n--- skills dir ---\n" + since(m), flush=True)

# ---- park nsh so the agent CLI owns the console -----------------------
print("\n########## parking nsh with sleep 600 ##########", flush=True)
send("sleep 600")
time.sleep(6)

# ---- Q1: the agent CLI's own command list -----------------------------
print("\n########## Q1: vela> command list ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
send("help")
time.sleep(10)
helptext = since(m)
print("\n--- vela> help ---\n" + helptext, flush=True)

cands = sorted(set(re.findall(
    r"\b(\w*heartbeat\w*|\w*trigger\w*|\w*proactive\w*|\w*digest\w*|\w*push\w*)\b",
    helptext, re.I)))
print(f"\n### trigger-ish tokens: {cands}", flush=True)

# ---- Q2: time one ask round-trip (SHORT prompt -- MAX_ARGS) -----------
print("\n########## Q2: ask round-trip ##########", flush=True)
subprocess.run(["ping", "-n", "3", "192.168.137.2"],
               capture_output=True, text=True)

PROMPT = "ask is bob eating enough lately"
m = mark()
t_send = time.time()
send(PROMPT)

hits = []
end = time.time() + 300
while time.time() < end:
    with lock:
        rows = lines[m:]
    hits = [(ts, tx) for ts, tx in rows if "[Agent]" in tx]
    if len(hits) >= 2:
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)

print("\n--- ask output ---\n" + since(m), flush=True)
print("\n########## RESULT ##########", flush=True)
base = t_send - t0
if len(hits) >= 2:
    print(f"placeholder [Agent]: at {hits[0][0] - base:6.1f} s", flush=True)
    print(f"real        [Agent]: at {hits[-1][0] - base:6.1f} s", flush=True)
    for ts, tx in hits:
        print(f"    {ts - base:6.1f}s  {tx}", flush=True)
elif len(hits) == 1:
    print(f"ONLY ONE [Agent]: line at {hits[0][0] - base:.1f} s", flush=True)
    print(f"    {hits[0][1]}", flush=True)
else:
    print("no [Agent]: line within 300 s", flush=True)

time.sleep(2)
stop = True
time.sleep(0.5)
ser.close()
fh.close()

"""Time one `ask` round-trip properly.

Round 2 measured nothing: the placeholder ("...") is printed twice, once raw
and once through the [agent] dispatcher, so a "two [Agent]: lines" detector
fires on the placeholder alone.  The unambiguous end-of-turn marker is the
trace line `[trace:...] END status=`, so wait for that.

nsh is already parked by the `sleep 600` from round 2 and ai_agent is
already running, so this just reattaches to the vela> prompt.
"""
import os
import re
import sys
import threading
import time

import serial
import serial.tools.list_ports

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RAW = os.path.join(HERE, "agent_ask_timing_raw.log")
PORT = "COM8"

ports = [p.device for p in serial.tools.list_ports.comports()]
print(f">>> ports: {ports}", flush=True)
if PORT not in ports:
    sys.exit(f"!!! {PORT} absent. ABORTING.")

lines = []
lock = threading.Lock()
stop = False
t0 = time.time()
fh = open(RAW, "wb")
NOISE = re.compile(r"\[llmdbg")


def reader(s):
    buf = b""
    while not stop:
        try:
            chunk = s.read(4096)
        except Exception:
            break
        if not chunk:
            continue
        fh.write(chunk)
        fh.flush()
        buf += chunk
        while b"\n" in buf:
            one, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
            txt = one.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r")
            with lock:
                lines.append((time.time() - t0, txt))
            if not NOISE.search(txt):          # llmdbg spam -> file only
                print(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] {txt}", flush=True)


ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 115200, timeout=0.2, write_timeout=10)
threading.Thread(target=reader, args=(ser,), daemon=True).start()


def mark():
    with lock:
        return len(lines)


def rows(m):
    with lock:
        return list(lines[m:])


# ---- let the in-flight ask from round 2 finish ------------------------
print("\n########## draining the in-flight ask ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
end = time.time() + 150
while time.time() < end:
    if any("END status=" in t for _, t in rows(m)):
        print("### in-flight ask completed.", flush=True)
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)
else:
    print("### no END seen while draining (may have finished already).",
          flush=True)

time.sleep(3)

# ---- the measured run -------------------------------------------------
PROMPT = "ask how is jay appetite trending"
print(f"\n########## TIMED RUN: {PROMPT!r} ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
t_send = time.time()
try:
    ser.write((PROMPT + "\r\n").encode())
except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
    stop = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
    ser.close()
    fh.close()
    sys.exit("!!! write timed out -- console wedged.")

t_end = None
end = time.time() + 300
while time.time() < end:
    for ts, tx in rows(m):
        if "END status=" in tx:
            t_end = ts
            break
    if t_end is not None:
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)

base = t_send - t0
print("\n########## RESULT ##########", flush=True)
if t_end is None:
    print("no END status= line within 300 s", flush=True)
else:
    print(f"total round-trip: {t_end - base:.1f} s", flush=True)

# milestones, for the demo cut
for ts, tx in rows(m):
    if any(k in tx for k in ("[Agent]:", "Tool call:", "Tool iter",
                             "END status=", "latency=", "Handshake OK",
                             "Skills summary")):
        print(f"    {ts - base:6.1f}s  {tx}", flush=True)

time.sleep(2)
stop = True
time.sleep(0.5)
ser.close()
fh.close()
print(f"\n>>> raw: {RAW}", flush=True)

10	The "board hangs ~30s after launching `ai_agent` with no WiFi configured" symptom (first seen 2026-08-26, recorded as unresolved in [[velapaw-sigkill-and-durable-stackfix]]) is **not a real system/ai_agent hang**. Root-caused and closed 2026-08-27.
11	
12	**Evidence**: every prior test used one continuous serial connection to capture output, and always went silent around t=30s (matches `network_wait_connected(30000)`'s 30s WiFi-connect timeout in `network_watch_task()`, `packages/ai_agent/src/agent_main.c`). But probing with **brand-new serial connections** (fresh `pyserial.Serial()` opens, not the same held-open connection) at timed intervals through and well past that point — t=10,20,28,30,32,35,40,60,90,120,180s — got clean, well-formed `ps` responses every single time, with `ai_agent`'s task and pthreads alive and normally scheduled throughout. The board and process were never actually stuck; only the one long-held serial session/capture went quiet.
13	
14	**Why the 30s mark specifically**: real behavioral transition, not a bug — with no saved WiFi SSID, `network_watch_task()` times out waiting for a connection at 30s and (in stock config, `CONFIG_AI_AGENT_NET_RPMSG` not set) its thread cleanly exits. Confirmed directly: the `ps` process-table byte length shrinks from 1156→1043 bytes exactly at the t=30-32s probe, matching one fewer pthread (the network-watch thread) after it returns. This is expected, intentional NuttX/ai_agent behavior, not a crash.
15	
16	**False lead ruled out along the way**: a "thread-exit-path" hypothesis (maybe NuttX mishandles this one self-exiting pthread specially) was directly tested by patching `agent_main.c` so the thread never exits (moved the `#endif` gating so the `while(!g_shutdown_requested) sleep(1)` loop ran unconditionally) — rebuilt, reflashed, retested. The patched build showed the identical apparent "freeze" timing under continuous-capture, proving the thread's exit behavior was never the cause. **This patch has since been reverted** — the source tree is back to stock as of the end of this session.
17	
18	**Takeaway for future hardware debugging on this board**: if a continuous single-serial-connection capture goes silent, don't assume the board/process died — reconnect with a fresh connection before concluding it's a real hang. The CDC-ACM console channel (or the pyserial-side capture) can apparently go stale on one long-held connection independent of system health.
19	
20	See [[velapaw-console-blocking]] for a related but distinct, actually-real console-blocking bug (193-byte CDCACM TX buffer stall, fixed in b83) — not the same mechanism as this false alarm, but worth checking first if a similar silence recurs.
21	
22	**SECOND, related false-alarm mechanism found 2026-09-02 — a fresh connection alone is NOT sufficient either.** A full session was burned re-chasing this exact "console unresponsive" symptom, this time appearing to predate `ai_agent` entirely (plain NSH `ps`/`help` on a stock fresh boot looked hung too). Three real-seeming hypotheses were tested and all falsified by direct hardware retest: `AGENT_CLI_PRIO` 30→70 (made it *look* worse, a 20min `ser.write()` hang from the probe script's own missing `write_timeout`), disabling `telnetd_autostart()`'s `close(0/1/2)` accept loop, and a genuine console-burying bug where a burst of ~6 unconditional `syslog(LOG_ERR,...)` bring-up breadcrumbs (RTC/FT6336-touch/speaker/camera in `board_lcd_initialize()`, `esp32s3_st7789.c`) exceeded the 193-byte `CONFIG_CDCACM_TXBUFSIZE` in one uninterrupted burst — real bug, now fixed by deleting those 6 prints (kept; see the code), but **still didn't fix the symptom**.
23	
24	**Actual root cause**: sending a single `\r\n` immediately after opening a fresh pyserial connection does not reliably reach NuttShell's readline loop — it gets silently absorbed (probably leftover framing/garbage on the line right after USB CDC-ACM re-enumeration), so NSH never sees a complete line and the console only echoes raw characters back at the driver level, looking indistinguishable from a real hang no matter how long you wait. **Fix: send several bare `\r\n` (5 worked reliably) after opening, THEN send the real command.** Confirmed hardware-verified this way: plain NSH `ps`/`help` respond instantly and correctly, and `ai_agent &` boots 100% cleanly through every subsystem (config store, message bus, memory, sessions, 36 tools, 10 skills, cron, heartbeat) straight to a working `vela>` CLI prompt with `network_watch`'s `[netmgr] Timed out waiting for network` firing on schedule as expected with no WiFi configured yet.
25	
26	**Takeaway, corrected**: "reconnect with a fresh connection" (the original takeaway above) is necessary but **not sufficient**. Always send a multi-`\r\n` wake sequence before the real command on any fresh connection to this board's console — see `nsh_probe_wake.py` pattern. Absence of a wake sequence is indistinguishable from a genuine hang by symptom alone, and can burn an entire session chasing phantom fixes (priority, telnetd, DMA/camera drivers were all innocent bystanders this time).

"""Time the exact prompt the README advertises, and capture the answer.

Usage: python ask_demo_prompt.py "ask how much did bob eat today"

What matters here is not just latency but whether the turn actually uses
the tool path (tools>=1 in the END line).  A tools=0 turn comes back in
~3s with the model saying it needs to look something up -- fast and
useless, which is the worst thing to put in a demo cut.

Fresh connection => multi-\r\n wake first, and require an echoed vela>
before trusting anything.  `ask` is limited by nsh MAX_ARGS, so keep the
prompt at or under ~7 words.
"""
import os
import re
import sys
import threading
import time

import serial
import serial.tools.list_ports

PROMPT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "ask how much did bob eat today"

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
slug = re.sub(r"\W+", "_", PROMPT)[:40]
RAW = os.path.join(HERE, f"ask_{slug}_raw.log")
PORT = "COM8"

ports = [p.device for p in serial.tools.list_ports.comports()]
print(f">>> ports: {ports}", flush=True)
if PORT not in ports:
    sys.exit(f"!!! {PORT} absent. ABORTING.")

lines = []
lock = threading.Lock()
stop = False
t0 = time.time()
fh = open(RAW, "wb")
NOISE = re.compile(r"\[llmdbg")


def reader(s):
    buf = b""
    while not stop:
        try:
            chunk = s.read(4096)
        except Exception:
            break
        if not chunk:
            continue
        fh.write(chunk)
        fh.flush()
        buf += chunk
        while b"\n" in buf:
            one, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
            txt = one.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r")
            with lock:
                lines.append((time.time() - t0, txt))
            if not NOISE.search(txt):
                print(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] {txt}", flush=True)


ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 115200, timeout=0.2, write_timeout=10)
threading.Thread(target=reader, args=(ser,), daemon=True).start()


def mark():
    with lock:
        return len(lines)


def rows(m):
    with lock:
        return list(lines[m:])


# ---- wake -------------------------------------------------------------
print("\n########## waking ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
for _ in range(5):
    try:
        ser.write(b"\r\n")
    except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
        stop = True
        time.sleep(0.5)
        ser.close()
        fh.close()
        sys.exit("!!! write timed out on wake.")
    time.sleep(1.0)
time.sleep(2)

woke = "\n".join(t for _, t in rows(m))
if "vela>" not in woke:
    stop = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
    ser.close()
    fh.close()
    sys.exit("!!! not at vela> -- re-park nsh with `sleep 600` first.")
print("### at vela>.", flush=True)

# ---- timed run --------------------------------------------------------
print(f"\n########## {PROMPT!r} ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
t_send = time.time()
try:
    ser.write((PROMPT + "\r\n").encode())
except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
    stop = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
    ser.close()
    fh.close()
    sys.exit("!!! write timed out sending the prompt.")

end_line = None
end = time.time() + 300
while time.time() < end:
    for ts, tx in rows(m):
        if "END status=" in tx:
            end_line = (ts, tx)
            break
    if end_line:
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)

# the final answer is dispatched a beat AFTER the END trace line
time.sleep(8)

base = t_send - t0
print("\n########## RESULT ##########", flush=True)
if not end_line:
    print("no END status= within 300 s", flush=True)
else:
    print(f"total round-trip: {end_line[0] - base:.1f} s", flush=True)
    print(f"trace: {end_line[1].strip()}", flush=True)
    mt = re.search(r"tools=(\d+)", end_line[1])
    if mt:
        n = int(mt.group(1))
        print(f"### tools used: {n} "
              f"({'REAL tool path' if n else 'NO tool path -- non-answer risk'})",
              flush=True)

print("\n--- agent replies ---", flush=True)
seen = set()
for ts, tx in rows(m):
    if "[Agent]:" in tx:
        body = tx.split("[Agent]:", 1)[1].strip()
        if body and body not in seen:
            seen.add(body)
            print(f"  {ts - base:6.1f}s  {body}", flush=True)

print("\n--- tool calls ---", flush=True)
for ts, tx in rows(m):
    if "Tool call:" in tx or "Executing:" in tx:
        print(f"  {ts - base:6.1f}s  {tx.strip()}", flush=True)

time.sleep(1)
stop = True
time.sleep(0.5)
ser.close()
fh.close()
print(f"\n>>> raw: {RAW}", flush=True)

VelaPaw Agent Call Sheet

One unbroken 60-second take, appended to the existing 4-minute demo. Everything the judges need for the 基础要求 of the AI 硬件产品创新 track.
BOARD ESP32-S3 · COM8 @115200
FIRMWARE 708b0bca… (1 567 136 B)
AGENT deepseek-chat · api.deepseek.com
RUNTIME 0:00 – 1:00

The one thing this take has to prove why it's shot live

The number the agent quotes must be created on camera, seconds earlier, by a physical feed. That single property is what separates a real on-device agent from a scripted screen recording — and it's the thing a judge cannot get from a screenshot. Everything below is arranged to protect it.

Pre-roll camera off · ~2 min

None of this is filmed. Do it in order; step 6 is what makes the on-camera commands reach the agent at all.

  1. Power up the board, or tap RESET if it's already on

    Allow ~15 s for the USB console to re-enumerate. Confirm COM8 is present before you open anything — COM8 alone means the app booted; COM3 alone means it fell into download mode.

  2. Press Enter three times to get the prompt

    A single Enter on a fresh connection is silently absorbed and the console then looks identical to a hang. Three is the documented minimum here.

    nsh>

  3. Bring up networking

    ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1

  4. Prime ARP from the Windows host

    Without this the first LLM request stalls with no timeout. Read the reply source address, not "0% loss" — a Tentative or Disconnected Ethernet 2 silently reroutes board traffic into the VPN and still reports success.

    ping -n 3 192.168.137.2 Reply from 192.168.137.2: bytes=32 … ← must be .137.2

  5. Start the agent

    Wait for AI Agent ready and the vela> banner — about 1 second after launch.

    ai_agent & [agent] [boot +1010ms] AI Agent ready. [cli] NSH CLI started. vela>

  6. Park nsh so the agent CLI owns the console

    This is load-bearing, not filler. ai_agent & backgrounds the agent but nsh keeps stdin — without this step every ask is eaten by nsh and comes back ask: command not found. The sleep hands the console to the vela> CLI.

    sleep 600
    Ten-minute clockWhen the sleep expires nsh takes the console back mid-shoot and ask starts failing. If your setup runs long, re-issue it before rolling.

  7. Clear the session history

    Skip this and the agent opens its answer with something like "Data's more recent than my earlier figures…" — carryover from earlier runs, which reads badly on camera and invites the wrong question.

    vela> session_clear_all

  8. Pre-type the two commands, don't improvise them

    Type each one but don't press Enter until the take. Typing live burns 4–5 s of a 60-second budget, and ask is capped by nsh's MAX_ARGS — an improvised longer question dies with ask: too many arguments.

The take rolling · 60 s

0:007 SEC

The custom Skill, on the device's own filesystem

Card out

11	**SOLVED + SHIPPED 2026-08-09.** VelaPaw's Enroll-tab camera preview had two bugs that looked related but weren't: an orientation bug (image rotated) and a color bug (purple tint). Both are now fixed and confirmed correct on real hardware (hand test: fingers-up renders fingers-up; color no longer purple).
12	
13	## Orientation: it was a 90 deg transpose, not a flip
14	
15	**Diagnostic trick that broke the case open:** hold a real hand up in front of the camera (fingers pointing up) and look at the preview. A **vertical→horizontal** result (fingers appearing sideways) can *only* come from a 90 deg rotation/transpose. Flip and mirror (the OV5640's `0x3820`/`0x3821` registers) can each only reverse one axis — neither, nor any combination, can ever turn vertical into horizontal. Chasing this with sensor flip/mirror registers is structurally unable to work; a color-bar test earlier in the debugging session had hinted at this (horizontal bars where vertical were expected) but got wrongly dismissed as a binning artifact.
16	
17	**Fix:** correct the rotation in software, in the HAL's downscale/resample step — `app/velapaw/hal/camera_ov5640.c`, in `velapaw_camera_get_frame()`. The old code was a plain resize + horizontal mirror. Determined the needed correction was **90 deg CW** by tracing where each output-image corner samples from in the raw 320x240 buffer (not by guessing — get this backwards and it's another flash cycle to find out). Final resample also folds in the existing selfie-mirror on the corrected (post-rotation) axis:
18	
19	```c
20	int dy = y * w / VELAPAW_FRAME_H;   /* w = CAM_W = 320 */
21	int sx = dy;
22	...
23	int mox = (VELAPAW_FRAME_W - 1) - x;
24	int dx = mox * h / VELAPAW_FRAME_W; /* h = CAM_H = 240 */
25	int sy = (h - 1) - dx;
26	const uint8_t *p = buf + ((size_t)sy * w + sx) * 2;
27	```
28	
29	**Important dependency:** this transpose is derived against whatever the sensor's raw output orientation is *at the time of the hand test*. If sensor-side flip/mirror registers (`0x3820`/`0x3821`) ever change again, the raw buffer's orientation changes too, and the hand test (and possibly the CW/CCW direction) needs to be redone. See [[velapaw-camera-connector]] for the physical mount/pinout side of the camera.
30	
31	## Color: the purple tint was from splitting OV5640's flip bits
32	
33	Earlier debugging assumed `0x3820`/`0x3821` bit1 = "sensor-side flip" (shifts Bayer CFA phase, causes purple) and bit2 = "ISP-side flip" (safe, post-debayer). Testing bit2-only (`0x05`/`0x05`) still produced the purple tint — that hypothesis was wrong. In the OV5640 (per standard reference driver code, e.g. esp32-camera's `ov5640.c`), **bits 1 and 2 are meant to be toggled together as one flip unit (mask `0x06`)**, not used as independent safe/unsafe halves — setting bit2 alone leaves the sensor in an undefined partial-flip state.
34	
35	**Fix:** since software now owns 100% of the orientation correction (see above), there's no need for the sensor to flip/mirror at all. Cleared bits 1+2 entirely, preserving whatever bit0 was for (unknown purpose, untouched, was already `1` in the working baseline): `ov5640_wr(i,0x3820,0x01);ov5640_wr(i,0x3821,0x01);` (board file, `ov5640_config_qvga()`). Do not reintroduce `0x3820`/`0x3821` bit1 or bit2 without re-testing color — that combination is the confirmed cause.
36	
37	## Workflow note
38	
39	Rebuild/reflash loop: VM has no sshd, so Windows serves source files via `python -m http.server` (repo root on :9100) and the VM pulls, rebuilds, and serves `nuttx.bin` back on :8000. **VM's own IP is 192.168.160.128; the Windows host (as seen from the VM) is 192.168.160.1** — these are easy to swap by mistake (a script inherited from earlier in a session had `WIN_HOST` set to the VM's own IP, which fails every pull silently until checked with `ipconfig` for the VMnet8 adapter). Flashing consistently needs the manual BOOT-hold + RESET-tap dance done *while `esptool` is actively retrying* (not before) — auto-reset via DTR/RTS is unreliable on this board; a `Write timeout` from a plain `write-flash` almost always means the chip wasn't actually in bootloader mode yet, not a driver problem (verified: raw pyserial writes to the port succeed fine even while esptool's handshake fails).

"""Scan built images for the OV5640 flip/mirror register writes.

The board file writes the register table as a byte array, so the pair
0x3820/0x3821 with their values sits contiguously in .rodata:

    38 20 01 38 21 07   -> BROKEN (bit1+bit2 still set on 0x3821) -> purple
    38 20 01 38 21 01   -> FIXED  (both flip bits cleared)

Anything else with 3820 in it gets printed too, so a third spelling
can't hide.
"""
import glob
import os
import re
import sys

PATS = {
    "BROKEN 38 20 01 38 21 07": bytes.fromhex("382001382107"),
    "FIXED  38 20 01 38 21 01": bytes.fromhex("382001382101"),
}

paths = sys.argv[1:]
for p in paths:
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        print(f"{p}: MISSING")
        continue
    data = open(p, "rb").read()
    hits = []
    for name, pat in PATS.items():
        off = data.find(pat)
        if off >= 0:
            hits.append(f"{name} @0x{off:x}")
    # any other 0x3820 pairing
    others = []
    for m in re.finditer(b"\x38\x20", data):
        i = m.start()
        ctx = data[i:i + 6]
        if ctx not in PATS.values() and len(ctx) == 6:
            others.append(ctx.hex(" "))
    print(f"\n=== {p}  ({len(data)} B)")
    print("   " + ("; ".join(hits) if hits else "no known pattern"))
    if others:
        print(f"   other 0x3820 contexts ({len(others)}): "
              + ", ".join(sorted(set(others))[:6]))

The `38 20 01 38 21 07` test only works if the registers are written as a byte **table**. They're written as separate `ov5640_wr()` calls, so 0x3820 lands in an Xtensa literal pool as `20 38 00 00` and the `0x01`/`0x07` value is a `movi.n` immediate inside the instruction — the two never sit next to each other. The 35 `38 20` hits in each image are coincidental data. That test in [velapaw-b82-camerafix-rebuild.md](C:/Users/VICTUS/.claude/projects/c--Users-VICTUS-openVela/memory/velapaw-b82-camerafix-rebuild.md) is wrong and I'll correct the memory once we know the real cause.

Also worth knowing: the flashed image (`708b0bcadd63743002a4ddba0ccf55e5`, 1567136 B) matches **none** of the Windows snapshots — closest is fastpath-cleanup at 1567152 B / `cd2b4edd…`. The build on the board was never mirrored here, so there's no exact rollback binary on Windows.

## Do this before any firmware work — it takes 10 seconds

There are two completely different causes that both look like this photo, and one of them isn't firmware at all:

- **Bayer-phase swap** (the documented `0x3820`/`0x3821` regression) — red and blue are *exchanged*. A red object renders blue, a blue object renders red.
- **Missing / dislodged IR-cut filter** on the OV5640 module — everything gets a magenta wash but red still reads red, and the cast changes with the light source (much worse under sunlight or incandescent, nearly gone pointing at a phone screen).

So: open Recognize, hold something **strongly red** in front of the lens, then something **strongly blue**.

- Red shows as blue → firmware, the register fix isn't in the flashed build.
- Red still shows as red, whole frame just washed pink → hardware, the filter. No rebuild will fix it, and it's a camera-module swap or reseat.

The photo alone can't separate these — the scene is mostly beige/skin tones, which is exactly where both failures look identical.

Paste these in the VM and send me the output. Command 1 first: if that md5 doesn't match, 2 and 3 are meaningless because the VM tree isn't what's on the board.

cd ~/openvela/nuttx

```bash

Command 3 is the stale-object test: if any `.o` or `libboards.a` is **older** than the `.c` next to it, that's the 2026-08-11 regression repeating and the fix is `find boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit -name '*.o' -delete` plus the `libboards.a` before rebuilding.

## The likely culprit is on the same line as the fix

```c
ov5640_wr(i,0x3820,0x01); ov5640_wr(i,0x3821,0x01); ov5640_wr(i,0x4514,0xbb);
```

`0x4514` is the OV5640's **BLC (black-level calibration) pattern** register, and its value is not free — it has to match the Bayer phase that the flip/mirror bits select. The standard pairing in the Linux `ov5640` driver and the ESP camera drivers is:

- mirror **on** (`0x3821` bits set) → `0x4514 = 0xbb`
- mirror **off** (`0x3821` bits cleared) → `0x4514 = 0x88`

This code clears the mirror bits but leaves `0x4514` at `0xbb` — the *mirrored* BLC pattern. Black-level offsets then get subtracted from the wrong colour cells, which crushes one channel and casts the whole frame. That matches a missing green far better than anything else on the table.

I'll flag this as a hypothesis, not a finding — it fits the symptom and the register pairing is documented, but I haven't proven it on your hardware. It's a one-byte change, so proving it is cheap.

Found it — two things in that output.

**`M boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld`** — that linker script is locally modified against git. It's correctly wired into the link (`ARCHSCRIPT +=` at line 29 of the devkit `Make.defs`, same as every other S3 board), so the wiring isn't the issue: the script's *contents* are. Line 30 still has `PROVIDE( cache_invalidate_addr = Cache_Invalidate_Addr );`, which means the alias is fine but its right-hand side — the ROM symbol `Cache_Invalidate_Addr` — is what's now undefined.

**Junk in that same directory**: `esp32CPP:`, `esp32s3_CPP:`, `flat_memory.lCPP:` are untracked garbage, filenames truncated and suffixed with `CPP:`. Those are the debris of a linker-script preprocessing step that went wrong at some point — in the exact directory whose script is now broken. Not a coincidence worth ignoring.

```bash

git diff boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld
```

```bash

echo "=== where is the ROM symbol defined? ==="
grep -rn "Cache_Invalidate_Addr" boards/ arch/ tools/ 2>/dev/null | head -20

The `git diff` is the one I expect to answer it. If it shows a removed `PROVIDE( Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x... )` or the file truncated, restoring the script fixes the link and we're back to testing `0x4514 = 0x88`.

Don't delete the `CPP:` files yet — if the diff is unrevealing, one of them may be a partial copy of what the script should contain.

One correction to my last message: I said the link had been broken since before you deleted the `.o`. That's the reading I'd still bet on, but it isn't proven — a modified `.ld` could have been edited at any point, including after the 09:57 build. The diff will date it.

The diff shows someone already hit this and tried to fix it — line 29 was **added** locally:

```
+PROVIDE( Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x400016b0 );
 PROVIDE( cache_invalidate_addr = Cache_Invalidate_Addr );
```

The address is right (matches `esp32s3.rom.ld:382` exactly). The problem is the *form*: **GNU ld only fires a `PROVIDE` when the symbol is referenced by an object file, not when it's referenced from another linker-script expression.** No compiled object references `Cache_Invalidate_Addr` (capitalised) — only `cache_invalidate_addr` — so line 29's PROVIDE never fires, line 30's expression has nothing to resolve to, and the alias stays undefined. The chain can't bootstrap itself.

That also explains why the sibling aliases (`cache_dbus_mmu_set` etc.) never complain: nothing references them either, so ld simply drops them silently.

Fix is to make line 29 a **definite assignment** so it always defines the symbol:

```bash
cd ~/openvela/nuttx
cp boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld \
   boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld.bak
sed -i 's/^PROVIDE( Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x400016b0 );$/Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x400016b0;/' \
   boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld
sed -n '26,32p' boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld
```

You should see line 29 as `Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x400016b0;` with no `PROVIDE(`. A definite assignment can't collide with `esp32s3.rom.ld`, because that file uses `PROVIDE` and PROVIDE always yields to a real definition.

"""Post-camera-fix regression check on ai_agent.

Follows the exact bring-up pattern that is known to work on this board:
  wake with multi-\r\n  ->  nsh>
  ifconfig eth0 ...
  ai_agent &
  sleep 600            <- this is what hands the console to the vela> CLI;
                          without it nsh eats `ask` as a builtin
  ask <prompt>

Waits for `END status=` (NOT a count of `[Agent]:` lines -- the placeholder
is echoed twice, so counting them fires on the placeholder alone).
"""
import os
import re
import sys
import threading
import time

import serial
import serial.tools.list_ports

PROMPT = "ask how much did bob eat today"
PORT = "COM8"
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RAW = os.path.join(HERE, "agent_regression_raw.log")

ports = [p.device for p in serial.tools.list_ports.comports()]
print(f">>> ports: {ports}", flush=True)
if PORT not in ports:
    sys.exit(f"!!! {PORT} absent. ABORTING.")

lines = []
lock = threading.Lock()
stop = False
t0 = time.time()
fh = open(RAW, "wb")
NOISE = re.compile(r"\[llmdbg")


def reader(s):
    buf = b""
    while not stop:
        try:
            chunk = s.read(4096)
        except Exception:
            break
        if not chunk:
            continue
        fh.write(chunk)
        fh.flush()
        buf += chunk
        while b"\n" in buf:
            one, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
            txt = one.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r")
            with lock:
                lines.append((time.time() - t0, txt))
            if not NOISE.search(txt):
                print(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] {txt}", flush=True)


ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 115200, timeout=0.2, write_timeout=10)
threading.Thread(target=reader, args=(ser,), daemon=True).start()


def mark():
    with lock:
        return len(lines)


def rows(m):
    with lock:
        return list(lines[m:])


def send(cmd, settle=2.0):
    try:
        ser.write((cmd + "\r\n").encode())
    except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
        globals()["stop"] = True
        time.sleep(0.5)
        ser.close()
        fh.close()
        sys.exit(f"!!! write timed out sending {cmd!r} -- console wedged.")
    time.sleep(settle)


# ---- wake ------------------------------------------------------------
print("\n########## waking (3x enter, then some) ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
for _ in range(5):
    try:
        ser.write(b"\r\n")
    except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
        stop = True
        time.sleep(0.5)
        ser.close()
        fh.close()
        sys.exit("!!! write timed out on wake.")
    time.sleep(1.0)
time.sleep(2)

woke = "\n".join(t for _, t in rows(m))
if "nsh>" not in woke and "vela>" not in woke:
    stop = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
    ser.close()
    fh.close()
    sys.exit("!!! no prompt after wake -- console not responding.")
print(f"### prompt seen: {'vela>' if 'vela>' in woke else 'nsh>'}", flush=True)

if "vela>" not in woke:
    # ---- network -----------------------------------------------------
    print("\n########## ifconfig eth0 ##########", flush=True)
    send("ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1", 3)

    # ---- start the agent ---------------------------------------------
    print("\n########## ai_agent & ##########", flush=True)
    send("ai_agent &", 25)

    # ---- park nsh so the vela> CLI owns stdin ------------------------
    print("\n########## sleep 600 (hand console to vela>) ##########", flush=True)
    m = mark()
    send("sleep 600", 6)
    ser.write(b"\r\n")
    time.sleep(3)
    if "vela>" not in "\n".join(t for _, t in rows(m)):
        stop = True
        time.sleep(0.5)
        ser.close()
        fh.close()
        sys.exit("!!! never reached vela> -- did ai_agent start?")
print("### at vela>.", flush=True)

# ---- timed ask -------------------------------------------------------
print(f"\n########## {PROMPT!r} ##########", flush=True)
m = mark()
t_send = time.time()
send(PROMPT, 0)

end_line = None
end = time.time() + 240
while time.time() < end:
    for ts, tx in rows(m):
        if "END status=" in tx:
            end_line = (ts, tx)
            break
    if end_line:
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)

time.sleep(8)
base = t_send - t0

print("\n########## RESULT ##########", flush=True)
if not end_line:
    print("!!! no END status= within 240 s -- agent loop did not complete", flush=True)
else:
    print(f"round-trip: {end_line[0] - base:.1f} s", flush=True)
    print(f"trace: {end_line[1].strip()}", flush=True)
    mt = re.search(r"tools=(\d+)", end_line[1])
    if mt:
        n = int(mt.group(1))
        print(f"### tools used: {n} "
              f"({'REAL tool path' if n else 'NO tool path -- non-answer'})",
              flush=True)

print("\n--- agent replies ---", flush=True)
seen = set()
for ts, tx in rows(m):
    if "[Agent]:" in tx:
        body = tx.split("[Agent]:", 1)[1].strip()
        if body and body not in seen:
            seen.add(body)
            print(f"  {ts - base:6.1f}s  {body}", flush=True)

print("\n--- skills / tools ---", flush=True)
for ts, tx in rows(m):
    if "Skills summary" in tx or "Tool call:" in tx or "Executing:" in tx:
        print(f"  {ts - base:6.1f}s  {tx.strip()}", flush=True)

time.sleep(1)
stop = True
time.sleep(0.5)
ser.close()
fh.close()
print(f"\n>>> raw: {RAW}", flush=True)

11	**SOLVED + SHIPPED 2026-08-09.** VelaPaw's Enroll-tab camera preview had two bugs that looked related but weren't: an orientation bug (image rotated) and a color bug (purple tint). Both are now fixed and confirmed correct on real hardware (hand test: fingers-up renders fingers-up; color no longer purple).
12	
13	## Orientation: it was a 90 deg transpose, not a flip
14	
15	**Diagnostic trick that broke the case open:** hold a real hand up in front of the camera (fingers pointing up) and look at the preview. A **vertical→horizontal** result (fingers appearing sideways) can *only* come from a 90 deg rotation/transpose. Flip and mirror (the OV5640's `0x3820`/`0x3821` registers) can each only reverse one axis — neither, nor any combination, can ever turn vertical into horizontal. Chasing this with sensor flip/mirror registers is structurally unable to work; a color-bar test earlier in the debugging session had hinted at this (horizontal bars where vertical were expected) but got wrongly dismissed as a binning artifact.
16	
17	**Fix:** correct the rotation in software, in the HAL's downscale/resample step — `app/velapaw/hal/camera_ov5640.c`, in `velapaw_camera_get_frame()`. The old code was a plain resize + horizontal mirror. Determined the needed correction was **90 deg CW** by tracing where each output-image corner samples from in the raw 320x240 buffer (not by guessing — get this backwards and it's another flash cycle to find out). Final resample also folds in the existing selfie-mirror on the corrected (post-rotation) axis:
18	
19	```c
20	int dy = y * w / VELAPAW_FRAME_H;   /* w = CAM_W = 320 */
21	int sx = dy;
22	...
23	int mox = (VELAPAW_FRAME_W - 1) - x;
24	int dx = mox * h / VELAPAW_FRAME_W; /* h = CAM_H = 240 */
25	int sy = (h - 1) - dx;
26	const uint8_t *p = buf + ((size_t)sy * w + sx) * 2;
27	```
28	
29	**Important dependency:** this transpose is derived against whatever the sensor's raw output orientation is *at the time of the hand test*. If sensor-side flip/mirror registers (`0x3820`/`0x3821`) ever change again, the raw buffer's orientation changes too, and the hand test (and possibly the CW/CCW direction) needs to be redone. See [[velapaw-camera-connector]] for the physical mount/pinout side of the camera.
30	
31	## Color: the purple tint was from splitting OV5640's flip bits
32	
33	Earlier debugging assumed `0x3820`/`0x3821` bit1 = "sensor-side flip" (shifts Bayer CFA phase, causes purple) and bit2 = "ISP-side flip" (safe, post-debayer). Testing bit2-only (`0x05`/`0x05`) still produced the purple tint — that hypothesis was wrong. In the OV5640 (per standard reference driver code, e.g. esp32-camera's `ov5640.c`), **bits 1 and 2 are meant to be toggled together as one flip unit (mask `0x06`)**, not used as independent safe/unsafe halves — setting bit2 alone leaves the sensor in an undefined partial-flip state.
34	
35	**Fix:** since software now owns 100% of the orientation correction (see above), there's no need for the sensor to flip/mirror at all. Cleared bits 1+2 entirely, preserving whatever bit0 was for (unknown purpose, untouched, was already `1` in the working baseline): `ov5640_wr(i,0x3820,0x01);ov5640_wr(i,0x3821,0x01);` (board file, `ov5640_config_qvga()`). Do not reintroduce `0x3820`/`0x3821` bit1 or bit2 without re-testing color — that combination is the confirmed cause.

## Purple round 2 — the REAL other half was `0x4514` (SOLVED 2026-09-05)

The tint came back on the ai_agent builds. The flip-bit fix above was intact and genuinely compiled in — this was a **different register on the same source line**. `0x4514` is the OV5640's **BLC (black-level calibration) pattern**, and its value is not free: it must match the Bayer phase the flip/mirror bits select. The standard pairing (Linux `ov5640` driver, esp32-camera):

- mirror **on** (`0x3821` bits 1+2 set) → `0x4514 = 0xbb`
- mirror **off** (`0x3821` bits cleared) → `0x4514 = 0x88`

The shipped line cleared the mirror bits but left `0x4514` at `0xbb` — the *mirrored* BLC pattern. Black-level offsets then get subtracted from the wrong colour cells. **Fixed line:** `ov5640_wr(i,0x3820,0x01);ov5640_wr(i,0x3821,0x01);ov5640_wr(i,0x4514,0x88);` — confirmed perfect on hardware 2026-09-05, md5 `4bfb6733d77bac88fb1e2d6e9ded5dee`. Whenever `0x3821`'s flip bits change, change `0x4514` with them.

**The symptom tells you which of the two it is, and it's decisive:** a flip/Bayer-phase error *exchanges* red and blue and leaves green alone (green is 2 of 4 Bayer cells either way) — it physically cannot cause green loss. A BLC-pattern mismatch crushes a channel: the frame goes violet/magenta (R+B, no G) while the LCD's own UI chrome stays perfectly coloured. **Judge from the whole frame's hue, not from a red/blue swap test** — chasing the flip bits when green is missing wastes hours.

**Do NOT verify with a byte scan of `nuttx.bin`** — see the correction in [[velapaw-b82-camerafix-rebuild]]. Those registers are separate `ov5640_wr()` calls, so the register number sits in an Xtensa literal pool and the value is a `movi.n` immediate; they are never adjacent bytes.

25	## Build (`cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:nsh -j4`)
26	`build.sh` in-tree (no `-m`) needs **no unionfs-fuse** (that's only for `-m` out-of-tree). Three fixes were required, all real:
27	1. **Toolchain not on PATH** — `envsetup.sh` does NOT add the cross-gcc. Add: `export PATH=$HOME/openvela/prebuilts/gcc/linux-x86_64/xtensa-esp32s3-elf/bin:$PATH` (put in `~/.bashrc`). Symptom without it: `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-gcc: command not found` ×hundreds.
28	2. **esp-hal spinlock skew (contest-branch bug)** — pinned esp-hal `9fc713a` (`ESP_HAL_3RDPARTY_VERSION` in `nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/Make.defs`) predates NuttX making `spinlock_t` a **struct**. `clk_ctrl_os.c`/`modem_clock.c` do `lock_type_t x = LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED` (=`0`) → "invalid initializer". Fix (patch the cloned HAL, NuttX branch only): sed `#define LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED 0` → `SP_UNLOCKED` (NuttX's struct initializer). Config can't fix it — no scalar spinlock_t variant exists. NOTE: this patches cloned 3rd-party source; survives incremental rebuild but a `distclean`/re-clone reverts it — re-apply.
29	3. **esptool for the image step** — `nuttx/tools/espressif/check_esptool.py` does `importlib.metadata.version("esptool")` with **system python3**, so pipx isolation is INVISIBLE to it. Must install into system python: `python3 -m pip install --break-system-packages esptool` (5.3.1 installs fine on 3.14, builds cp314 wheels). MIN_VERSION 4.8.0; esptool 5's `elf2image` CLI still works.

31	## Flashing + boot — MILESTONE 2 DONE (2026-07-05, `nsh>` on real hardware)
32	Confirmed `uname -a` → `NuttX ... xtensa esp32s3-devkit` over USB on the board. Physical board IS the planned **ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5** (boot splash `esp32-s3-touch-lcd-3.5/2.2.6`), shipped with **Xiaozhi (小智) AI** factory firmware. Its **USB-C = ESP32-S3 native USB-Serial/JTAG** (`VID 303A PID 1001`), NOT a UART bridge.

35	- **Perms:** `newgrp` is NOT installed on Ubuntu 26.04 minimal; `usermod -aG dialout $USER` only applies next login. Immediate fix: `sudo chmod 666 /dev/ttyACM0`.
36	- **Flash cmd** (SIMPLE BOOT `--ram-only-header` → one file at `0x0`, no bootloader/PT): `esptool --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/ttyACM0 write_flash 0x0 nuttx.bin` (esptool 5 warns write_flash→write-flash, still works). Auto-reset via USB-JTAG worked; if `Connecting...` stalls, hold BOOT/tap RESET/release. **`Hard resetting` re-enumerates the USB** → esptool prints a harmless `could not open port` after a verified write, and `/dev/ttyACM0` briefly vanishes (VMware may need a re-Connect).
37	- **Console:** `sudo picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyACM0`, Enter → `nsh>`. Exit `Ctrl-A Ctrl-X`.

41	## Milestone 3.1 — LCD bring-up (IN PROGRESS 2026-07-05)
42	**Authoritative pins** (from Xiaozhi board cfg `78/xiaozhi-esp32` → `main/boards/waveshare/esp32-s3-touch-lcd-3.5/config.h`, cross-checked): LCD is **ST7796, 320×480**, SPI: **MOSI=IO1, MISO=IO2, SCLK=IO5, DC=IO3**, **CS = hardwired low** (NC, sole SPI device), **RST = on TCA9554 expander EXIO1** (NC as GPIO), **backlight = IO6** (active-high). Shared **I2C: SDA=IO8, SCL=IO7**, TCA9554 @ **0x20**. Xiaozhi ran it landscape 480×320 SWAP_XY, **BGR**, **INVERT_COLOR**. (Ignore web search "MOSI23/SDA22/BL25" — that's the CLASSIC-ESP32 board; S3 has no GPIO 22-25.)
43	**Approach (fastest to pixels):** piggyback on the working `esp32s3-devkit` board (NOT a new board — avoids boards/Kconfig surgery), add a `waveshare_lcd` defconfig (usbnsh/CDCACM console base + LCD) + a self-contained `src/esp32s3_st7789.c`. Template = `lckfb-szpi-esp32s3` (SPI ST7789 + I2C expander + `/dev/fb0`) and the devkit's own `esp32s3_st7735.c`/`esp32s3_board_spi.c` (DC via `esp32s3_spi2_cmddata`→`GPIO_LCD_DC`; must set that .h define to **3**). Key facts: **NuttX has no ST7796 driver → use `CONFIG_LCD_ST7789` at 320×480** (Sitronix-compatible; may need init/orientation/color tuning). **PCA9557 driver == TCA9554** (register-identical) → `CONFIG_IOEXPANDER_PCA9557` at 0x20, pulse EXIO1 via `IOEXP_SETDIRECTION/IOEXP_WRITEPIN`. `pca9557_config_s = {0x20,100000,NULL}`. Devkit bringup auto-registers fb via `fb_register(0,0)` under `CONFIG_VIDEO_FB`. Test with `CONFIG_EXAMPLES_FB` → `fb` cmd. Expect iteration (blank→color→orientation).

45	## LCD status (2026-07-06 late) — PANEL PROVEN GOOD via BIT-BANG; the ESP32-S3 SPI PERIPHERAL is the real bug.
46	**Decisive result:** bit-banging MOSI=GPIO1 / CLK=GPIO5 / DC=GPIO3 as plain GPIOs (esp32s3_gpiowrite, NO SPI peripheral) → screen fills RED, then a full-screen 8-color-bar test pattern rendered PERFECTLY (correct colors incl. red=red/blue=blue, correct landscape orientation MADCTL=0x28, full 480x320 coverage). So the whole display pipeline is proven end-to-end via bit-bang. So panel + AXP power + ST7796 init + pins are ALL correct. The failure the whole time was that **NuttX's esp32s3 SPI2 hardware never actually drove GPIO1/GPIO5** even though its transactions "completed" (fb demo ran clean at 480x320x16, no error, but blank; our raw SPI writes blank too). RDDID reads are a NON-signal here — MISO is NOT wired (factory config.h lists no MISO; write-only panel) so RDDID is always 0xFF regardless of anything. Ruled out: DMA (set `# CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPI_DMA is not set` → poll path, still black); pin mux (forced `esp32s3_gpio_matrix_out(GPIO1,FSPID_OUT_IDX)` + `(GPIO5,FSPICLK_OUT_IDX)` after init, still black); SWCS w/ cs=-1, MISO=-1. Even a 1-byte SPI_SEND (poll) produces nothing. Note: `esp32s3_spibus_initialize` returns CACHED (skips esp32s3_spi_init/pin-config) if `priv->refs!=0` (line ~1677) — a real gotcha but not the cause here (forced mux didn't help). Speed progression, full 480x320 frame: naive gpiowrite bit-bang **860 ms** → register W1TS/W1TC 3 writes/bit **460 ms** → **shadow GPIO_OUT_REG 2 writes/bit = 310 ms (~3.2 fps, current best).** KEY LESSON: the NOP delay was NEVER the bottleneck (4→1 nop made 0 difference); it's the GPIO register-WRITE count. Shadow trick = read GPIO_OUT_REG(0x60004004) once → `base = out & ~(MOSI|CLK)` (preserves other pins) → per bit write `base|data` then `base|data|CLK_M` (2 writes, CLK falls at next bit's data write). Safe because only pins 1/3/5/6 are GPIO outputs (I2C/USB are peripheral-driven, unaffected by GPIO_OUT_REG). **/dev/fb0 FRAMEBUFFER STACK WORKS (2026-07-07):** minimal `struct lcd_dev_s` in the board file (getvideoinfo=480x320 FB_FMT_RGB16_565, getplaneinfo putrun/putarea/bpp16/runbuf, get/setpower→backlight) + board_lcd_getdev returns it → CONFIG_LCD_FRAMEBUFFER wraps it as /dev/fb0. `fb` demo renders correct nested color rects end-to-end. FIX = **unify ALL bytes (command+data) onto ONE shadow-register routine** (`clock_byte` via GPIO_OUT_REG, D/C carried in the shadow `g_out`, and every byte routine ends CLK low with `wreg(REG_OUT,base)`). lcdfb calls putarea(rs,re,cs,ce, run=fbmem+starty*stride+startx*2, stride) — per-row `p=buffer+r*stride`, stream (ce-cs+1)*2 bytes.
