56	**THE FIX (after hours of white screen): the ST7796 logic rail is powered by the on-board AXP2101 PMIC (I2C 0x34), which our firmware never initialized → chip unpowered → register reads all 0xFF, blank/white panel.** Vendor power seq (from Xiaozhi board .cc; done BEFORE display init): AXP2101 enable **ALDO1=3.3V (reg0x92=(3300-500)/100), BLDO1=1.5V (0x96), BLDO2=2.8V (0x97), then reg0x90 |= 0x31** (enable ALDO1|BLDO1|BLDO2). Also DC1=3.3V (0x82) but avoid touching reg0x80 DCDC-enable (risks the ESP32 rail). Implemented as raw I2C writes to 0x34 in `board_lcd_initialize` (helpers axp_wr/axp_rd) on the same I2C0 bus (pins 7/8) — after i2cbus_init, before TCA9554/SPI. Once powered, the ST7796 lights up. **Remaining polish (all minor now):** filled GREEN(0x07E0) but panel showed BLUE → fix color order (BGR / byte-endian / `LCD_ST7789_INVCOLOR` / `_BGR` / `_DATA_ENDIAN_LITTLE`); remove the debug green-fill + RDDID reads from board_lcd_getdev; the `fb` app needs `CONFIG_FB_UPDATE` to flush its own draws; tune orientation (SWAP_XY/mirror) + offsets. Panel init: we send an ST7796 17-cmd vendor sequence over SPI in board code (st7796_init_and_fill) since NuttX has no ST7796 driver (ST7789 driver used only for the fb/putarea plumbing).
57	
58	## (superseded) earlier LCD dead-end — panel stayed WHITE; was the AXP2101 power (above)
59	Config `esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd` (files: `configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig` + `src/esp32s3_st7789.c`, DC set to GPIO3 in `esp32s3-devkit.h`). **Builds, flashes, boots.** **CONFIRMED WORKING via RAMLOG dmesg** (`[wslcd]` syslog): backlight GPIO6, **TCA9554 expander via `pca9557` driver @0x20 (`expander writes ret=0`** — drives IO_0 low + IO_1 reset pulse, matching Xiaozhi's both-pins sequence), SPI2 init, `st7789_lcdinitialize -> OK`, `/dev/fb0` (480×320 RGB565), `fb` example runs. **NOT working:** panel is backlit + powered but shows **clean white — no image.**
60	**Diagnosis (definitive):** NuttX has **no ST7796 driver**; the ST7789 driver's generic init (it DOES send SLPOUT/DISPON) is **insufficient to turn on the ST7796's pixels**. `lcdfb_initialize` does a full black flush at startup, which would show BLACK if SPI reached an on panel — it's white → panel not displaying. **FIX NEEDED: send the ST7796 vendor init** (Xiaozhi `.cc` uses `esp_lcd_new_panel_st7789` + a 17-cmd vendor array: 0x11 SLPOUT, 0x3A COLMOD=0x55, 0xF0 cmd-set unlock, 0xC0-C5 power, 0xE0/E1 gamma, 0x29 DISPON). Approach options: send these raw over SPI in board code before/around st7789 init (careful st7789 SWRESET doesn't wipe), or write a minimal st7796 driver. Also add **`CONFIG_FB_UPDATE`** (the `fb` app's FBIO_UPDATE is `#ifdef CONFIG_FB_UPDATE`, else it never flushes app draws). Cheap extra check: lower `CONFIG_LCD_ST7789_FREQUENCY` 40M→10M (signal integrity). Xiaozhi panel: SWAP_XY, BGR, INVERT_COLOR, 480×320.
61	
62	## Flash + debug loop that WORKS (use this, VMware passthrough is too flaky)
63	VMware USB passthrough drops the device on every re-enumeration (flash reset, console). **Solution: flash+debug from WINDOWS.** (1) VM builds, then serve: `cd ~/openvela/nuttx && python3 -m http.server 8000` (VM IP was 192.168.160.128). (2) Windows pull: `Invoke-WebRequest http://<vmip>:8000/nuttx.bin -OutFile C:\Users\VICTUS\esp-flash\nuttx.bin`. (3) **In VMware: VM→Settings→USB→UNCHECK "Automatically connect new USB devices"**, then VM→Removable Devices→Espressif→"Connect to Host" — board now STAYS on Windows through re-enumerations. (4) Download mode = **hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT** → enumerates `VID_303A PID_1001` on a COM port (was COM3). (5) Flash: `py -m esptool --chip esp32s3 --port COM3 write-flash 0x0 C:\Users\VICTUS\esp-flash\nuttx.bin` (esptool 5.3.1 installed on Windows via py -m). (6) esptool "Hard resetting via RTS" does NOT boot the app over USB-JTAG → **tap RESET** to boot; runs as `VID_0525 PID_A4A7` NuttX CDC (was COM4). (7) Read console via .NET `System.IO.Ports.SerialPort` at 115200 — **MUST send `\r\n` (CRLF) line endings**, `\r` alone doesn't submit to nsh; open with DtrEnable/RtsEnable=$false to avoid resetting. `dmesg` reads the RAMLOG (`CONFIG_RAMLOG_SYSLOG=y`). pyserial `miniterm` crashes on this CDC (ClearCommError) — use .NET SerialPort instead. Board buttons: 3 unlabeled; identify via `dmesg -w` in VM watching USB re-enum (RESET = re-enumerates, BOOT = silent). Charge-only USB-C cable wasted time earlier — use a DATA cable.
64	
65	## Milestone 4 — VelaPaw APP PORT onto the hardware (IN PROGRESS 2026-07-07)
66	The full emulator app (`app/velapaw/`, was D:-only) is now **in the VM tree at `~/openvela/apps/examples/velapaw/`** (moved there, NOT packages/demos). Transfer method: tar on Windows → `py -m http.server` → VM `wget`. **NOTE: Windows port 8080 is blocked by security software (connections reset before reaching python, even localhost); use port 9000+** for host→VM HTTP. Server is stopped now; re-`py -m http.server 9000` in `C:\Users\VICTUS` if you need to re-transfer (but the app is already in the VM).
67	- **Build wiring done:** `Make.defs` repointed `packages/demos/contest2026_043_velapaw`→`examples/velapaw`; `Makefile` rewritten to add `ui/ui_lvgl.c` + `STACKSIZE=32768` under `ifeq ($(CONFIG_VELAPAW_UI),y)`, `-I$(APPDIR)/examples/velapaw`, stub CSRCS (camera_mock, feeder_mock, infer+infer_stub, identity, store_stub). The Make build ignores CMakeLists (that's the CMake/TFLM path); Makefile = stub path only.
68	- **Config symbols** (added to `configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig`): `CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_043_VELAPAW=y` + `CONFIG_VELAPAW_UI=y`. First pass leaves `VELAPAW_INFER_TFLM` **off** (→ infer_stub + camera_mock synthetic frames; assets/ 1MB photos NOT compiled). `apps/examples/Kconfig` is auto-generated (gitignored `/Kconfig`) → reconfigure auto-discovers velapaw/Kconfig, no manual source line.
69	- App structure recap: `velapaw_main.c` `main()` → if `CONFIG_VELAPAW_UI` calls `velapaw_ui_run()` (never returns). `ui/ui_lvgl.c` = **1271 lines / 46KB** — the real LVGL 9.1 dashboard, designed as a 600px portrait column for 1280x800; **MUST be re-laid-out for our 480x320 panel** (next big task). Runs as NSH builtin `velapaw`.
70	- **Build cmd loop** (single paste auto-retries the esp-hal spinlock): `cd ~/openvela && fix_hal (grep -rlE 'define +LOCK_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED +0' arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3 | xargs sed -i 's/...0/...SP_UNLOCKED/') && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4`, retry once if `invalid initializer`/`clk_ctrl_os`. Verify: `grep VELAPAW nuttx/.config` + `strings nuttx.bin | grep -i velapaw`.
71	- **BUILD SUCCEEDS (2026-07-07):** `nuttx.bin` = **705 KB**, links the full real `ui_lvgl.c` dashboard (verified strings: `VelaPaw - Enroll`, `captured sample %d/%d`, `saved %s (id %d) %dg`, `LVGL ready; touch indev`). The ONLY compile fix needed beyond the config was **enabling the montserrat fonts ui_lvgl.c uses — 14/16/22/24** (defconfig had only 20): `CONFIG_LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_{14,16,22,24}=y`. esp-hal spinlock still reverts on each reconfigure → the fix_hal+retry-once wrapper handles it automatically (2nd build links clean). Two harmless warnings remain (`g_bcs_votes`/`g_bcs_nvotes` unused).
72	- **RE-LAYOUT DONE — full VelaPaw UI runs on the 480x320 panel with working touch (2026-07-07).** Rewrote `ui/ui_lvgl.c` from the 600px/1280x800 portrait column to full-screen 480x320 landscape: `#define SCR_W 480/SCR_H 320/COL_W 460`, font hierarchy `F_TITLE=20/F_HEAD=16/F_BODY=F_SMALL=14` (only the already-enabled sizes), slim 24px header (breadcrumb+bell, dropped avatar), 30px tab bar, camera preview cards 120-130px (IMG_SCALE 200), and **converted build_pets/build_trends from hardcoded 800px-tall absolute y-offsets to scrollable flex columns**. Tab pages scroll when content exceeds the short screen. ALL recognition/feeding/store logic + callbacks kept byte-identical. Photo confirms: 4 tabs (Enroll/Recognize/My Pets/Trends) fit, Enroll shows camera card + "Sample 0 of 5" + View btn, touch navigates. Master copy edited on D:\...\app\velapaw\ui\ui_lvgl.c, pushed to VM via the Windows:9000 http server, rebuilt (679844 B).
73	- **Speed:** bit-bang panel is the floor (~3fps full-frame). Cut churn: gated preview to camera tabs, then made it **fully event-driven** (repaint only on view-change/capture, not a timer) — Enroll now static/snappy; Recognize grabs a live frame each 1.2s recog cycle. Helped but bit-bang is still the limit; real speedup = fix the parked SPI2 peripheral (needs a logic analyzer).
74	- **LAUNCH GOTCHA (cost several cycles):** the .NET SerialPort `velapaw` command submit is INTERMITTENT (~1 in 3) — it echoes `velapaw` but often doesn't execute, and a RESET leaves the PREVIOUS run's framebuffer on-screen (PSRAM not cleared), so a stale UI looks like "it ran". ALWAYS confirm launch by reading the `velapaw/ui: LVGL ready; touch indev ok` stdout line before trusting the screen. Reliable submit: open port, wait 800ms, send 3x CRLF, type command CHAR-BY-CHAR (50ms apart), then 3x CRLF, drain 8s for "LVGL ready". Consider making velapaw the boot init/rcS entry to stop fighting the serial.
75	## OV5640 camera bring-up (started 2026-07-07)
76	- **No ESP32-S3 camera capture driver exists in the openvela tree** — only `esp32s3_lcd.c` (LCD_CAM in LCD mode), `ov2640.c` (wrong sensor), and the full V4L2/imgsensor/imgdata framework (so once a driver registers `/dev/video0`, the app's `hal/camera_v4l2.c` works as-is). So the camera is a **from-scratch DVP driver port** (the multi-day hard path).
77	- **Reference obtained:** cloned `espressif/esp32-camera` to VM `~/ref/esp32-camera` and pulled the source to Windows scratch `...\scratchpad\esp32cam\`. Port FROM these proven files (register access identical on bare metal; swap IDF HAL calls for direct writes / NuttX GDMA + I2C_TRANSFER):
78	  - `sensors/ov5640.c` + `sensors/private_include/ov5640_settings.h` (DVP init table) + `ov5640_regs.h` — SCCB init sequence.
79	  - `target/esp32s3/ll_cam.c` (23KB, THE hard part) + `target/private_include/ll_cam.h` — LCD_CAM camera mode + GDMA capture.
80	  - `driver/sccb.c`, `target/xclk.c`, `driver/cam_hal.c`.
81	- **Key facts extracted:** OV5640 SCCB = I2C 7-bit **0x3C**, **16-bit reg addr + 8-bit data, big-endian** (maps to NuttX I2C_TRANSFER: msg0 = 2 addr bytes write, msg1 = 1 byte read). Reset/pdn reg **SYSTEM_CTROL0 0x3008** (bit7 sw-reset, bit6 sw-powerdown). Chip ID regs **0x300A=0x56, 0x300B=0x40**. **Selfie mirror = HW regs: 0x3820 vflip (|=0x06), 0x3821 hmirror (|=0x06)** — OR do software mirror in the downscale loop (`sx = CAM_W-1-...`); user wants selfie because lens faces rear.
82	- **XCLK = LEDC, low-speed mode, 1-bit duty resolution, freq ~20MHz, duty=1, hpoint=0** on GPIO38 (esp32-camera's `xclk.c`). NuttX defconfig currently has `# CONFIG_ESP32S3_LEDC is not set`, PWM off, I2C_DRIVER off. Board I2C0 = SCL7/SDA8 already up; **CAM_PWDN = TCA9554 EXIO0** (set low to power on; expander already driven in board file via pca9557, they toggle EXIO1=LCD_RST).
83	- **Board file** `boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit/src/esp32s3_st7789.c` is only 124 lines and owns i2c+expander; add camera power/XCLK/probe there. Camera DVP pins (from velapaw-hardware): VSYNC=17 HREF=18 PCLK=41 XCLK=38 D0=45 D1=47 D2=48 D3=46 D4=42 D5=40 D6=39 D7=21.
84	- **PHASE 1 DONE (2026-07-07): OV5640 responds — boot log `[cam] OV5640 id=0x5640 ret=0/0`.** Confirms camera power (EXIO0/CAM_PWDN already driven low by the board), SCCB (I2C 0x3C), AND that the LEDC XCLK code works. The probe lives in the board file `esp32s3_st7789.c` (`cam_xclk_start()` + `ov5640_rd()` + `cam_probe()`, called at end of `board_lcd_initialize`). **soc/soc.h gotcha:** the `hardware/esp32s3_ledc.h`/`_system.h`/`gpio_sigmap.h` headers pull in `soc/soc.h` (not on the board include path) → board won't compile if you include them. FIX = hardcode the addrs/bits. **Working XCLK recipe (20MHz on GPIO38, verified):** LEDC base 0x60019000 (CH0_CONF0 +0x00, HPOINT +0x04, DUTY +0x08, CONF1 +0x0c, TIMER0_CONF +0xa0, CONF +0xd0); enable = set SYSTEM(0x600C0000) PERIP_CLK_EN0(+0x18) bit11 + clear PERIP_RST_EN0(+0x20) bit11; `LEDC_CONF=1`(APB src) then set bit31(CLK_EN); TIMER0_CONF = `(2<<0)|(1<<(4+8))` (duty_res=2 → div-by-4, integral presc=1) then set bit25(PARA_UP); CH0: CONF0=0,CONF1=0,HPOINT=0,DUTY=(2<<4), then set CONF0 bit2(SIG_OUT_EN), CONF1 bit31(DUTY_START), CONF0 bit4(PARA_UP); route via `esp32s3_gpio_matrix_out(38, 73 /*LEDC_LS_SIG_OUT0_IDX*/ + 0, 0, 0)` + `esp32s3_configgpio(38, OUTPUT)`. Board src master now lives at Windows scratch `...\scratchpad\board_st7789.c` (pull/edit/push via Windows:9100 http server).
85	- **PHASE 2 (in progress): DVP capture. Big win — NuttX has its own GDMA driver + LCD_CAM, so DON'T port IDF's DMA stack.** Reuse NuttX API (`#include "esp32s3_dma.h"`, clean header no soc/soc.h): `esp32s3_dma_request(ESP32S3_DMA_PERIPH_LCDCAM /*=5*/, tx_prio, rx_prio, burst_en)` -> chan; `esp32s3_dma_set_ext_memblk(chan,false,ESP32S3_DMA_EXT_MEMBLK_64B)` (PSRAM); `esp32s3_dma_setup(desc,num,buf,len,false/*RX*/,chan)`; `esp32s3_dma_load(desc,chan,false)`; `esp32s3_dma_enable(chan,false)`; `esp32s3_dma_wait_idle(chan,false)`. Desc struct `esp32s3_dmadesc_s{ctrl,pbuf,next}`, max 4095 B/desc. Template = `esp32s3_lcd.c` (flip TX->RX, LCD_*->CAM_*). Pattern: `periph_module_enable(PERIPH_LCD_CAM_MODULE)` OR raw SYSTEM. Pins via `esp32s3_gpio_matrix_in(pin, idx, inv)` (in esp32s3_gpio.h). Cache: after RX DMA, `extern int cache_invalidate_addr(uint32_t addr,uint32_t size);` before reading the PSRAM buffer.
86	- **Phase-2 hardcoded register facts (soc/soc.h off board path, so hardcode):** LCD_CAM base **0x60041000**: CAM_CTRL=+0x4, CAM_CTRL1=+0x8, CAM_RGB_YUV=+0xc, LC_DMA_INT_ENA=+0x64, _ST=+0x6c, _CLR=+0x70. CAM_CTRL fields: STOP_EN b0, VSYNC_FILTER_THRES[3:1], UPDATE_REG b4, BYTE_ORDER b5, BIT_ORDER b6, LINE_INT_EN b7, VS_EOF_EN b8, CLKM_DIV_NUM[16:9], CLK_SEL[30:29](=3 for 160MHz). CAM_CTRL1 fields: REC_DATA_BYTELEN[15:0](=framebytes-1), LINE_INT_NUM[21:16], CLK_INV b22, VSYNC_FILTER_EN b23, 2BYTE_EN b24, DE_INV b25, HSYNC_INV b26, VSYNC_INV b27, VH_DE_MODE_EN b28, START b29, RESET b30, AFIFO_RESET b31. GPIO-matrix INPUT idx: CAM_DATA_IN0=133 (D0..D7 =133..140), CAM_PCLK=149, CAM_H_ENABLE(HREF)=150, CAM_V_SYNC=152. SYSTEM LCD_CAM clk: PERIP_CLK_EN1(0x600C001C) bit8, PERIP_RST_EN1(0x600C0024) bit8. Board DVP pins (velapaw-hardware): VSYNC=17 HREF=18 PCLK=41 D0=45 D1=47 D2=48 D3=46 D4=42 D5=40 D6=39 D7=21 (XCLK=38 already LEDC).
87	- **OV5640 config sequence (port from `sensors/ov5640.c` + `ov5640_settings.h`, all via SCCB 16-bit-reg writes):** (1) `write 0x3008=0x82` sw-reset + 100ms; (2) write the whole `sensor_default_regs[]` array (~180 pairs, handles REG_DLY 0xffff=delay-ms, REGLIST_TAIL 0x0000=end); (3) `set_pll(...)` writes 0x3034=0x1A,0x3035,0x3036,0x3037,0x3108,0x3824,0x460C,0x3103=0x13 — PLL params set PCLK; (4) pixformat RGB565 = `sensor_fmt_rgb565`: **FORMAT_CTRL 0x501F=0x01, FORMAT_CTRL00 0x4300=0x61**; (5) `set_framesize` = windowing writes X_ADDR_ST/END(0x3800..0x3807), **X_OUTPUT_SIZE 0x3808/0x380A = w/h**, X_TOTAL_SIZE(0x380C), X_OFFSET(0x3810), ISP scale bit 0x5001; needs the `resolution[]`+`ratio_table` from ov5640.c for a chosen size (QVGA 320x240). (6) `set_image_options`: **SELFIE MIRROR = write TIMING_TC_REG21 (0x3821) |= 0x06 (hmirror) + reg 0x4514=0xbb** (h-mirror case); vflip = 0x3820|=0x06. In-sensor hmirror is the clean selfie flip (or do it in software `sx=CAM_W-1-...`). Also enable color-bar TEST via 0x503D=0xC0 for a lens-independent capture sanity check.
88	- **PHASE 2 CAPTURE WORKS (2026-07-07) — OV5640 color-bar test pattern captured & VISIBLE ON THE PANEL.** The full custom DVP stack works: LEDC XCLK -> OV5640 SCCB QVGA-RGB565 config -> LCD_CAM camera mode -> NuttX GDMA RX -> PSRAM -> bit-bang blit. Recognizable colors (red/green/white/magenta/blue) = DVP path + RGB565 format fundamentally correct. All code is in the board file `esp32s3_st7789.c` (funcs: `ov5640_wr`, `ov_default_regs[]`, `ov5640_config_qvga`, `cam_pins_init`, `cam_lcdcam_init`, `cam_dma_init`, `cam_capture_once`, `cam_blit`, `cam_capture_test`). **REQUIRED CONFIG: `CONFIG_ESP32S3_DMA=y`** (else `esp32s3_dma_*` undefined at link). Working CAM_CTRL = `(3<<29)|(8<<9)|(4<<1)` (clk_sel=3, clkm_div=8, vsync_filter_thres=4); CAM_CTRL1 = `0xffff | (1<<23)`; NuttX GDMA: `esp32s3_dma_request(ESP32S3_DMA_PERIPH_LCDCAM,0,1,true)` gave chan 0, buf in PSRAM (0x3c0c0040), 38 descs; `cache_invalidate_addr` before reading.
89	- **PHASE 2b DONE — CLEAN full-frame capture (2026-07-07):** vertical color bars, no banding/shear, fill the frame. FIX = **VSYNC-sync + vs_eof**: `cam_wait_vsync()` polls the VSYNC pad level directly (`(rreg(0x6000403C /*GPIO_IN_REG*/) >> 17) & 1`; wait high-pulse then low = frame start), then reset AFIFO + arm the GDMA at that frame start, with **CAM_CTRL vs_eof_en=1** so the DMA runs to the next VSYNC = exactly one aligned frame. (Earlier: no-sync no-vs_eof gave shear/banding = over-capture of >1 frame; vs_eof without sync gave a partial frame.) Capture is now solid.
90	- **COLOR mapping still off** (bars show scrambled colors; white+green right, others swapped). Flipping the blit byte order (p[x]/p[x+1]) did NOT change it → it's a **channel (R/B) or sensor format** thing, NOT blit byte order. Defer to phase 3: fix in the RGB565->RGB888 conversion (extract R/G/B, remap channels) against a REAL scene, or try sensor FORMAT_CTRL00=0x6F vs 0x61 / CAM_CTRL byte_order bit5. Not a blocker. 
91	- **lcdfb OVERWRITES boot-time bit-bang blits:** a blit done in `board_lcd_initialize` gets painted over ~instantly by the `lcdfb`/`/dev/fb0` initial flush of stale PSRAM (the persistent medium-blue = last velapaw LVGL screen). To SEE a boot capture I added a TEMP `up_mdelay(15000)` after `cam_capture_test` in board_lcd_initialize (REMOVE it later). Real visualization = go through `/dev/fb0` / the velapaw preview (phase 3).
92	- **PHASE 3 DONE — LIVE OV5640 CAMERA WORKING IN VELAPAW ON HARDWARE (2026-07-08).** Real recognizable image in the Enroll/Recognize preview, live-updating, enrollment captures real thumbnails. Architecture: board exposes globals `board_ov5640_init(i2c)` (config once at boot, called from board_lcd_initialize after panel_init) + `board_ov5640_capture(uint8_t**buf,int*w,int*h)` (VSYNC-synced grab into g_cambuf). App HAL `hal/camera_ov5640.c` (swapped for camera_mock.c in the velapaw Makefile CSRCS) externs board_ov5640_capture (**FLAT build → app can call board fns directly**), downscales 320x240 RGB565 -> 128x128 RGB888 with selfie mirror (`mx=(w-1)-sx`). **KEY FIX: RGB565 is BIG-ENDIAN in the capture buffer — assemble `px=(p[0]<<8)|p[1]`** (little-endian gave a rainbow scramble). Removed the temp 15s hold + boot blit. **`FRAME_INTERVAL_MS=150`** in ui_lvgl.c for the live preview (was 1000 for the static mock; the event-driven-only preview from the speed pass FROZE the live feed — restored the periodic `if((tab==0||tab==1)&&now-last_frame>...)` grab in the main loop).
93	- **FLASH GOTCHA (cost ~8 failed attempts):** the ESP32-S3 native USB (VID_303A/PID_1001) started giving pyserial **"Write timeout"** on every flash after heavy velapaw/camera use. Cable swap, full power-cycle, `--before usb-reset`, killing stray python, and PnP disable/enable ALL FAILED — **the fix was a DIFFERENT PC USB port** (front-panel/hub port had weak data lines). Flash from a rear/motherboard port.

A mismatch subtracts black-level offsets from the wrong colour cells and crushes a channel.
- **Symptom discriminator (decisive):** a flip/Bayer-phase error *exchanges* red and blue and leaves green untouched (green is 2 of 4 Bayer cells either way) — it physically cannot cause green loss. - **GNU ld `PROVIDE` semantics:** a `PROVIDE` only fires when the symbol is referenced by an **object file**, not when referenced from another linker-script expression. Chained `PROVIDE(a = b)` where `b` is itself only PROVIDEd cannot bootstrap — `b` must be a definite assignment.

One more shim fix needed: **remove `pow` from float_shim.h** — `std::pow(2,15)` (int literals) is ambiguous between the shim's float pow and global double pow (the other 15 shim overloads are fine). After the clean rebuild + pow removal: BUILD OK. NOTE the binary is unchanged size (680656 B) because nothing references tflite-micro yet -> linker drops it as dead code; it's PROVEN to build but not in the image until velapaw's backend is wired.

Steps that worked: (1) generate model C-array: `python3 <tflm>/tensorflow/lite/micro/tools/generate_cc_arrays.py velapaw/infer/gen/velapaw_model_data.cc velapaw/infer/model/velapaw.tflite` (+ .h) — array name derives from OUTPUT name → `g_velapaw_model_data` (matches backend). So it faults/hangs on first access to the 1.4MB model flatbuffer (`tflite::GetModel()` / `g_model->version()`). ## Link trap: `undefined reference to cache_invalidate_addr` (SOLVED 2026-09-05)
The camera code in the board file declares `extern int cache_invalidate_addr(uint32_t,uint32_t);` and calls it before reading the DMA'd PSRAM frame. That symbol is not in any NuttX library — it is a **ROM function** aliased in `boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld` (wired into every S3 board's `Make.defs`). A previous session added `PROVIDE( Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x400016b0 );` there and **it never fires**: GNU ld only honours a `PROVIDE` when the symbol is referenced by an **object file**, not when it is referenced from another linker-script expression — so the chained `PROVIDE( cache_invalidate_addr = Cache_Invalidate_Addr )` on the next line had nothing to resolve to. Fix = make the capitalised one a **definite assignment**:
```
Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x400016b0;
PROVIDE( cache_invalidate_addr = Cache_Invalidate_Addr );
```
(address cross-checked against `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp-hal-3rdparty/components/esp_rom/esp32s3/ld/esp32s3.rom.ld`). Backup `esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld.bak`. **This break is latent** — it only surfaces when something forces a relink of the board objects (e.g. deleting the st7789 `.o` to clear the stale-object trap in [[velapaw-b82-camerafix-rebuild]]), so a tree that "builds fine" can still be carrying it. It's a local edit, so `repo sync` will eat it.

**Build entry point in this tree is `cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4`** — a bare `make` inside `nuttx/` is not the supported path. Also: **do not run `~/openvela/rebuild_camera_fix.sh` when the board file has local edits** — it `wget`s `esp32s3_st7789.c` and `app/velapaw/hal/camera_ov5640.c` from the Windows server on :9100 and silently overwrites them before building.

**What this session proves, in the track guide's terms:**

- `read_file {"path": "/data/ai_agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md"}` is the **first** tool call. The model chose to load your custom Skill unprompted, then followed its steps to read `status.md` and `feed_log.md`. That is the "≥1 custom Skill at `/data/ai_agent/skills/`" requirement demonstrably driving behaviour, not just present on disk.
- `Skills summary: 916 bytes` — the real load signal (`Skills system ready (10 built-in)` is the compile-time constant that lists 10 while the directory holds 12, as expected).
- `END status=ok iters=3 tools=2 llm_ms=5160 elapsed=5s` — real remote round trip, TLS handshake to `api.deepseek.com`, `tools=2` rules out a canned non-answer. Second and third calls reuse the pooled connection.
- `session_clear_all` first means the answer can't be replay from persisted history — a good thing to have on camera for the judges.

**Three things worth knowing before this becomes the submitted evidence:**

1. **`status.md` shrank from 663 B to 288 B** since the run earlier today (`feed_log.md` grew 599 → 658 B, which is just one more feeding — that part is consistent). The whole answer is derived from `status.md`, so it's worth one `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` to confirm all three pets are still in it and the 44 g baseline / "over" body condition are real values rather than a truncated file. I can't verify the numbers from the log alone.

2. **The heartbeat is at 1800 s / 30 min.** Nothing proactive will fire inside a demo window of realistic length. If the proactive scenario is being filmed rather than cited, you need `heartbeat_trigger` on camera or the interval dropped again for the take.

3. **The `[llmdbg]` / `[llmdbg-loop]` / `[llmdbg-skl]` instrumentation dominates the transcript** — roughly 80% of those lines are debug scaffolding, and the per-file `readdir`/`stat` trace alone is ~40 lines before the agent does anything. For a report appendix or video that's noise a judge has to read past. It's a `syslog` verbosity question, not a code change, if you want a cleaner take.

The lead I'd bet on: line 23 is `#include <nuttx/config.h>`, so this script is **preprocessed** before ld sees it — and your boards tree is littered with `esp32s3_CPP:`, `esp32CPP:`, `flat_memory.lCPP:`. Those names look like a `$(CPP)` invocation that lost its `-o` target and wrote output to a mangled filename (`flat_memory.l` + `CPP:`). If the preprocessed script the linker actually consumes is stale or was generated by one of those misfires, the edit on line 29 would never reach ld — and whether it's stale is exactly the kind of thing that can differ between two runs.

The new evidence changes the diagnosis, and not in my favour.

`cache_invalidate_addr` is **also** undefined from `libarch.a(esp32s3_spiflash.o)` at `esp32s3_spiflash.c:735` and `:998` — that's core NuttX arch code, nothing to do with our board file or the camera. And your grep confirms `esp32s3.rom.ld` already defines `Cache_Invalidate_Addr` upstream. So the intended chain is: `esp32s3.rom.ld` defines the capitalised ROM symbol → `rom_aliases.ld` PROVIDEs the lowercase alias.

That means the real fault is that **neither script is reaching the linker**, and my line-29 edit yesterday was addressing a symptom, not the cause. It cannot be the fix — a definite assignment in a script ld never reads does nothing. Whatever made yesterday's build link, I don't currently have an explanation for, and I'm not going to invent one.

Also worth noting: the `CPP:` junk files are 0 bytes, which fits them being artifacts of an unquoted `echo "CPP: $1->$2"` in NuttX's preprocess macro — the `>` got interpreted as a redirect. Harmless in themselves, but they confirm these linker scripts go through a preprocessing step, so the file ld actually reads is a *generated* one we haven't located yet.

This paste gets the actual link command, which settles it:

```sh
cd ~/openvela/nuttx

echo "=== how ARCHSCRIPT becomes ld flags ==="
grep -rn 'ARCHSCRIPT' Make.defs tools/Config.mk tools/Unix.mk \
  arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/Make.defs 2>/dev/null | head -20

echo
echo "=== is the ROM symbol script wired in at all? ==="
grep -rn 'rom\.ld\|esp32s3\.rom\|ROMSCRIPT' \
  arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/Make.defs \
  boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit/scripts/Make.defs 2>/dev/null

echo
echo "=== THE LINK COMMAND: which scripts does ld actually get? ==="
make V=1 nuttx 2>&1 | tee /tmp/link.log
echo
echo "=== -T / script args extracted ==="
grep -o -- '-T[^ ]*' /tmp/link.log | sort -u
grep -o -- '--script[= ][^ ]*' /tmp/link.log | sort -u

echo
echo "=== does the ld line mention rom_aliases or esp32s3.rom? ==="
grep -c 'rom_aliases' /tmp/link.log
grep -c 'esp32s3\.rom\.ld' /tmp/link.log
```

`make V=1 nuttx` only needs to relink — all objects are current — so this is fast, and it will echo the full `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-ld` invocation.

What I expect to see, and what each means:

- **`-T…rom_aliases.ld` absent from the ld line** → `ARCHSCRIPT` isn't being expanded into `LDFLAGS` for this config. That's the actual bug, and it's fixable in the board's `scripts/Make.defs` without touching any script content.
- **`-T…rom_aliases.ld` present** → ld is reading a preprocessed copy, and we go find where that copy lives and whether it's stale.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- NuttX RTOS on ESP32-S3 (8 MB PSRAM, 16 MB flash), built in a VMware Linux VM (`king@king-VMware-Virtual-Platform`, `~/openvela`, VM IP `192.168.160.128`; Windows host as seen from VM is `192.168.160.1`), flashed from Windows 11.
- **COM8** = NuttX CDCACM runtime console (`nsh>`/`vela>`). **COM3** = Espressif USB-Serial/JTAG ROM port.
- **OV5640 `0x4514` is the BLC (black-level calibration) pattern register, coupled to the Bayer phase set by `0x3821`'s flip bits.** mirror **on** → `0x4514 = 0xbb`; mirror **off** → `0x4514 = 0x88`.
- **Symptom discriminator:** a flip/Bayer-phase error *exchanges* red and blue and leaves green untouched — it physically cannot cause green loss. A **BLC-pattern mismatch** produces a violet/magenta frame (R+B, no G). Judge from whole-frame hue.
- **GNU ld `PROVIDE` semantics:** a `PROVIDE` only fires when the symbol is referenced by an **object file**, not from another linker-script expression. Chained `PROVIDE(a = b)` where `b` is itself only PROVIDEd cannot bootstrap.
- **NuttX preprocesses linker scripts** — `#include <nuttx/config.h>` at line 23 of `esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld` — and ld is handed `<name>.ld.tmp` copies, NOT the source `.ld`. **This is the newly-discovered crux.**
- **NuttX's preprocess macro emits `@echo "CPP: $1->$2"`**; the unquoted `>` is the likely origin of the 0-byte junk files `esp32CPP:`, `esp32s3_CPP:`, `flat_memory.lCPP:` in `boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/`.
- **`ai_agent &` backgrounds the agent but nsh keeps stdin.** `sleep 600` is what hands the console to the `vela>` CLI thread.
- **The placeholder `[Agent]:` line is echoed TWICE.** The unambiguous end-of-turn marker is `[trace:...] END status=`.
- **`tools=N` in the END trace is the real/fake discriminator.** `tools=0` = fast non-answer.
- **`Skills summary: NNN bytes` is the real signal a Skill loaded**; `Skills system ready (N built-in)` is a compile-time constant (says 10 while the directory holds 12 files).
- **`(void)0;  // DBGOFF: <original>` is the chosen silencing form** — preserves statement structure so a braceless `if` body can't swallow the following line, keeps the original code greppable and reversible.

"""Capture a presentable ai_agent demo transcript on the debug-silenced build.

Exact bring-up pattern that works on this board:
  3x enter -> nsh>
  ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 ...
  host->board ping (primes ARP; without it the first request stalls)
  ai_agent &
  sleep 600          <- hands the console to the vela> CLI
  session_clear_all  <- rules out history replay
  ask <prompt>

Everything the board prints is written verbatim to clean_demo_transcript.txt.
End of turn is `[trace:...] END status=`, never a count of `[Agent]:` lines.
"""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import serial
import serial.tools.list_ports

PORT = "COM8"
PROMPT = "ask how much did jay eat today"
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "clean_demo_transcript.txt")

ports = [p.device for p in serial.tools.list_ports.comports()]
print(f">>> ports: {ports}", flush=True)
if PORT not in ports:
    sys.exit(f"!!! {PORT} absent. ABORTING.")

lines = []
lock = threading.Lock()
stop = False
t0 = time.time()
fh = open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


def reader(s):
    buf = b""
    while not stop:
        try:
            chunk = s.read(4096)
        except Exception:
            break
        if not chunk:
            continue
        buf += chunk
        while b"\n" in buf:
            one, buf = buf.split(b"\n", 1)
            txt = one.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip("\r")
            with lock:
                lines.append((time.time() - t0, txt))
            fh.write(txt + "\n")
            fh.flush()
            print(txt, flush=True)


ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 115200, timeout=0.2, write_timeout=10)
threading.Thread(target=reader, args=(ser,), daemon=True).start()


def mark():
    with lock:
        return len(lines)


def rows(m):
    with lock:
        return list(lines[m:])


def die(msg):
    global stop
    stop = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
    ser.close()
    fh.close()
    sys.exit(f"!!! {msg}")


def send(cmd, settle=2.0):
    try:
        ser.write((cmd + "\r\n").encode())
    except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
        die(f"write timed out sending {cmd!r} -- console wedged.")
    time.sleep(settle)


# ---- wake: three enters, then a couple more for luck ------------------
print("\n### waking (enter x5)", flush=True)
m = mark()
for _ in range(5):
    try:
        ser.write(b"\r\n")
    except serial.SerialTimeoutException:
        die("write timed out on wake.")
    time.sleep(1.0)
time.sleep(2)

woke = "\n".join(t for _, t in rows(m))
if "nsh>" not in woke and "vela>" not in woke:
    die("no prompt after wake -- console not responding.")
print(f"### prompt: {'vela>' if 'vela>' in woke else 'nsh>'}", flush=True)

if "vela>" not in woke:
    print("\n### ifconfig eth0", flush=True)
    send("ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1", 3)

    print("\n### host->board ping (prime ARP)", flush=True)
    r = subprocess.run(["ping", "-n", "3", "192.168.137.2"],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    for ln in r.stdout.splitlines():
        if "Reply from" in ln or "loss" in ln:
            print(f"    {ln.strip()}", flush=True)

    print("\n### ai_agent &", flush=True)
    send("ai_agent &", 25)

    print("\n### sleep 600 (hand console to vela>)", flush=True)
    m = mark()
    send("sleep 600", 6)
    ser.write(b"\r\n")
    time.sleep(3)
    if "vela>" not in "\n".join(t for _, t in rows(m)):
        die("never reached vela> -- did ai_agent start?")
print("### at vela>.", flush=True)

# ---- clear history so nothing can be replayed ------------------------
print("\n### session_clear_all", flush=True)
send("session_clear_all", 4)

# ---- the ask ---------------------------------------------------------
print(f"\n### {PROMPT!r}", flush=True)
m = mark()
t_send = time.time()
send(PROMPT, 0)

end_line = None
deadline = time.time() + 240
while time.time() < deadline:
    for ts, tx in rows(m):
        if "END status=" in tx:
            end_line = (ts, tx)
            break
    if end_line:
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)

time.sleep(8)
base = t_send - t0

print("\n" + "=" * 60, flush=True)
print("RESULT", flush=True)
print("=" * 60, flush=True)
if not end_line:
    print("!!! no END status= within 240 s -- loop did not complete", flush=True)
else:
    print(f"round-trip: {end_line[0] - base:.1f} s", flush=True)
    print(f"trace: {end_line[1].strip()}", flush=True)
    mt = re.search(r"tools=(\d+)", end_line[1])
    if mt:
        n = int(mt.group(1))
        print(f"tools used: {n} "
              f"({'REAL tool path' if n else 'NO tools -- non-answer'})",
              flush=True)

print("\n--- agent replies (deduped) ---", flush=True)
seen = set()
for ts, tx in rows(m):
    if "[Agent]:" in tx:
        body = tx.split("[Agent]:", 1)[1].strip()
        if body and body not in seen:
            seen.add(body)
            print(f"  {ts - base:6.1f}s  {body}", flush=True)

print("\n--- skills / tool calls ---", flush=True)
for ts, tx in rows(m):
    if any(k in tx for k in ("Skills summary", "Tool call:", "Executing:",
                             "read_file", "Skills system ready")):
        print(f"  {ts - base:6.1f}s  {tx.strip()}", flush=True)

print("\n--- noise check (should be zero) ---", flush=True)
noise = [tx for _, tx in rows(0)
         if any(k in tx for k in ("[llmdbg", "[agent-dbg", "[cli-dbg",
                                  "[nsh_fileapp"))]
print(f"  debug lines on console: {len(noise)}", flush=True)
for tx in noise[:5]:
    print(f"    {tx.strip()}", flush=True)

time.sleep(1)
stop = True
time.sleep(0.5)
ser.close()
fh.close()
print(f"\n>>> transcript: {OUT}", flush=True)

Shadow trick = read GPIO_OUT_REG(0x60004004) once → `base = out & ~(MOSI|CLK)` (preserves other pins) → per bit write `base|data` then `base|data|CLK_M` (2 writes, CLK falls at next bit's data write). ## Link trap: a link that fails with HUNDREDS of undefined ROM symbols = **empty `*.ld.tmp` files** (SOLVED 2026-09-05)
**The real root cause, and the one to check FIRST.** NuttX preprocesses every linker script (`esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld` starts with `#include <nuttx/config.h>`) and hands **`<name>.ld.tmp` copies** to `ld`, not the `.ld` sources. An interrupted or failed build leaves those `.tmp` files **0 bytes**. `ld` then gets ten `-T` scripts that are all empty — the command line looks perfectly correct (`grep -c rom_aliases` on the `make V=1` log returns 1), but every ROM symbol and every linker-defined memory symbol is missing.

**Symptom:** a flood of `undefined reference` across `esp32s3_start.o`, `libarch.a(esp32s3_psram_octal.o / rtc_clk.o / cache_hal.o / mmu_hal.o / esp_rom_uart.o / bootloader_*.o / esp_loader.o / regi2c_ctrl.o / clk.o)` — `ets_printf`, `esp_rom_*`, `cache_*`, `Cache_*`, `wdt_hal_*`, `EFUSE`, `UART0/1/2`, `TIMERG0`, `RTCCNTL`, `_bss_start/_bss_end/_sheap/_init_start`, `_image_irom_*`, `_rodata_reserved_*` — plus `dangerous relocation: l32r: literal placed after use` from libgcc. **Do not chase any single name from that list**; `tail`ing the log makes whichever one printed last (here `cache_invalidate_addr` from `esp32s3_st7789.c`) look like the whole bug. It isn't.

**Diagnose:** `ls -l` the `.tmp` files — `find nuttx -name '*.ld.tmp' -size 0`. **Fix:** delete them so they regenerate, then rebuild:
```sh
cd ~/openvela/nuttx && find . -name '*.ld.tmp' -size 0 -delete
cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4
```
Related junk: 0-byte files named `esp32CPP:` / `esp32s3_CPP:` / `flat_memory.lCPP:` in `boards/xtensa/esp32s3/common/scripts/` are leftovers of a broken `$(ECHO_BEGIN)"CPP: $1->$2"` echo (`PREPROCESS` macro, `tools/Config.mk:287`). Harmless, delete them.

**CORRECTION — the `PROVIDE`-chain theory recorded here earlier was wrong.** I had concluded the break was `esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld`'s chained `PROVIDE( cache_invalidate_addr = Cache_Invalidate_Addr )` never firing (GNU ld only honours a `PROVIDE` when an **object file** references the symbol, not another linker-script expression) and "fixed" it by making the capitalised one a definite assignment (`Cache_Invalidate_Addr = 0x400016b0;`). The ld semantics are real, but they were **not** what broke this build — the `.ld` source was intact the whole time and `ld` was reading an empty `.tmp` copy of it. That edit is still in the tree, is harmless, and cannot be credited with the fix. Backup `esp32s3_rom_aliases.ld.bak`. It's a local edit, so `repo sync` will eat it.

Full-desktop recording would capture everything you have open — Chrome, VS Code, the GitHub repo page, Hotspot Shield, VMware. I'd rather not put that in a contest video, so I'll pin the demo window to a fixed spot and record **only that region**:

input.content:
# Screen-record the ai_agent demo run.
#
# Win11 hosts consoles inside Windows Terminal, so ffmpeg's `-i title=...`
# window capture can't find them. Instead: launch the demo, move its window to
# a known position/size, bring it to the front, and capture ONLY that region of
# the desktop -- so nothing else that's open ends up in the recording.
#
# Output is .mkv (playable even if the capture is cut short), remuxed to .mp4.

$here = "C:\Users\VICTUS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9\scratchpad"
$stamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss"
$mkv = Join-Path $here "velapaw_demo_$stamp.mkv"
$title = "VelaPaw ai_agent demo"

# region to capture (even numbers -- libx264 rejects odd dimensions)
$X = 0; $Y = 0; $W = 1280; $H = 760

Add-Type @"
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public class Win {
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetWindowPos(IntPtr h, IntPtr after, int x, int y, int cx, int cy, uint flags);
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetForegroundWindow(IntPtr h);
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool ShowWindow(IntPtr h, int cmd);
}
"@

Write-Host ">>> launching demo window"
$demo = Start-Process -FilePath "cmd.exe" -PassThru -WorkingDirectory $here `
    -ArgumentList @("/c", "title $title & py clean_demo.py --preroll 20")

# find the window (it belongs to WindowsTerminal.exe, not cmd.exe)
$hwnd = [IntPtr]::Zero
for ($i = 0; $i -lt 40; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
    $w = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.MainWindowTitle -like "*$title*" } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($w) { $hwnd = $w.MainWindowHandle; break }
}

if ($hwnd -ne [IntPtr]::Zero) {
    [Win]::ShowWindow($hwnd, 9) | Out-Null          # SW_RESTORE
    [Win]::SetWindowPos($hwnd, [IntPtr]::Zero, $X, $Y, $W, $H, 0x0040) | Out-Null
    [Win]::SetForegroundWindow($hwnd) | Out-Null
    Write-Host ">>> demo window pinned to ${W}x${H} at ${X},${Y}"
} else {
    Write-Host "!!! could not locate the demo window -- capturing the region anyway"
}

Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
Write-Host ">>> starting capture -> $mkv"
$ff = Start-Process -FilePath "ffmpeg" -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden -ArgumentList @(
    "-y", "-loglevel", "error",
    "-f", "gdigrab", "-framerate", "12",
    "-offset_x", $X, "-offset_y", $Y, "-video_size", "${W}x${H}",
    "-i", "desktop", "-t", "300",
    "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "20",
    "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", $mkv
)

$demo.WaitForExit()
Write-Host ">>> demo exited with code $($demo.ExitCode)"

Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
if (-not $ff.HasExited) { Stop-Process -Id $ff.Id -Force }
Start-Sleep -Seconds 2

if (-not (Test-Path $mkv)) { Write-Host "!!! no recording produced"; exit 1 }
$f = Get-Item $mkv
Write-Host ">>> recording: $($f.FullName)  $([math]::Round($f.Length/1MB,2)) MB"

# still frame from near the end, so the capture can be eyeballed
& ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -sseof -6 -i $mkv -frames:v 1 (Join-Path $here "demo_frame_check.png")

$mp4 = [IO.Path]::ChangeExtension($mkv, ".mp4")
& ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i $mkv -c copy $mp4
if (Test-Path $mp4) { Write-Host ">>> mp4: $mp4  $([math]::Round((Get-Item $mp4).Length/1MB,2)) MB" }

& ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height `
    -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 $mkv

Important catch — that recorded take is **not** valid evidence:

```
[agent] Cache hit, skipping LLM call
[trace:...] END status=ok iters=1 tools=0 llm_ms=0 elapsed=0s
```

`tools=0`, `llm_ms=0`. Asking the identical question again hit the RAM `llm_cache` and replayed the earlier answer without calling the LLM at all. That's the known cache-poisoning trap — only the *first* run after the flash was real (`iters=3 tools=2 llm_ms=5730`). A judge reading `tools=0` would see a canned reply.

input.content:
# Record the ai_agent demo through PuTTY on COM8.
#
# PuTTY is a classic Win32 window (unlike Win11's console host, which lives
# inside WindowsTerminal.exe), so ffmpeg can capture it by title -- only the
# terminal is recorded, nothing else on the desktop.
#
# PuTTY owns COM8 while it runs, so the transcript comes from PuTTY's own
# session logging rather than from a second serial reader.
#
# usage:  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File record_putty_demo.ps1 "ask <novel prompt>"
#
# The board's llm_cache is RAM-resident and keyed on the prompt: re-asking a
# question already asked since the last reboot replays it with tools=0/llm_ms=0.
# Always pass a prompt that has not been used since boot.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$here   = "C:\Users\VICTUS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9\scratchpad"
$putty  = "C:\Program Files\PuTTY\putty.exe"
$stamp  = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss"
$mkv    = Join-Path $here "velapaw_putty_$stamp.mkv"
$log    = Join-Path $here "putty_session_$stamp.log"
$sess   = "VelaPawDemo"

$Prompt = if ($args.Count -ge 1) { $args[0] } else { "ask give me todays feeding digest for jay" }

# ---- port check -------------------------------------------------------
$ports = [System.IO.Ports.SerialPort]::GetPortNames()
Write-Host ">>> ports: $($ports -join ', ')"
if ($ports -notcontains "COM8") { Write-Host "!!! COM8 absent -- aborting"; exit 1 }

# ---- a saved PuTTY session, so the recording is legible ---------------
# PuTTY takes font/size only from a saved session, not the command line.
$key = "HKCU:\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions\$sess"
if (-not (Test-Path $key)) { New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null }
$sz = @{
    Protocol          = "serial"
    SerialLine        = "COM8"
    Font              = "Consolas"
    LogFileName       = $log
    LineCodePage      = "UTF-8"
}
$dw = @{
    SerialSpeed       = 115200
    SerialDataBits    = 8
    SerialStopHalfbits= 2
    SerialParity      = 0
    SerialFlowControl = 0
    FontHeight        = 14
    FontIsBold        = 0
    FontCharSet       = 0
    TermWidth         = 118
    TermHeight        = 34
    ScrollbackLines   = 20000
    LogType           = 2      # all session output
    LogFlush          = 1
    LogFileClash      = 0      # overwrite, never prompt
    CloseOnExit       = 0
    UTF8Override      = 1
}
foreach ($k in $sz.Keys) { New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name $k -Value $sz[$k] -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null }
foreach ($k in $dw.Keys) { New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name $k -Value $dw[$k] -PropertyType DWord  -Force | Out-Null }
Write-Host ">>> PuTTY session '$sess' configured (COM8, Consolas 14, log -> $log)"

Add-Type @"
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public class Win {
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetWindowPos(IntPtr h, IntPtr after, int x, int y, int cx, int cy, uint flags);
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetForegroundWindow(IntPtr h);
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool ShowWindow(IntPtr h, int cmd);
}
"@

Write-Host ">>> launching PuTTY"
$pt = Start-Process -FilePath $putty -PassThru -ArgumentList @("-load", $sess)

$hwnd = [IntPtr]::Zero; $wtitle = $null
for ($i = 0; $i -lt 40; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
    $pt.Refresh()
    if ($pt.MainWindowHandle -ne [IntPtr]::Zero) {
        $hwnd = $pt.MainWindowHandle; $wtitle = $pt.MainWindowTitle; break
    }
}
if ($hwnd -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) { Write-Host "!!! PuTTY window never appeared"; exit 1 }
Write-Host ">>> window: '$wtitle'"

[Win]::ShowWindow($hwnd, 9) | Out-Null
[Win]::SetWindowPos($hwnd, [IntPtr]::Zero, 40, 40, 0, 0, 0x0041) | Out-Null   # move only, keep size
[Win]::SetForegroundWindow($hwnd) | Out-Null
Start-Sleep -Seconds 2

Write-Host ">>> starting capture -> $mkv"
$ff = Start-Process -FilePath "ffmpeg" -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden -ArgumentList @(
    "-y", "-loglevel", "error",
    "-f", "gdigrab", "-framerate", "12", "-i", "title=$wtitle",
    "-t", "420",
    "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "20",
    "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-vf", "scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2",
    $mkv
)
Start-Sleep -Seconds 3

# ---- drive the session ------------------------------------------------
$wsh = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell

function Type-Line([string]$text, [int]$settle = 2) {
    $wsh.AppActivate($pt.Id) | Out-Null
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 200
    foreach ($ch in $text.ToCharArray()) {
        $wsh.SendKeys([string]$ch)
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 45          # human-paced, readable on video
    }
    $wsh.SendKeys("{ENTER}")
    Start-Sleep -Seconds $settle
}

Write-Host ">>> waking console (enter x3)"
$wsh.AppActivate($pt.Id) | Out-Null
Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 400
for ($i = 0; $i -lt 3; $i++) { $wsh.SendKeys("{ENTER}"); Start-Sleep -Seconds 1 }
Start-Sleep -Seconds 2

$so_far = if (Test-Path $log) { Get-Content $log -Raw } else { "" }
if ($so_far -notmatch "vela>") {
    Write-Host ">>> not at vela> -- bringing the agent up"
    Type-Line "ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1" 3
    Write-Host ">>> host->board ping (primes ARP)"
    ping -n 3 192.168.137.2 | Select-String "Reply from|loss" | ForEach-Object { "    $_" }
    Type-Line "ai_agent &" 25
    Type-Line "sleep 600" 6
    $wsh.SendKeys("{ENTER}"); Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
} else {
    Write-Host ">>> already at vela>"
}

Write-Host ">>> session_clear_all"
Type-Line "session_clear_all" 4

Write-Host ">>> $Prompt"
$askMark = (Get-Item $log).Length
Type-Line $Prompt 0

$deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(240)
$endLine = $null
while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    $fs = New-Object IO.FileStream($log, 'Open', 'Read', 'ReadWrite')
    $sr = New-Object IO.StreamReader($fs)
    $null = $fs.Seek($askMark, 'Begin')
    $tail = $sr.ReadToEnd()
    $sr.Close(); $fs.Close()
    $m = [regex]::Match($tail, "\[trace:[0-9a-f]+\] END status=.*")
    if ($m.Success) { $endLine = $m.Value.Trim(); break }
}

if ($endLine) { Write-Host ">>> $endLine" } else { Write-Host "!!! no END status= within 240 s" }

Write-Host ">>> holding 25 s so the reply stays on screen"
Start-Sleep -Seconds 25

# ---- stop cleanly -----------------------------------------------------
# x264 -preset veryfast holds several seconds of frames; force-killing ffmpeg
# discards them, which once truncated the recording right before the reply.
Start-Sleep -Seconds 6
if (-not $ff.HasExited) { Stop-Process -Id $ff.Id -Force }
Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
if (-not $pt.HasExited) { Stop-Process -Id $pt.Id -Force }

if (-not (Test-Path $mkv)) { Write-Host "!!! no recording produced"; exit 1 }
Write-Host ">>> recording: $mkv  $([math]::Round((Get-Item $mkv).Length/1MB,2)) MB"

$mp4 = [IO.Path]::ChangeExtension($mkv, ".mp4")
& ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i $mkv -c copy $mp4
if (Test-Path $mp4) { Write-Host ">>> mp4: $mp4  $([math]::Round((Get-Item $mp4).Length/1MB,2)) MB" }
& ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height `
    -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 $mkv
Write-Host ">>> transcript: $log  ($((Get-Item $log).Length) bytes)"

+

Compared the local tree against `openvela/dev-ai-contest-2026` (upstream head `101c3a2`). Nothing is committed or pushed.

## Summary

The pushed repo is **VelaPaw without the agent**. The entire step 0–8 `ai_agent` body of work exists locally but has never been committed — 8 modified files, 4 new paths, ~523 insertions.

One commit exists locally that isn't on open-vela: `6849b01` "docs: state repository + contest branch explicitly at the top of both READMEs" (2 lines). It's pushed to your `KingMbewe` fork, not upstream.

## What's new and uncommitted

**1. The agent layer — `agent/`, ~75 KB, entirely new**

| File | |
|---|---|
| `agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md` | 1,084 B — the contest-required custom Skill |
| `agent/HEARTBEAT.md` | 281 B — proactive trigger |
| `agent/README.md` | 4.7 KB |
| `agent/patches/0001-platform-bringup.patch` | 15.7 KB — `agent_compat.h`, `agent_config.h`, `agent_main.c`, `agent_mem.h`, `network_manager.c`, `vela_tls.c` |
| `agent/patches/0002-request-size-and-transport.patch` | 11.8 KB — `tool_registry.c` (the 20-tool cut), `llm_proxy.c`, `llm_router.c`, `cmd_llm.c` |
| `agent/patches/0003-agent-correctness.patch` | 43.3 KB — `agent_loop.c`, `context_builder.c`, `memory_store.c`, `tool_files.c`, `skill_loader.c`, `nsh_commands.c`, `heartbeat.c`, `config_store.c` |

`contest2026_043_CircuitForge.xml` gains one line linkfiling `agent/` → `packages/demos/contest2026_043_velapaw_agent`.

**2. Device code — 3 files**

- `store_stub.c` **+432 lines**: agent-readable persistence (`history.bin`, `status.md`, `feed_log.md` under `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/`) via 10 new statics, plus the civil-day rollover fix (`vp_days_from_civil`/`vp_sync_day`/`vp_shift_days`) and the VP01→VP02 header bump.
- `ui_lvgl.c`: clock seed changed from a one-shot pre-2017 plausibility test to a self-correcting build-date **floor** (`VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR` = 2026-09-03).
- `app/velapaw/Makefile` + `board/esp32s3_appinit.c`: velapaw stack **131072 → 49152**, changed in step in both places, because task stacks now come from the `XTENSA_IMEM` heap and `ai_agent` needs the room.

**3. Docs** — new `docs/AI_AGENT.md` + `_zh` (14 KB each); both READMEs gain a §4 on the agent, a status paragraph, and §4–9 renumbered to §5–10.

**4. Logs** — new 30 MB jsonl for 2026-09-04; manifest event count 18,426 → 40,922.

## Gaps worth knowing about — on the board but in *neither* GitHub nor the local repo

These matter more than the uncommitted diff, because they mean a clean clone can't reproduce the firmware in the demo video:

1. **`board/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig` is dated 2026-08-06 and contains zero agent symbols** — no `CONFIG_EXAMPLES_AI_AGENT_VELA`, no `IOB_NBUFFERS`/`NCHAINS`/`THROTTLE`, no `XTENSA_IMEM_*`/`ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS`. Building from the repo as it stands produces firmware with no agent at all. Every one of those symbols is load-bearing — the IMEM trio is the PSRAM-stack freeze fix, the IOB trio is what took `ask` from stalling to ~4 s.

2. **The three patches are a pre-silencing snapshot.** They add **115** `[llmdbg-*]`/`[agent-dbg]`/`[cli-dbg]` syslog lines and remove none. They were generated 2026-09-04 09:27, before the debug-silencing pass — so rebuilding from them gives the noisy console, not the clean one in the video.

3. **Committed `nuttx.bin` is the pre-agent binary** — 2026-08-09, md5 `e8d9b7c3…`, **zero** `ai_agent` strings, vs the flashed build `ce83189340b3422e0a…`. It's stale by a month.

4. **The camera violet fix is absent.** `board/esp32s3_st7789.c` still carries the comment `0x4514 -- ruled out last round`, i.e. it predates yesterday's `0x4514 → 0x88` fix. Repo camera output would still be violet on agent builds.

5. `VelaPaw_Demo.mp4` (55.8 MB) is the old video; the 59 s combined cut isn't in the repo. Today's session log isn't collected either — the untracked one stops at 2026-09-04 00:53.

**One caveat on scope:** this is a Windows-side comparison only. The VM tree `~/openvela` is authoritative and I didn't touch it, so the `D:` mirror may lag the VM in ways not visible here — items 1 and 4 are direct evidence that it does.

4	The narrative write-up is in **[../docs/AI_AGENT.md](../docs/AI_AGENT.md)**
5	([中文](../docs/AI_AGENT_zh.md)); this file is the operational index.
6	
7	```
8	agent/
9	├── skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md   the custom Skill
10	├── HEARTBEAT.md                       the proactive task list
11	└── patches/                           changes to packages/ai_agent
12	```
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Board assets (`skills/`, `HEARTBEAT.md`)
17	
18	These two files are **runtime data on the board's littlefs**, not source that
19	the build consumes. At runtime they live at:
20	
21	| Repo file | Board path |
22	|---|---|
23	| `skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md` | `/data/ai_agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md` |
24	| `HEARTBEAT.md` | `/data/ai_agent/HEARTBEAT.md` |
25	
26	> **They are not installed by the build or by the manifest linkfile.** The
27	> linkfile only makes them visible inside the openVela tree. Provisioning is a
28	> separate step — they must be written to `/data` once per board, over the NSH
29	> console or by mounting the littlefs image. They then persist across reboots
30	> and across firmware reflashes, because `write-flash 0x0 nuttx.bin` writes
31	> 0x0–~0x17ec80 and the `/data` partition starts at **0x180000**.
32	
33	Two gotchas if you provision over the console: NSH truncates an input line at
34	~80 characters (`CONFIG_NSH_LINELEN`), so long `echo … >> /long/path` commands
35	are silently cut mid-string and leave a corrupt file; and verify by comparing
36	`ls -l`'s byte count against what you intended, not by reading the console echo
37	— the echo shows the *command*, not the file.
38	
39	## 2. Framework patches (`patches/`)
40	
41	Against `packages/ai_agent` at commit **`41723c6`**. The three patches touch
42	**disjoint file sets**, so each applies independently and in any order.
43	
44	| Patch | Files | What it fixes |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| `0001-platform-bringup.patch` | 6 | Makes the agent run at all on a 16 MB ESP32-S3: PSRAM-stack freeze, the heap walk that kills a freshly-booted board, LLM/socket timeouts (420 s / 480 s), task stacks |
47	| `0002-request-size-and-transport.patch` | 4 | Makes it fast and reliable: excludes 20 tools irrelevant to a feeder (schemas were 9 946 B of a 19 391 B request, against a ~7 840 B usable IOB budget), plus HTTP retry and transport handling |
48	| `0003-agent-correctness.patch` | 8 | Makes the answers *right*: heartbeat session replay, the `list_dir` prefix and local-tool-shortcut defects, the stale-history freshness directive, `ask` truncating at 7 words, and the natural-language fast paths left dispatching to tools `0002` removed |
49	
50	Applying them:
51	
52	```bash
53	cd <openvela-workspace>/packages/ai_agent
54	git apply --check ../../contest2026_043_CircuitForge/agent/patches/*.patch  # dry run
55	git apply         ../../contest2026_043_CircuitForge/agent/patches/*.patch
56	```
57	
58	Then force a rebuild of the C files — **header-only edits do not recompile
59	dependents in this tree**, which will silently give you a stale image:
60	
61	```bash
62	find packages/ai_agent/src -name '*.c' -exec touch {} +
63	./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4
64	```
65	
66	`0001` also depends on three Kconfig symbols that are **not** in these patches
67	because they belong to the board config, not the framework — they are in
68	[`../board/configs/`](../board/configs/):
69	`XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP`, `XTENSA_IMEM_REGION_SIZE=0x30000`, and the
70	easily-missed `ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS`. Without all three the agent task's stack
71	lands in PSRAM and the first `ask` freezes the whole chip.
72	
73	## 3. Verifying a build really has the changes
74

76	than assume:

79	grep AI_AGENT nuttx/.config
80	strings nuttx/nuttx.bin | grep -i ai_agent
81	md5sum nuttx/nuttx.bin        # image size is NOT a usable identifier
82	```

87	
88	If you ever change the `s_excluded_tools[]` denylist in `0002`, re-run this
89	grep and require it to come back **empty** — cutting a tool leaves callers

98	- `[skills] Skills summary: NNN bytes` — the real signal that skills loaded.

100	  nothing.**
101	- `END status=ok iters=N tools=M` — read this, not the prose. An answer that
102	  reads perfectly with `iters=1 tools=0` was replayed from history, not derived

   - **PuTTY takes font/terminal size only from a saved session** (registry `HKCU:\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions\<name>`), not the command line. `LogType=2` + `LogFlush=1` + `LogFileClash=0` gives a session transcript without a second serial reader.

   - **PuTTY renames its window asynchronously** (`PuTTY` → `COM8 - PuTTY`); gdigrab title matching requires an EXACT match, so it races. Region capture avoids this.
   - **`GetWindowRect` includes Win11's invisible resize border (~8–20 px)** and can return a pre-resize height. **`DwmGetWindowAttribute(hwnd, 9, ...)` (DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS) returns the pixels actually painted.**

   - **Debug silencing is implemented as `(void)0;  // DBGOFF: syslog(...)`** — the original call is preserved as a comment, so grepping for `[llmdbg` or `LOG_INFO` in a patch counts commented-out lines and is a false positive. The correct test excludes lines containing `DBGOFF`.


   ```powershell
   # Three enters, not one: a freshly booted board eats the first \r\n on connect,
   # so a single Enter can leave the terminal blank and the ls goes nowhere.
   for ($i = 0; $i -lt 3; $i++) { $wsh.SendKeys("{ENTER}"); Start-Sleep -Seconds 1 }

   ```

   ```powershell

   # muxer's finalise step, which on a short capture means x264 has flushed
   # nothing yet -- the previous run left a 0-byte, headerless mkv that way.
   Write-Host ">>> waiting for ffmpeg to finish and finalise the file"
   ```

Full diff review done — here are the last two files, then what I copied.

## `board/esp32s3_appinit.c` — +145 / −0 (purely additive)

The `VELAPAW_AUTOSTART_STACK 49152` change was already in the repo; nothing was removed. The 145 added lines are one self-contained block: a **telnetd auto-start** that brings NSH up on TCP/23 over the USB network, written during the 2026-09-01 bring-up when the CDC-ACM console was thought dead.

Three things worth knowing about it:

- It **does not run.** The call site is `// telnetd_autostart(); // TEMP-DISABLED 2026-09-02 for console-close(0/1/2) hang isolation test`. It is compiled-out dead code in the flashed firmware.
- It carries a hand-copied local mirror of `struct telnetd_config_s`, with a comment recording the real bug it hit — a field-type mismatch (`t_priority` as `int` instead of `uint8_t`) silently corrupted every field after it, so port 23 accepted nothing. That's a genuinely useful note.
- `telnetd_debug_announce()` UDP-blasts to hardcoded `10.0.0.1:9999` — the pre-ICS golden address, now stale (the board is `192.168.137.2`).

## `board/esp32s3_bringup.c` — +54 / −40

Three real changes, mostly **reordering**:

1. **tmpfs mount moved earlier** (before the SPIRAM bankswitch block), with a comment recording that the old tmpfs-at-`/data` mount was deleted on 2026-09-01 because it raced/shadowed the real littlefs mount and meant `/data` never survived a reboot.
2. **The whole `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIRELESS` block moved ~220 lines earlier**, and gained:
   ```c
   #ifdef CONFIG_USBDEV_COMPOSITE
     board_composite_connect(0, 0);
   #endif
   ```
   This is **load-bearing** — it's what enumerates the CDC-ACM + CDC-NCM composite, i.e. COM8 *and* `eth0`. Without it there is no console and no networking.

   ⚠️ One thing to flag: `board_composite_connect()` is nested **inside** the `#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIRELESS` guard. USB composite has nothing to do with WiFi. It works today only because the defconfig happens to enable wireless; turn WiFi off and the console silently disappears. That's an accidental coupling, not a deliberate one.
3. Adds `syslog(LOG_ERR, "[bringup] fb_register ret=%d\n", ret);` — one new boot-time debug line, plus `#include <malloc.h>` and `#include <nuttx/board.h>`.

## Copied into the working tree

All 8 files, md5-verified byte-identical to the VM source:

| Destination | |
|---|---|
| `nuttx.bin` | `ce83189…a8a5c` — matches the flashed build |
| `board/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig` | +76/−5 |

They're the same class of gap — without them the repo's `board/` doesn't build the `nuttx.bin` sitting next to it — but say the word and I'll revert either one; they're plain file copies, `git checkout -- board/esp32s3_appinit.c board/esp32s3_bringup.c` undoes them.

# Shrink real.mp4 (483 MB, 2560x1440@30, 4:58) under GitHub's 10 MB comfort limit
# and even out its audio.
#
# Audio: the source is NOT quiet (-16.35 LUFS integrated) -- the problem is an
# LRA of 14.5, i.e. loud stretches and near-inaudible ones. So the balancing is
# the compressor; loudnorm afterwards just re-lands the level at -16 LUFS with
# 1.5 dB of true-peak headroom. measured_* come from a run of THIS chain, not
# of the bare input -- the compressor changes what loudnorm sees.
#
# Video: two-pass ABR, because CRF cannot hit a byte target and this one is
# tight -- ~0.009 bpp at 720p30. hqdn3d runs BEFORE the scale: handheld phone
# footage is noisy, and at this bitrate the noise would eat bits that the LCD
# text needs.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$dir = "C:\Users\VICTUS\Downloads\VelaPaw-demo-20260905"
$src = Join-Path $dir "real.mp4"
$out = Join-Path $dir "real_10mb.mp4"
$sp  = "C:\Users\VICTUS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9\scratchpad"
$plg = Join-Path $sp "real_x264"

$VBIT = "205k"     # 205k video + 64k audio over 298.6 s ~= 9.6 MB incl. mux overhead
$ABIT = "64k"

$vf = "hqdn3d=3:2:6:4,scale=1280:-2:flags=lanczos"
$af = "pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0+0.5*c1," +
      "highpass=f=70," +
      "acompressor=threshold=-22dB:ratio=3:attack=15:release=250," +
      "loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=8:measured_I=-27.03:measured_TP=-5.31:" +
      "measured_LRA=7.80:measured_thresh=-37.76:offset=0.51:linear=true," +
      "aresample=48000"

Remove-Item "$plg*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

Write-Host ">>> pass 1/2 (video stats)"
& ffmpeg -y -hide_banner -loglevel error -stats -i $src `
    -an -vf $vf -c:v libx264 -preset slower -b:v $VBIT `
    -pass 1 -passlogfile $plg -pix_fmt yuv420p -f mp4 NUL
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "pass 1 failed ($LASTEXITCODE)" }

Write-Host ">>> pass 2/2 (video + balanced audio)"
& ffmpeg -y -hide_banner -loglevel error -stats -i $src `
    -vf $vf -c:v libx264 -preset slower -b:v $VBIT `
    -pass 2 -passlogfile $plg -pix_fmt yuv420p -profile:v high `
    -af $af -c:a aac -b:a $ABIT -ac 1 -ar 48000 `
    -movflags +faststart $out
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "pass 2 failed ($LASTEXITCODE)" }

$mb = [math]::Round((Get-Item $out).Length / 1MB, 2)
Write-Host ">>> $out  = $mb MB"
& ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration,size,bit_rate `
    -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height,channels,sample_rate,bit_rate `
    -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 -- $out

Analysed `real.mp4` first — 483 MB, 2560×1440@30, 4:58.6, 13.4 Mbps.

On the audio: it isn't quiet (integrated **−16.35 LUFS**, peaks at −0.8 dBTP). What's unbalanced is the **range** — LRA **14.5**, so loud stretches sit ~15 dB above the quiet narration. So the fix is compression first, then re-levelling:

- downmix to mono (L−R measures −44.5 dB vs −20.2 dB, so the stereo carries almost nothing — mono buys real quality per bit at this budget)
- 70 Hz highpass, then `acompressor` 3:1 @ −22 dB → LRA **14.5 → 7.8**
- two-pass `loudnorm` to **−16 LUFS / −1.5 dBTP**, measured against the compressed chain rather than the raw input

On the size: 10 MB over 298.6 s is ~267 kbps total, so it's a genuinely tight budget for handheld footage. 205k video (two-pass ABR — CRF can't hit a byte target) + 64k audio, downscaled to 1280×720, with `hqdn3d` ahead of the scale so the phone's sensor noise doesn't eat the bits the LCD text needs. Checked for letterboxing — none consistent, so no crop.

Two-pass encode running in the background. I'll check a frame of the small on-screen text when it lands and drop to 960×540 if 720p turns out too mushy to read.

# Pass 2 only -- the pass-1 stats log is still valid (identical video filter
# chain and output resolution; only the rate target changed).
#
# Two fixes over the first run:
#   * 205k -> 190k video. The first attempt landed at 9.97 MB: mp4 mux overhead
#     (~9 kbps) plus the encoders overshooting their targets ate the margin.
#   * alimiter after loudnorm. loudnorm could not meet TP=-1.5 with a linear
#     gain so it fell back to dynamic mode, whose limiter overshoots, and the
#     AAC encode added more on top -- the first output measured +0.76 dBTP,
#     i.e. clipping. A hard ceiling at 0.8 (~-1.9 dBFS) leaves the AAC encoder
#     room to overshoot and still stay under 0.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$dir = "C:\Users\VICTUS\Downloads\VelaPaw-demo-20260905"
$src = Join-Path $dir "real.mp4"
$out = Join-Path $dir "real_10mb.mp4"
$sp  = "C:\Users\VICTUS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9\scratchpad"
$plg = Join-Path $sp "real_x264"

$vf = "hqdn3d=3:2:6:4,scale=1280:-2:flags=lanczos"
$af = "pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0+0.5*c1," +
      "highpass=f=70," +
      "acompressor=threshold=-22dB:ratio=3:attack=15:release=250," +
      "loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=8:measured_I=-27.03:measured_TP=-5.31:" +
      "measured_LRA=7.80:measured_thresh=-37.76:offset=0.51:linear=true," +
      "aresample=48000," +
      "alimiter=limit=0.8:attack=5:release=50:level=false"

Write-Host ">>> pass 2/2 @ 190k + true-peak limiter"
& ffmpeg -y -hide_banner -loglevel error -stats -i $src `
    -vf $vf -c:v libx264 -preset slower -b:v 190k `
    -pass 2 -passlogfile $plg -pix_fmt yuv420p -profile:v high `
    -af $af -c:a aac -b:a 64k -ac 1 -ar 48000 `
    -movflags +faststart $out
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "pass 2 failed ($LASTEXITCODE)" }

Write-Host ""
Write-Host (">>> {0} MB" -f [math]::Round((Get-Item -LiteralPath $out).Length / 1MB, 2))
& ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration,size,bit_rate `

    -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 -- $out

& ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i $out -vn `
    -af "loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=8:print_format=json" -f null - 2>&1 |
    Select-String 'input_i|input_tp|input_lra'

Done — `real_10mb.mp4` in the same folder.

| | source | output |
|---|---|---|
| size | 483.35 MB | **9.45 MB** |
| video | 2560×1440@30, 13.4 Mbps | 1280×720@30, 192 kbps |
| audio | AAC 44.1k stereo, 192 kbps | AAC 48k mono, 64 kbps |
| integrated loudness | −16.35 LUFS | −16.20 LUFS |
| loudness range | **14.5 LU** | **5.1 LU** |
| true peak | −0.80 dBTP | −0.71 dBTP |
| duration | 4:58.6 | 4:58.7 (unchanged) |

**Audio balance:** LRA 14.5 → 5.1 is the actual change you asked for — the quiet narration stretches now sit close to the loud ones instead of ~15 dB below. Chain was mono downmix → 70 Hz highpass → 3:1 compression at −22 dB → two-pass `loudnorm` to −16 LUFS → true-peak limiter.

Two corrections I made mid-way:
- First encode landed at **9.97 MB** — technically under 10 but with no margin, so I dropped video 205k → 190k.
- First encode also measured **+0.76 dBTP**, i.e. actually clipping: `loudnorm` couldn't hit its true-peak target with a linear gain and fell back to dynamic mode, whose limiter overshoots, and AAC added more on top. Added an explicit `alimiter` ceiling; it now sits at −0.71 dBTP.

**Video:** checked frames before and after. The close-up LCD shots — the ones that carry the demo — are fully legible at 720p (`My Pets`, "08:00 ✔ ate 09:07 15g", "BCS: Over ➤ consider a vet check" all read clean), so I didn't need to drop to 540p. `hqdn3d` runs before the downscale so the phone's sensor noise doesn't eat bits the text needs. The wide panning shot at ~1:00 is soft, but it's soft in the source too — motion blur, not the encode. Burned-in bilingual subtitles are crisp throughout. No letterboxing to crop.

Original `real.mp4` left untouched.

One thing worth flagging: the repo still carries the old **55.8 MB `VelaPaw_Demo.mp4`** at its root — well past GitHub's 50 MB warning threshold. Say the word if you want this one swapped in for it.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   Three sequential asks in this window, all for the VelaPaw contest entry (team `contest2026_043_CircuitForge`, "AI 硬件产品创新" track, openVela `ai_agent` on real ESP32-S3 hardware):

   **Task B (carried in, now COMPLETE) — repo comparison + pull.** Finish the file-by-file diff review of VM artefacts against the committed repo, then copy the verified files in. Originating asks: *"the code was already pushed to the github: https://github.com/open-vela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge so i want you to analyze and compare what has changed, just give me the analyzsis dont commit or push"* → *"so tell me what will be pushed"* → *"do that"* (approving the pull of items existing on the VM but in neither GitHub nor the local repo, so the repo can reproduce the flashed firmware).

   **Task C (COMPLETE) — video shrink.** *"There is a video in the folder called real make that video have a balanced audio and reduce it to 10MB per github rule"* — `real.mp4` in `C:\Users\VICTUS\Downloads\VelaPaw-demo-20260905`.

   **Task D (IN PROGRESS) — quality checks.** *"what other quality checks can be made"* — asked immediately after I delivered the shrunk video. I have been running a battery of checks; the consolidated answer has NOT yet been given to the user.

   ### Standing constraints (still in force — preserve verbatim)

   - **Do NOT execute commands directly against the Linux VM** — print exact shell commands as text for the user to paste and report back. Windows-host actions (esptool flashing, PowerShell, COM port detection, driving the board's serial console, HTTP pulls from the VM) remain directly permitted.
   - **"check the port first"** — verify which COM port actually exists before opening one.
   - **The exact repro pattern the user insists on:** "Power up the board (or reset it if it's already on) / Press Enter 3 times to get the nsh> prompt / ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1 / ai_agent & / sleep 600 (to land at the vela> console) / ask hello / thats the pattern"
   - **"remember to press enter three times to get nsh"** / **"remember to place enter"**
   - **"use putty for next recording"** — recordings are driven through PuTTY, not a Python serial script.
   - **"make sure claude ai is still using the vpn when splitting"** — prove any split-tunnel route work does not divert Anthropic traffic out of the tunnel, BEFORE requesting elevation.
   - **The VPN must stay connected** — "i cant access this session without vpn so keep that in mind".
   - **Never route `8.8.8.8`/`8.8.4.4` outside the HotspotShield tunnel** — use AliDNS `223.5.5.5`.
   - The user **explicitly rejected a git baseline commit**; rollback is plain file copies. **Do not run `git add`/`commit`/`tag`/`push` on the contest repo unless newly asked.** Reconfirmed: "just give me the analyzsis dont commit or push".
   - Do not interpose unrequested safety scans — the user rejected a pre-export secret scan with **"no just export"**.
   - **No HTTP-server helper processes started by me** — patches delivered as self-contained paste-able commands ("No just give me the command").
   - Memory `feedback-no-stray-bash-before-vm-commands.md`: **STOP calling Bash/PowerShell as a noop/placeholder before VM-console-only commands** — recurred 15+ times.
   - Never `git checkout` `agent_loop.c` — would remove wanted `[llmdbg-loop]` instrumentation.
   - **Never enable Hyper-V / WinNAT on this machine** — breaks the VMware build VM.
   - Never enable `CONFIG_RTC` (kills USB console), `CONFIG_NETINIT_THREAD` (hangs the board), `CONFIG_DEBUG_USB_INFO` (wedges the console). Never use flash address `0x818000`.
   - Explicitly deferred: **feeder actuation** ("then about achuating the feeder will decide later") — do NOT start.
   - **Never run `make olddefconfig` in this tree.**
   - **`D:\openVela\packages\ai_agent` is materially behind the VM and must NOT be used to author patches.** The VM tree is authoritative.
   - **Never run `~/openvela/rebuild_camera_fix.sh` when the board file has local edits.**
   - **The build command is `./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4` run from `~/openvela`.**
   - **Do not record the full desktop** — capture only the demo window.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**

   - NuttX RTOS on ESP32-S3 (8 MB PSRAM, 16 MB flash), built in a VMware Linux VM (`king@king-VMware-Virtual-Platform`, `~/openvela`, VM IP `192.168.160.128`, Windows host `192.168.160.1`), flashed from Windows 11.
   - **COM8** = NuttX CDCACM runtime console (`nsh>`/`vela>`). **COM3** = Espressif USB-Serial/JTAG ROM port. Mutually exclusive.
   - `board_composite_connect(0, 0)` under `CONFIG_USBDEV_COMPOSITE` is what enumerates the CDC-ACM + CDC-NCM composite (COM8 *and* `eth0`).
   - **`XTENSA_IMEM_REGION_SIZE` real value is `0x48000`**, not the previously-documented `0x30000`. `ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS` is a `select`ed symbol so never appears in a defconfig.
   - **ffmpeg 9.0-full_build-www.gyan.dev**, gcc 16.1.0, MSYS2. Has libvmaf, ssim, psnr, xpsnr, astats, blackdetect, freezedetect, silencedetect, signalstats.
   - **ffmpeg filtergraph parsing double-unescapes**: a Windows absolute path in a filter option (e.g. `libvmaf=log_path=C:\...`) fails as `Invalid argument`; `C\:/...` also fails. **A relative path with forward slashes and no colon works.** cwd is `C:\Users\VICTUS\openVela`.
   - **Two-pass loudnorm**: `measured_*` values must come from a measurement of the *same filter chain* that will be used, not the bare input — a compressor upstream changes what loudnorm sees.
   - **loudnorm `linear=true` silently falls back to dynamic mode** when a static gain can't meet both I and TP targets; dynamic mode's limiter overshoots, and AAC encoding adds more on top → an explicit `alimiter` is required to guarantee headroom.
   - **PowerShell 5.1 `NativeCommandError`**: redirecting a native exe's stderr wraps lines in ErrorRecords and sets `$?`/exit code to failure even on exit 0. Do not treat as a real failure.
   - **`blackdetect` timestamps are relative to `-ss`** — a seek-then-detect run reports seek-relative times that must be offset to compare against a full-file run.
   - x264 `-preset veryfast` buffers frames; force-killing ffmpeg on a short capture leaves a 0-byte headerless mkv. Let `-t` expire and `WaitForExit()`.
   - **`transpose=2`** = 90° counter-clockwise.
   - **Debug silencing is implemented as `(void)0;  // DBGOFF: syslog(...)`** — grepping for `[llmdbg` counts commented-out lines; the correct test excludes lines containing `DBGOFF`.
   - Contest repo has two remotes: `fork` (github.com/KingMbewe/…) and `openvela` (github.com/open-vela/…), contest branch `dev-ai-contest-2026`.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   ### `board/esp32s3_appinit.c` — VM vs repo, +145 / −0 (purely additive; reviewed, then copied in)

   The `VELAPAW_AUTOSTART_STACK 49152` change was already in the repo (no removals). The 145 added lines are one self-contained **telnetd auto-start** block written 2026-09-01 when the CDC-ACM console was thought dead. Key characteristics:

   - **It does not run.** The call site is commented out:
     ```c
     // telnetd_autostart(); // TEMP-DISABLED 2026-09-02 for console-close(0/1/2) hang isolation test
     ```
   - Carries a hand-copied local mirror of `struct telnetd_config_s` because board code only sees `nuttx/include`, not `apps/include`:
     ```c
     struct telnetd_config_s
     {
       uint16_t d_port;
       sa_family_t d_family;
       uint8_t t_priority;
       size_t t_stacksize;
     #ifndef CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL
       main_t t_entry;
     #endif
     #ifdef CONFIG_LIBC_EXECFUNCS
       FAR const char *t_path;
     #endif
       FAR char * const *t_argv;
     };
     int telnetd_daemon(FAR const struct telnetd_config_s *config);
     int nsh_telnetmain(int argc, FAR char *argv[]);
     ```
     with a comment recording the real bug hit the first time: a field-type mismatch (`t_priority` as plain `int` instead of `uint8_t`) silently corrupted every field after it, so TCP port 23 accepted no connections.
