Here's the full battery I ran on `real_10mb.mp4` (and on `real.mp4` as the reference), plus what it turned up.

## Checks that came back clean

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Full-file decode with `-xerror` | zero errors — no truncated/corrupt frames |
| Frame parity vs source | **8958 = 8958** exactly |
| A/V start timestamps | both streams `0.000000` in both files — no sync offset |
| A/V duration drift | video 298.600 s / audio 298.701 s. The extra ~91 ms is AAC encoder priming+padding on the tail, not accumulating drift |
| Clipping (`astats`) | Peak −0.82 dB, **Abs Peak count 1**, DC offset −0.000113, **Flat factor 0.000000** (no flatlining) |
| Loudness | −16.20 LUFS / LRA 5.10 / −0.71 dBTP (source was −16.35 / **LRA 14.50** / −0.80) |
| `faststart` | `moov` at byte 36, `mdat` not in the first 64 KB → streams without a full download |
| Metadata privacy | source had `creation_time`, `Hw=1`, `te_is_reencode=1` but **no GPS or device tags**; output carries only brand + encoder strings, **no creation_time**. Clean for a public push |
| Silence detection | no silences ≥3 s at −50 dB |
| Letterbox (`cropdetect`) | none |

## Two findings

**1. The dark/frozen tail is source content, not an encode defect — and it's the most important part of the video.**

`blackdetect` on the output flagged `black_start:255.43 black_end:262.60 duration:7.17` plus eight `freezedetect` events between 250.4 s and 294.5 s. I verified against the source with a `-ss 240` seek: it reported `black_start:15.433333` with the identical `7.166667` duration → 15.433 + 240 = **255.433**, an exact match. Same for every freeze timestamp. So the encoder didn't blank anything.

What's actually there is the **PuTTY console**: the ai_agent boot log and the LLM feeding-digest reply. YAVG ≈ 16/255 because it's white text on black, and "frozen" because it's static text between scroll events. # Audio chain is unchanged from the previous build (compressor is what fixes
# the LRA 14.5 imbalance; loudnorm re-lands the level; alimiter guarantees the
# true-peak ceiling that loudnorm's dynamic-mode fallback cannot).

 120-180s  mean=88.48   250-299s  mean=92.82   <- console section

What it is 23 24 **VelaPaw is a smart pet feeder that recognizes *which* pet is at the bowl and dispenses that individual pet's scheduled meal — with every bit of AI running on the device itself. No cloud, no phone, no account.** 25 26 In a multi-pet home, a normal timed feeder can't tell the cats apart, so the greedy one eats everyone's food and portion control is impossible. VelaPaw solves this the way a human would: it *looks* at the animal, identifies it, and feeds it only its own ration, at its own mealtimes. Because the camera, the neural networks, the clock, and the dispenser are all self-contained, it keeps working with the internet down and never sends images of your home anywhere. 27 28 **Highlights** 29 30 - 🐾 **Per-pet identification** — an on-device INT8 neural network recognizes each enrolled pet by face, not by a tag or collar. 31 - 🍽️ **Recognition-gated feeding** — a pet is fed only when it is *recognized at the bowl* **and** one of *its* meals is due (and not skipped), at most once per meal per day. Each meal slot has its own **skip-meal** toggle. 32 - 🗣️ **Voice-settable schedules** — meal times can be spoken, not just tapped: a MEAL→HOUR→CONFIRM voice dialog, driven by an on-device keyword-spotting model, sets a pet's feeding schedule hands-free. There is no wake word — the dialog is started with a tap in the edit-pet screen, then answered by voice. VelaPaw has no always-listening wake-up feature, so the contest's designated wake-word requirement (§ Participation Rules) does not apply here. 33 - ⚖️ **Portion & daily-limit control** — per-pet gram portions with a hard daily cap. 34 - 🩺 **Health monitoring** — a second on-device network estimates Body Condition (under / ideal / over), and the feeding-history analytics raise a **sudden-appetite-drop alert**, an early illness sign. 35 - 🕑 **Real timekeeping** — a hardware RTC keeps schedules accurate across power loss. 36 - 🌐 **Bilingual UI** — English / 中文, with a live in-app language toggle. 37 - 💾 **Everything persists** — enrolled pets, schedules, and pet photos survive a power cut. 38 - 🖥️ **Runs as an appliance** — boots straight into a touchscreen UI; no console needed. 39 40 **Why now:** in March 2026, Xiaomi shipped the Mijia Smart Pet Feeder 2 (Visual Edition) — a mass-market feeder (¥449–549, ≈$65–80) that added a camera specifically to bring AI vision into feeding. That's independent, at-scale validation of VelaPaw's founding bet — a camera belongs at the feeder — carried one step further: from watching a bowl to knowing *whose* bowl it is, identified by face and fed entirely on-device with no app, account, or cloud. Full comparison in [§06 Market & Value](VelaPaw_Project_Intro.pdf) of the project intro. 41 42 --- 43 44 ## 2. On-device AI (the heart of the project) 45 46 Recognition is **open-set metric learning**, not a fixed classifier. The model is a generic pet feature-extractor (MobileNetV3-Small backbone + a spatial-attention *TSFM* module) that turns a camera frame into an L2-normalized 128-D **embedding**. Enrolling a pet stores the averaged embedding of a few photos; recognition is a cosine match against the enrolled pets. This is why **adding a pet needs no retraining** — enrollment is a first-class step, and recognition quality is driven by good enrollment photos rather than a frozen label set. 47 48 | | | 49 |---|---| 50 | **Identity model** | MobileNetV3-Small + TSFM attention, INT8, 128-D embedding, 128×128 input | 51 | **Body-condition model** | 3-class (under/ideal/over) INT8 CNN | 52 | **Runtime** | TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers (`apps/mlearning/tflite-micro`) | 53 | **Acceleration** | ESP-NN SIMD kernels on the Xtensa LX7 → **~1.3 s / inference** (vs ~6.75 s reference) | 54 | **Where models live** | flash-loaded at runtime (1.4 MB identity @ `0x600000`, 626 KB BCS @ `0x760000`) — too large to memory-map, so read into PSRAM on boot | 55 56 Both models were trained off-device with the pipeline in [`host/`](host/) (TensorFlow/Keras → INT8 post-training quantization → `.tflite`). 57 58 --- 59 60 ## 3. How it works — from camera to kibble 61 62 ``` 63 camera frame ──► embedding (TFLM, INT8) ──► cosine match vs enrolled pets 64 │ 65 recognized pet + score 66 │ 67 is one of THIS pet's meals due & unfed today? 68 │yes │no 69 dispense N g show "next meal 18:00" 70 (28BYJ-48 stepper, paddle rotor) 71 │ 72 log to history · update trends · BCS check 73 ``` 74 75 The gate in the middle is the whole idea: recognition alone would feed a greedy pet all day; a timer alone would feed whichever animal happened to be standing there. **Both must agree.** 76 77 **Software architecture** (clean HAL boundaries, in [`app/velapaw/`](app/velapaw/)): 78 79 - `ui/` — LVGL touchscreen UI (Enroll · Recognize · My Pets · Trends) 80 - `infer/` — inference interface + the TFLite-Micro backend + the trained models 81 - `identity/` — enrollment store, cosine matcher, per-pet flash persistence, pet photos 82 - `store/` — feeding history & behavior analytics 83 - `hal/` — camera (OV5640) and feeder (28BYJ-48 stepper) hardware abstraction 84 85 **Board support** ([`board/`](board/)) — a custom board file drives the display, the OV5640 camera via the ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM peripheral, the PCF85063 RTC over I²C, and the feeder's **28BYJ-48 stepper** through a ULN2003 driver on four GPIOs (IN1–IN3/IN4 on GPIO9/10/11/**43**). The display runs over **hardware SPI at 40 MHz with DMA**. The ES8311 audio codec's private I²S bus (GPIO12–16, not routed to any header) drives the onboard mic and speaker for the voice-settable schedules. 86 87 --- 88 89 ## 4. The on-device AI agent (the one part that needs internet) 90 91 The openVela **`ai_agent`** framework runs on the same ESP32-S3, as a layer *on top of* the finished feeder. It gives VelaPaw a second way to be useful: instead of the owner going to the screen to check on a pet, the device reads its own feeding records and speaks up when something looks wrong. 92 93 **What runs on the device** 94 95 | | | 96 |---|---| 97 | **Custom Skill** | A feeding-digest Skill at `/data/ai_agent/skills/` — it reads VelaPaw's own feeding records (written to flash by the feeder every time it dispenses) and turns them into a per-pet summary: grams, meals, and appetite measured against that pet's own baseline. | 98 | **Ask it (CLI)** | `ask how much did bob eat today` — the agent reads the live records off the device's flash and answers from them, not from a canned reply. | 99 | **Proactive push** | A heartbeat task re-reads the records on a timer and pushes a warning **only when a pet crosses a concern threshold** — a quiet device means nothing is wrong. It fires unattended, with nobody at the console. (The demo build uses a short 3-minute interval so the push can be seen firing within a demo; a shipping product would use hours.) | 100 101 **Offline vs online — where the line is** 102 103 > **The feeder itself never needs the internet.** Recognition, the meal schedule, portion and daily-limit control, body-condition scoring, the feeding history and trends, the voice dialog and the entire UI all run on the ESP32-S3 with no network of any kind. Unplug the network and VelaPaw keeps identifying pets and feeding them on schedule, exactly as before. 104 > 105 > **The agent layer is the only part that needs the internet**, because it talks to a hosted LLM over the device's USB network interface (CDC-NCM). With the network down, `ask` and the proactive push stop — and nothing else does. No feeding decision is ever made in the cloud, and no image ever leaves the device. 106 107 Full write-up — architecture, the Skill, the framework patches, and the captured proactive push: **[docs/AI_AGENT.md](docs/AI_AGENT.md)** ([中文](docs/AI_AGENT_zh.md)). 1	# VelaPaw × ai_agent — on-device agent integration
2	
3	> Track: **AI 硬件产品创新** · Team **contest2026_043_CircuitForge**
4	> This document is the 交付完整的应用场景说明 required by the track guide:
5	> user story, feature list, and which `ai_agent` capabilities were used.
6	
7	VelaPaw is an on-device multi-pet smart feeder (see the [main README](../README.md)).
8	This document covers the layer added on top of it: the openVela **`ai_agent`**
9	framework running on the same ESP32-S3, turning a feeder that *records* what
10	happened into one that **notices** and **speaks up**.
11	
12	> **Scope — this is the only part of VelaPaw that needs an internet connection.**
13	> The feeder itself is fully self-contained: recognition, meal scheduling,
14	> portion and daily-limit control, body-condition scoring, the voice dialog and
15	> the touchscreen UI all run on-device and keep working with the network down.
16	> The agent layer is **additive and optional** — it talks to a hosted LLM, so it
17	> needs connectivity, but nothing in the feeding path depends on it. Pull the
18	> network and VelaPaw still recognizes pets and feeds them correctly; it simply
19	> stops offering the digest. This is a deliberate boundary, not a limitation we
20	> ran out of time to remove: the safety-critical path stays offline.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 1. User story
25	
26	> **Mei has two cats, Jay and Bob.** VelaPaw already feeds them correctly — it
27	> recognizes each cat by face and dispenses only that cat's ration. But Mei
28	> works long days, and the thing that actually matters to her isn't the log of
29	> what was dispensed. It's the question she can't answer from a log: *is either
30	> of them off their food?*
31	>
32	> A cat that stops eating is an early illness sign, and it is easy to miss,
33	> because "Bob ate 10 g today" means nothing without knowing Bob normally eats
34	> 30 g. Mei would have to open an app, read a table, remember the baseline, and
35	> do the arithmetic — every day, for each cat.
36	>
37	> With the agent on board, she doesn't. **The feeder tells her.** Twice an hour
38	> the device re-reads its own feeding records, compares each pet against that
39	> pet's own baseline and the owner's daily limit, and stays silent unless
40	> something is actually wrong. When something is wrong, it says so in plain
41	> language, with the numbers:
42	>
43	> > **Bob** — the one to watch today. ⚠️ Only **10 g in 1 meal** (33 % of his
44	> > 30 g/day baseline). His last meal was this morning at 09:24; no feeding
45	> > since. Watch whether he comes for a second meal this evening; monitor for
46	> > lethargy or hiding; if appetite stays low into tomorrow, consider a vet check.
47	>
48	> And when she does want to ask, she can — in her own words, on the device,
49	> without an app: `ask which of my pets should I be worried about today`.
50	
51	**The problem it solves:** raw feeding telemetry is not health insight. A
52	per-pet baseline comparison is the difference between data a busy owner ignores
53	and a warning she acts on. The agent closes that gap on the device itself.
54

71	### 2.2 Custom Skill (基础要求 §2)
72	
73	**`velapaw-feeding-digest`** — installed at `/data/ai_agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md`,
74	alongside the 10 built-in skills.
75	
76	It teaches the agent VelaPaw's domain: where the feeding records live, what the
77	columns mean, and — critically — **what counts as a concern**:
78	
79	```
80	4. Flag a concern ONLY if any of these is true:
81	   - appetite below 50 percent of baseline
82	   - grams today reached the owner daily limit
83	   - body condition is not ideal
84	   - no feed event today in the log
85	5. Otherwise say the pet is on track, one sentence.
86	6. Use only numbers from those files. Never invent.
87	```
88	
89	The explicit thresholds are what make the output actionable rather than a
90	restatement of the log, and rule 6 is what keeps a language model from
91	inventing plausible-looking grams.
92	
93	**The data bridge** is a deliberate design choice: VelaPaw's C application
94	writes its feeding and body-condition history to plain Markdown at
95	`/data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` and `feed_log.md`. The agent reads them with
96	the ordinary `read_file` tool — no custom tool, no IPC, no shared memory. The
97	app and the agent stay decoupled, and the same files are human-readable when
98	debugging.

100	### 2.3 Proactive + execution scenario (基础要求 §3)
101	
102	**Type: 定时主动 (scheduled) with 阈值主动 (threshold) decision logic.**
103	
104	The `ai_agent` **heartbeat** service — not `cron` — is the proactive path. Every
105	30 minutes it feeds `/data/ai_agent/HEARTBEAT.md` to the agent as a `system`
106	message:
107	
108	```markdown
109	# Heartbeat
110	周期性检查任务（agent 定期执行）：
111	- [ ] Run the VelaPaw Feeding Digest skill.
112	If it finds a concern, notify the owner with numbers.
113	If all is on track, reply HEARTBEAT_OK only.
114	```
115	
116	Each firing is a full agentic run: the agent loads the skill, calls `read_file`
117	on the two data files, applies the threshold rules, and either pushes a warning
118	or answers `HEARTBEAT_OK`. **Silence is the normal case** — the device speaks
119	only when a threshold is crossed, which is what makes the alert worth reading.
120	
121	Captured unattended on hardware: `iters=4 tools=3`, four `read_file` calls,
122	request bodies growing 15 592 → 16 209 → 17 697 → 18 760 B as tool results
123	accumulated. Verified genuinely live, not replayed, by enrolling a new pet
124	mid-run and watching the next firing find it.
125	
126	### 2.4 Bonus: memory across sessions (进阶要求 §2)
127	
128	`session_mgr` persists every conversation to
129	`/data/ai_agent/sessions/tg_<chat_id>.jsonl` on littlefs, so context survives a
130	**power cut**, not merely a process restart — the constrained-storage case the
131	guide asks about. Chats are namespaced by `chat_id` (`console`, `heartbeat`),
132	so the CLI conversation and the proactive channel keep separate histories.
133	
134	Cross-session memory cuts both ways, and handling that is part of the work: a
135	device whose *state changes between turns* must not answer today's question
136	from yesterday's reply. See §3.3.

146	## 3. Technical implementation — which `ai_agent` capabilities were used
147	
148	| Capability | How VelaPaw uses it |
149	|---|---|
150	| **Agent loop (ReAct)** | Multi-round tool-calling; a real answer takes 2–4 iterations |
151	| **Tool system** | `read_file` / `list_dir` / `get_current_time` on the live data files |
152	| **Skills system** | One custom domain skill + the built-in set; 916 B skills summary in the system prompt |
153	| **Heartbeat service** | The proactive channel (30 min interval) |
154	| **Session manager** | Persistent per-`chat_id` history on littlefs |
155	| **Config store** | LLM backend + API key at `/data/ai_agent/config/config.json` |
156	| **Message bus** | `system:heartbeat` and `cli:console` dispatch |
157	| **`vela_tls`** | HTTPS to the LLM with connection pooling |
158	| **LLM cache** | RAM-only response cache, deliberately **bypassed** for the heartbeat chat |
159	
160	### 3.1 Making the framework run on this board
161	
162	Four fixes were needed before the agent would run at all on a 16 MB ESP32-S3:
163	
164	1. **PSRAM stack freeze.** `ask` hard-froze the whole chip: the agent loop's
165	   pthread stack landed in PSRAM (`0x3c…`), and a littlefs read disables the
166	   cache that PSRAM is reached through. Fixed with three Kconfig symbols
167	   (`XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP`, `XTENSA_IMEM_REGION_SIZE=0x48000`,
168	   `ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS`). The stock 0x18000 stack cannot boot this app, and
169	   `0x30000` — enough to stop the freeze — still left `pthread_create` returning
170	   `ENOMEM` once ai_agent's 6 pthreads shared the heap with velapaw.
171	2. **Heap walk kills the board.** `mallinfo()` as the agent task's first
172	   statement hangs holding the heap lock on a freshly-booted board. Replaced
173	   with a non-walking status report.
174	3. **IOB exhaustion.** A 15 KB request against the default IOB pool stalled with
175	   no timeout. `IOB_NBUFFERS`/`IOB_NCHAINS=64`, `THROTTLE=24`.
176	4. **LLM timeouts.** A good 62.6 s reply was being discarded by a 60 s watchdog
177	   (`AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SEC`, now 420 s; socket 480 s).
178	
179	### 3.2 Making it fast and reliable
180	
181	**Cutting 20 unused tools was the single highest-impact change.** Every
182	registered tool's JSON schema is serialized into *every* request, and a pet
183	feeder has no use for wearable sensors, a music player, Feishu documents or a
184	quickapp launcher. Measured on hardware: **9 946 B of a 19 391 B request body
185	was tool schemas**, against an IOB pool of `NBUFFERS(64) × BUFSIZE(196)` =
186	12 544 B — of which, after `THROTTLE(24)`, only ~7 840 B is usable by a sender.
187	A single request was ~2.5× the pool and could complete only by blocking and
188	draining as ACKs recycled buffers.
189	
190	**Shrinking the request is the fix; a send timeout is not** — a timeout turns
191	the load-bearing wait into a hard failure. (We tried the timeout first. It made
192	things worse, and that image is marked as a regression in our build lineage.)
193	Trimming the registry to the 16 tools this product actually needs took
194	reliability from intermittent to **8/8** and latency from **150–300 s to
195	3.6–35.6 s**.
196	
197	A related non-finding, recorded because it cost real time: the "1-in-3
198	zero-byte HTTP failure" was **not a bug** — an idle keep-alive close that
199	`vela_tls` recovers from in-band, 3/3.
200	
201	### 3.3 Making the answers *correct* — the freshness problem
202	
203	The hardest class of bug here was not a crash. It was the agent returning a
204	**confident, well-formed, wrong** answer. Three distinct defects, all found by
205	reading traces rather than trusting the prose:
206	
207	1. **Heartbeat replayed its own history.** Because sessions persist across
208	   reboot, firing *N* could answer from firing *N−1*'s text without opening a
209	   single file — `iters=1 tools=0` and a plausible digest. As a product bug: a
210	   pet fed at 14:00 still reported unfed at 14:30. Fixed by skipping history for
211	   the heartbeat chat.
212	2. **`list_dir` returned nothing, and that nothing became the answer.** The
213	   prefix was matched against the absolute path while the model passes a
214	   relative one, so every entry was filtered out; and `list_dir` sat in the
215	   "local tool shortcut" set, which ends the turn and hands raw tool output
216	   straight to the user. An owner asking which pet to worry about literally
217	   received `(no files found)`. Fixed by matching **either** path form, always
218	   recursing, and removing `list_dir` from the shortcut set. Across three
219	   hardware runs the model spelled the argument three different ways
220	   (`"velapaw"`, `"/data/ai_agent/"`, omitted) — a tool that handles only the
221	   spelling you happened to observe will look fixed and then fail.
222	3. **Stale conversation history vs. changing device state.** The console
223	   *should* keep history, so it can't simply be cleared. Instead
224	   `build_messages` now injects a mid-array `system` message ahead of the user
225	   turn stating that device state may have changed, that any figure quoted
226	   earlier is stale, and that current-state questions must be answered by
227	   re-reading the files. Trimming history was the fallback and proved
228	   unnecessary.
229	
230	Also fixed along the way: `ask` silently truncated questions at seven words
231	(`MAX_ARGS 8` in `nsh_commands.c`, raised to 32), and the agent no longer takes
232	the shortcut when tool output begins with `Error: `.
233	
234	### 3.4 Verification
235	
236	Every claim above was verified from the agent's own trace lines, not from the
237	readability of its prose. The final console run, with stale history deliberately
238	left in place:
239	
240	```
241	tools executed : 3 ['list_dir', 'read_file', 'read_file']
242	    /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md (476 B)
243	    /data/ai_agent/velapaw/feed_log.md (241 B)
244	req bytes      : 11312, 12667, 14008
245	cache replay   : no
246	END status=ok iters=3 tools=2 llm_ms=5260 elapsed=7s
247	```
248	
249	— then the correct Bob warning quoted in §1. `cache replay: no` proves the reply
250	came off the wire; the two `read_file` sizes prove the numbers came from the
251	files.
252	
253	**Two techniques worth reusing:**
254	
255	- **An `llm_cache` hit is a free byte-for-byte equality test between two runs.**
256	  The cache keys on the first 64 characters, so a hit proves two runs delivered
257	  identical content — that is what proved `ask` truncation was a fixed buffer
258	  rather than a serial-link problem.
259	- **`Skills system ready (N built-in)` is a compile-time constant** and proves
260	  nothing about whether a skill loaded. `Skills summary: NNN bytes` is the real
261	  signal.
262	
263	---

1 English | 中文 2 3 # VelaPaw — Engineering Deep-Dive 4 5 Technical notes on how VelaPaw is built: the on-device AI pipeline, the depth of 6 openVela use, the hardest problems solved, and the performance engineering. This 7 is the companion to the [README](../README.md) for readers who want the details. 8 9 --- 10 11 ## 1. System at a glance 12 13 Everything runs on a single **ESP32-S3** (Xtensa LX7, 8 MB PSRAM, 16 MB flash) 14 under **openVela / NuttX**, with an **LVGL** touchscreen UI. There is no 15 companion phone, no cloud, and no network dependency — capture, inference, 16 scheduling, timekeeping and dispensing are all local. 17 18 **Flash layout (16 MB)** 19 20 | Offset | Contents | Size | Note | 21 |---|---|---|---| 22 | `0x000000` | Firmware (`nuttx.bin`) | ~750 KB | openVela + app + LVGL | 23 | `0x600000` | Identity model (`velapaw.tflite`) | 1.44 MB | flash-loaded to PSRAM at boot | 24 | `0x760000` | Body-condition model (`bcs.tflite`) | 626 KB | flash-loaded to PSRAM at boot | 25 | `0x800000` | Enrolled pets (magic `VPAW`) | 8 KB | names, schedules, face embeddings | 26 | `0x810000` | Pet photos (magic `VICN`) | 32 KB | card thumbnails | 27 28 The two neural networks are **too large to memory-map** — the DROM0 MMU window 29 saturates well before a 1.4 MB `const` array maps — so they are flashed as raw 30 blobs and read into PSRAM buffers at boot via the NuttX software `spi_flash_read` 31 path. Because flash reads suspend the CPU cache, that read runs on a short-lived 32 thread whose stack is a `.bss` (internal-SRAM) buffer. 33 34 --- 35 36 ## 2. The recognition pipeline 37 38 ``` 39 camera frame ─► embed (TFLM INT8, background worker) ─► cosine match vs enrolled 40 │ 41 pet id + score + margin 42 │ 43 schedule gate: is a meal of THIS pet 44 due today and not yet eaten? 45 │yes │no 46 dispense N g show next meal 47 │ 48 log history · trends · body-condition 49 ``` 50 51 **Open-set, not closed-set.** Recognition is metric learning, not an N-way 52 classifier: the model maps a 128×128 frame to an L2-normalized 128-D embedding, 53 enrollment stores the averaged embedding of a few photos, and matching is cosine 54 similarity against the enrolled set. The practical payoff is that **adding a pet 55 requires no retraining** — enrollment is a runtime operation, and the accepted/ 56 rejected decision is a tunable threshold. (A consequence worth knowing: rejecting 57 arbitrary non-pet objects is inherently hard for a generic feature extractor, so 58 enrollment quality — tight, well-lit face shots — is the dominant lever on 59 false-accepts.) 60 61 **Inference is off the UI thread.** The ~1.3 s `Invoke()` runs on a dedicated 62 worker thread; the LVGL loop hands it a frame and keeps rendering, so touch and 63 the camera preview stay live during inference. Recognition is also **on-demand** 64 (it runs when a pet is at the bowl, not continuously) to bound the workload. 65 66 --- 67 68 ## 3. Depth of openVela use 69 70 VelaPaw is not a thin app on top of a BSP — it exercises openVela across the 71 stack: 72 73 - **`apps/mlearning/tflite-micro`** is the AI runtime. The app links it directly 74 (`backend_tflm.cc`) and runs two independent `MicroInterpreter`s (identity + 75 body-condition) with PSRAM tensor arenas. 76 - **LVGL** (openVela graphics) drives the four-tab touch UI. 77 - **Custom board bring-up** (`board/esp32s3_st7789.c`) drives, from scratch on 78 the ESP32-S3 peripherals: 79 - the **ST7796 display** over hardware SPI2 + GDMA; 80 - the **OV5640 camera** via the **LCD_CAM** peripheral with a GDMA receive 81 channel (configured over SCCB/I²C) — run out on a **30 cm FFC + coupler** so 82 the camera mounts independently of the board (see [`hardware/README.md`](../hardware/README.md)); 83 - the **PCF85063 RTC** over I²C (raw register access — no `CONFIG_RTC`, which 84 keeps the USB-CDC console alive); 85 - the **28BYJ-48 stepper feeder** through a **ULN2003** driver on four GPIOs 86 (IN1–IN3/IN4 on GPIO9/10/11/**43** — 43 is U0TXD, free because the console 87 is on the USB-Serial/JTAG port; GPIO12/13/15 are the ES8311 codec's private 88 I²S bus, used instead for the voice-settable schedules), stepped in software 89 through the coil sequence. 90 - **Auto-start** (`board/esp32s3_appinit.c`) launches the app from 91 `board_app_initialize()` — NSH calls it via `boardctl(BOARDIOC_INIT)` after 92 `esp32s3_bringup()` has registered the LCD/touch/camera — so the device boots 93 straight into its UI while keeping the shell available for debugging. 94 95 --- 96 97 ## 4. The hardest problem: hardware-SPI display 98 99 This is the standout piece of hardware debugging in the project. 100 101 **Symptom.** Over hardware SPI, a *full-screen* write rendered, but *any partial 102 window* (`CASET`/`RASET` to a sub-rectangle + `RAMWR`) never appeared — while the 103 identical byte sequence over a bit-banged GPIO path worked perfectly. It survived 104 ~60 build cycles of software and config changes (framebuffer mirroring, DMA on/ 105 off, software CS, PSRAM-coherency fixes, pin-routing forcing). 106 107 **Method — measure, don't guess.** With a logic analyzer (sigrok/PulseView on an 108 FX2 clone), the SPI pins can't be probed directly — they're not on the header — 109 so the board firmware **mirrors** `FSPID_OUT`/`FSPICLK_OUT` onto spare header 110 GPIOs via the GPIO matrix, plus a trigger marker. A decisive first step was a 111 **ground-truth test**: drive four known square waves on the probe pins and refuse 112 to trust any capture until they read clean. That immediately exposed a wiring/ 113 grounding problem that had been producing garbage — and only *then* did the real 114 capture become trustworthy. 115 116 **Finding.** The decoded capture showed the ESP32 emitting a **byte-perfect** 117 `CASET 00 28 00 8B / RASET 00 28 00 8B / RAMWR / pixels` stream — correct 118 commands, correct DC alignment, exactly 8 clean clock edges per byte, zero 119 glitches. The peripheral was innocent all along. 120 121 **Root cause.** The panel's **chip-select is hardwired low**, so it can never 122 re-synchronize its bit counter on a CS edge — it counts clock edges forever. The 123 firmware bit-banged the panel init and *then* handed the pads to the SPI 124 peripheral; that pad handover glitches the clock by a single edge, and from that 125 instant the panel is off by one bit. Every subsequent command decodes as garbage, 126 `RAMWR` is never recognized, no pixels reach GRAM, and the screen simply keeps 127 showing whatever bit-bang last painted — which looked exactly like "hardware SPI 128 renders nothing." 129 130 **Fix.** Give the pads to the SPI peripheral **first**, then **hardware-reset the 131 panel** (a software reset can't work — it would itself be misread), then run the 132 entire init over SPI. Once the panel is re-synced under SPI ownership, partial 133 windows render correctly. 134 135 **Payoff.** With the path proven, the display was moved off bit-banging entirely 136 and onto hardware SPI (see §5). A bug that looked like a dead end became a 137 performance win. 138 139 --- 140 141 ## 5. Performance engineering 142 143 **ESP-NN on the LX7 (≈5× inference speed-up).** The identity model is mostly 144 depthwise convolution, which runs slowly on the TFLite-Micro *reference* kernels 145 (~6.75 s / inference). Wiring in the **ESP-NN** SIMD kernels for the Xtensa LX7 146 brings it to **~1.3 s**. The subtle part was that the ESP-NN kernel set has to be 147 dropped into the tflite-micro kernel directory and the matching *reference* 148 kernels filtered out to avoid duplicate symbols; and a class of "crash on first 149 conv" turned out to be **stale incremental builds**, not a kernel bug — a clean 150 build runs stably. 151 152 **Hardware SPI + DMA display (≈4× UI repaint speed-up).** Once the SPI path was 153 correct (§4), the display went from bit-banging every pixel (CPU toggling GPIOs) 154 to the hardware SPI2 peripheral at **40 MHz with GDMA**. A full 480×320 repaint 155 dropped from **~246 ms to ~61 ms**. Two details mattered: pixel rows are bounced 156 through an internal-SRAM buffer because SPI DMA can't read PSRAM cache-coherently, 157 and the address-window setup was batched from 11 SPI calls down to 5 (LVGL sets a 158 window on every `putarea`). 159 160 --- 161 162 ## 6. Build & reproducibility notes 163 164 A few non-obvious constraints, recorded so the build is reproducible: 165 166 - **App/library define parity.** The app and the prebuilt `tflite-micro` library 167 share headers, so header-visible defines must match exactly. In particular 168 `TF_LITE_STATIC_MEMORY` changes the layout of `TfLiteTensor` — defining it on 169 only one side lets `AllocateTensors` pass but makes the first `Invoke` write 170 through a mis-offset pointer and wedge the SoC. The Makefile mirrors the 171 library's define set exactly. 172 - **`-fno-threadsafe-statics`** is required on the C++ flags: without it the first 173 function-local static in TFLM init deadlocks in `__cxa_guard_acquire` on this 174 libsupc++ build (a silent hang, not a crash). 175 - **Config changes re-clone esp-hal**, which reverts a spinlock initializer patch; 176 the first build after any defconfig change may need the patch re-applied. 177 178 ### ESP-NN acceleration — a public-repo change, provided as a fork/PR 179 180 The ~1.3 s inference figure requires the **ESP-NN** SIMD kernels, and that 181 integration modifies a **public** openVela repo (`apps/mlearning/tflite-micro`). 182 Per the contest rules — *public-repo changes are submitted as a fork-and-PR to 183 `dev-ai-contest-2026`, not committed into the team repo* — the ESP-NN work is 184 delivered as a fork/PR rather than vendored here. **Out of the box, this team 185 repo builds and runs with the reference kernels (~6.75 s); applying the ESP-NN 186 fork brings it to ~1.3 s.** 187 188 The integration consists of three parts: 189 190 1. **The esp-nn library** (Espressif's Apache-2.0 SIMD kernels for the Xtensa 191 LX7) added at `apps/mlearning/esp-nn/`. 192 2. **Kernel wrappers** (`conv`, `depthwise_conv`, `fully_connected`, `pooling`, 193 `add`, `mul`, `softmax`) dropped into 194 `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/tflite-micro/tensorflow/lite/micro/kernels/esp_nn/`. 195 3. **A Makefile block** in `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/Makefile` that compiles 196 the esp-nn sources with `-DESP_NN=1 -DCONFIG_NN_OPTIMIZED -mlongcalls`, adds 197 its include dirs, and **filters out the matching reference kernels** so there 198 are no duplicate symbols. 199 200 The exact wrappers, the Makefile block, and a step-by-step reproduction recipe 201 are provided as reference material in [`docs/esp-nn/`](esp-nn/). 202 203 > **PR:** _``_ 204 205 Two gotchas found during the integration: the esp-nn assembly sources 206 (`*esp32s3.c`) are excluded (the opt-C path is used); and an early "crash on the 207 first conv" was traced to **stale incremental builds**, not a kernel fault — a 208 clean rebuild runs stably. 209 210 --- 211 212 ## 7. Off-device: model training 213 214 The two INT8 models are trained off-device with the pipeline in [`host/`](../host/) 215 (TensorFlow/Keras). The identity model is a MobileNetV3-Small backbone with a 216 spatial-attention **TSFM** module and an ArcFace metric-learning head; it is 217 exported via INT8 post-training quantization to a `.tflite` whose ops are all 218 TFLM builtins. The body-condition model is a compact 3-class CNN trained the same 219 way. See [`docs/BENCHMARK_AB.md`](BENCHMARK_AB.md) for the fast-vs-accurate model 220 comparison. 221 222 --- 223 224 *This document reflects the engineering as built and verified on real ESP32-S3 225 hardware.* 226

1	# `agent/` — VelaPaw's `ai_agent` layer
2	
3	Everything VelaPaw adds on top of the stock openVela `ai_agent` framework.
4	The narrative write-up is in **[../docs/AI_AGENT.md](../docs/AI_AGENT.md)**
5	([中文](../docs/AI_AGENT_zh.md)); this file is the operational index.
6	
7	```
8	agent/
9	├── skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md   the custom Skill
10	├── HEARTBEAT.md                       the proactive task list
11	└── patches/                           changes to packages/ai_agent
12	```
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Board assets (`skills/`, `HEARTBEAT.md`)
17	
18	These two files are **runtime data on the board's littlefs**, not source that
19	the build consumes. At runtime they live at:
20	
21	| Repo file | Board path |
22	|---|---|
23	| `skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md` | `/data/ai_agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md` |
24	| `HEARTBEAT.md` | `/data/ai_agent/HEARTBEAT.md` |
25	
26	> **They are not installed by the build or by the manifest linkfile.** The
27	> linkfile only makes them visible inside the openVela tree. Provisioning is a
28	> separate step — they must be written to `/data` once per board, over the NSH
29	> console or by mounting the littlefs image. They then persist across reboots
30	> and across firmware reflashes, because `write-flash 0x0 nuttx.bin` writes
31	> 0x0–~0x17ec80 and the `/data` partition starts at **0x180000**.
32	
33	Two gotchas if you provision over the console: NSH truncates an input line at
34	~80 characters (`CONFIG_NSH_LINELEN`), so long `echo … >> /long/path` commands
35	are silently cut mid-string and leave a corrupt file; and verify by comparing
36	`ls -l`'s byte count against what you intended, not by reading the console echo
37	— the echo shows the *command*, not the file.
38	
39	## 2. Framework patches (`patches/`)
40	
41	Against `packages/ai_agent` at commit **`41723c6`**. The three patches touch
42	**disjoint file sets**, so each applies independently and in any order.
43	
44	| Patch | Files | What it fixes |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| `0001-platform-bringup.patch` | 6 | Makes the agent run at all on a 16 MB ESP32-S3: PSRAM-stack freeze, the heap walk that kills a freshly-booted board, LLM/socket timeouts (420 s / 480 s), task stacks |
47	| `0002-request-size-and-transport.patch` | 4 | Makes it fast and reliable: excludes 20 tools irrelevant to a feeder (schemas were 9 946 B of a 19 391 B request, against a ~7 840 B usable IOB budget), plus HTTP retry and transport handling |
48	| `0003-agent-correctness.patch` | 8 | Makes the answers *right*: heartbeat session replay, the `list_dir` prefix and local-tool-shortcut defects, the stale-history freshness directive, `ask` truncating at 7 words, and the natural-language fast paths left dispatching to tools `0002` removed |
49	
50	Applying them:
51	
52	```bash
53	cd <openvela-workspace>/packages/ai_agent
54	git apply --check ../../contest2026_043_CircuitForge/agent/patches/*.patch  # dry run
55	git apply         ../../contest2026_043_CircuitForge/agent/patches/*.patch
56	```
57	
58	Then force a rebuild of the C files — **header-only edits do not recompile
59	dependents in this tree**, which will silently give you a stale image:
60	
61	```bash
62	find packages/ai_agent/src -name '*.c' -exec touch {} +
63	./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4
64	```
65	
66	`0001` also depends on three Kconfig symbols that are **not** in these patches
67	because they belong to the board config, not the framework — they are in
68	[`../board/configs/`](../board/configs/):
69	`XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP`, `XTENSA_IMEM_REGION_SIZE=0x48000`, and the
70	easily-missed `ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS`. Without all three the agent task's stack
71	lands in PSRAM and the first `ask` freezes the whole chip.
72	
73	`0x30000` was the value that first stopped the freeze, but it is **not** enough
74	for the shipped build: every task and pthread stack is carved from this heap,
75	and with `ai_agent`'s task plus its 6 pthreads alongside velapaw's 48 KB stack
76	`pthread_create` came back `ENOMEM`. The flashed firmware uses `0x48000` — the
77	value in `board/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig`. `ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS` is a
78	`select`ed symbol, so it never appears in a defconfig; check it in `.config`.
79	
80	## 3. Verifying a build really has the changes
81	
82	This board has burned us twice with silently stale builds, so verify rather
83	than assume:
84	
85	```bash
86	grep AI_AGENT nuttx/.config
87	strings nuttx/nuttx.bin | grep -i ai_agent
88	md5sum nuttx/nuttx.bin        # image size is NOT a usable identifier
89	```
90	
91	At runtime, on the console:
92	
93	- `[tools] Tools JSON built (16 builtin + 0 providers)` — the tool cut is in.
94	
95	If you ever change the `s_excluded_tools[]` denylist in `0002`, re-run this
96	grep and require it to come back **empty** — cutting a tool leaves callers
97	behind, and `handle_nl_fast_path()` runs *before* the LLM, so a shortcut
98	pointing at an unregistered tool returns its result to the user as the final
99	answer:
100	
101	```bash
102	grep -n 'get_heartrate\|get_steps\|get_wear_state\|vibrate\|music_\|feishu_\|quickapp' \
103	  packages/ai_agent/src/core/agent_loop.c
104	```
105	- `[skills] Skills summary: NNN bytes` — the real signal that skills loaded.
106	  **`Skills system ready (N built-in)` is a compile-time constant and proves
107	  nothing.**
108	- `END status=ok iters=N tools=M` — read this, not the prose. An answer that
109	  reads perfectly with `iters=1 tools=0` was replayed from history, not derived
110	  from the data files.
111

1	# TFLite-Micro Latency/Integration Spike — Report
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-06-27
4	**Goal:** De-risk on-device AI for VelaPaw — confirm TFLite-Micro integrates and runs on openVela, and measure the tensor-arena footprint, op coverage, and compute profile of a MobileNet-class INT8 CNN.
5	**Model:** `person_detect.tflite` (bundled in tflite-micro) — INT8 MobileNet-v1-0.25, 96×96×1 grayscale, ~294 KB. A close compute proxy for VelaPaw's "fast" embedding backbone (MobileNetV3-Small @ 96×96).
6	**Vehicle:** the in-tree `tflm_benchmark` tool (`CONFIG_TFLITEMICRO_BENCHMARK_TOOL`), run on the goldfish ARM emulator.
7	
8	> **Critical caveat on latency:** the emulator is QEMU emulating **ARM cortex-a15** on an x86 host — NOT the ESP32-S3's **Xtensa LX7**. Absolute milliseconds here are **not** a hardware estimate. What *is* portable and trustworthy: (1) integration works, (2) arena footprint, (3) op coverage, (4) the relative compute breakdown across layer types.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Results
13	
14	### ✅ Integration — works
15	TFLite-Micro builds for openVela (ARM cross), links into the image, and runs a full INT8 inference to completion. Output `CRC32: 0x24B4C645` (deterministic, model executed correctly). `nuttx.bin` grew 1.88 MB → 2.70 MB with TFLM + deps linked in.
16	
17	### ✅ Tensor arena — ~82 KB (the key portable number)
18	```
19	[[ Arena ]]      Bytes    % Arena
20	Total           84,420    100.0
21	NonPersistent   55,296     65.5
22	Persistent      29,124     34.5
23	```
24	- Configured arena 204,800 B; **actual used 84,420 B (~82 KB)**.
25	- On the ESP32-S3-EYE (8 MB PSRAM) this is **negligible** — arena sizing is a non-issue for VelaPaw. Even several models loaded at once fit easily.
26	
27	### ✅ Operator coverage — all supported by the default resolver
28	`CONV_2D`, `DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D`, `AVERAGE_POOL_2D`, `RESHAPE`, `SOFTMAX` — all ran with the stock op resolver. (VelaPaw's MobileNetV3-Small adds SE blocks / hard-swish → will also need `MUL`, `ADD`, `LOGISTIC`/`HARD_SWISH`; verify those when the real model is exported.)
29	
30	### Compute profile (one inference) — CONV dominates
31	```
32	Layer type          ticks      share
33	CONV_2D            643,819     ~84%
34	DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D  122,680     ~16%
35	AVERAGE_POOL_2D        439     ~0%
36	SOFTMAX              1,048     ~0%
37	RESHAPE                119     ~0%
38	TOTAL              768,105
39	AllocateTensors     24,860   (one-time)
40	```
41	**Takeaway:** ~84% of inference time is standard `CONV_2D`. Latency on real hardware is therefore almost entirely a function of how fast INT8 convolutions run.
42	
43	### ⚠️ Latency (emulated only — do not quote as S3)
44	~768,105 profiler ticks ≈ **~0.77 s** of emulated cortex-a15 time for one inference. This reflects QEMU emulation, not silicon, and uses TFLM **reference** kernels (no LX7/NEON acceleration in this path). Treat only as an upper-bound sanity check that the pipeline runs.
45	
46	---
47	
48	## What this means for VelaPaw (and the plan's Risk #1)
49	
50	The plan's biggest risk was "INT8 fine-grained ID may miss the <300 ms target on the S3 LX7." This spike sharpens that:
51	
52	- **Arena/memory: solved** — ~82 KB, trivial on 8 MB PSRAM.
53	- **Op coverage: green** for a MobileNet core; recheck SE/hard-swish ops for MobileNetV3.
54	- **Latency: still the open risk, and it hinges on conv kernels.** Since CONV_2D is ~84% of the work, hitting <300 ms on the S3 depends almost entirely on **optimized INT8 convolution kernels (ESP-NN)**. In Phase 0 we found **no ESP-NN** in the tree (only `cmsis-nn` = ARM, `nnlib-hifi4` = HiFi DSP — neither targets the S3's LX7). With reference kernels, real-hardware latency will be far above target.
55	
56	**Decision implied:** before committing to MobileNetV3+TSFM at 96×96, the next hardware step (Phase 5, or a quick ESP32-S3 bring-up) must establish whether ESP-NN can be added to this TFLM build. If not, the mitigations from the plan move up: smaller input (e.g. 64×64), shrink the backbone/embedding head, widen the presence-gate interval. The emulator cannot answer the absolute-latency question — only the arena, op, and profile questions, which it now has.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Build integration notes (Windows)
61	
62	Getting the in-tree benchmark tool to build on native Windows needed three fixes (TFLM library itself built cleanly; all issues were in the benchmark/codegen tooling). Documented for reproducibility:
63	
64	1. **Benchmark CMakeLists was a standalone `project(tflm_benchmarking CXX)`** → re-ran compiler detection (defaulted to `nmake`, no host compiler) and aborted the subdir before the app registered. Neutralized `cmake_minimum_required`/`project()` so it inherits the parent cross-toolchain.
65	   File: `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/tflite-micro/tensorflow/lite/micro/tools/benchmarking/CMakeLists.txt`
66	2. **Meta-data banner** (`collect_meta_data.sh`) ran under cmd.exe and then tried to `pip install tensorflow`. Bypassed entirely via `-DGENERIC_BENCHMARK_NO_META_DATA` and dropping `show_meta_data.cc` from sources (same file).
67	3. **`generate_cc_arrays.py` built the C identifier from the full Windows path** (`g_D:\openVela\...`) — used `abs_fname.split('/')` which doesn't split Windows backslashes. Fixed `get_array_name()` to use `os.path.basename` + `os.path.splitext`.
68	   File: `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/tflite-micro/tensorflow/lite/micro/tools/generate_cc_arrays.py`
69	
70	### Reproduce
71	```bash
72	source /d/openVela/vela-env.sh
73	cd /d/openVela/nuttx
74	# enable (deps auto-resolve via olddefconfig):
75	kconfig-tweak --file build/.config -e SYSTEM_FLATBUFFERS -e MATH_GEMMLOWP -e MATH_KISSFFT \
76	  -e MATH_RUY -e TFLITEMICRO -e TFLITEMICRO_BENCHMARK_TOOL
77	kconfig-tweak --file build/.config --set-str BENCHMARK_MODEL_PATH \
78	  "D:/openVela/apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/tflite-micro/tensorflow/lite/micro/models/person_detect.tflite"
79	kconfig-tweak --file build/.config --set-val BENCHMARK_TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE 204800
80	vela_olddefconfig
81	cmake -B build -DBOARD_CONFIG="$VELA_BOARD_CONFIG" -GNinja
82	cmake --build build -j8
83	# run (sends the command to NSH via stdin, headless):
84	cd /d/openVela && export HOST_OS=windows HOST_ARCH=x86_64
85	(sleep 22; printf 'tflm_benchmark\n'; sleep 120) | ./emulator.sh nuttx/build -no-window
86	```
87	
88	---
89	
90	## Status
91	
92	Spike complete. Integration + memory + op-coverage + compute-profile de-risked. The one question the emulator structurally cannot answer — absolute LX7 latency — is now clearly scoped and tied to ESP-NN availability, to be resolved at hardware bring-up.
93

1	# VelaPaw — feeder hardware
2	
3	Gravity hopper → **paddle rotor** → chute → bowl, driven by a **28BYJ-48 stepper** (via a ULN2003 board), with **IN4 on GPIO43**.
4	
5	## Why a rotor and not a flap
6	
7	A flap's dose depends on how long it stays open **and** how full the hopper is — the same 800 ms drops noticeably more food when the hopper is heavy. A rotor pocket holds a fixed volume, so the dose depends only on how many pockets you index. Since the product claim is *per-pet portion control*, a mechanism that drifts as the hopper empties would quietly undermine it.
8	
9	The rotor is driven by a **28BYJ-48 stepper** (via a ULN2003 board), which rotates **continuously in one direction** — so pockets ratchet inlet→outlet and per-pocket dosing is exact:
10	
11	```
12	grams = pockets × GRAMS_PER_POCKET
13	```
14	
15	> **Why a stepper, not a servo.** An MG90S servo can only *oscillate*, and with the inlet and outlet 180° apart a zero-net-rotation wobble can never carry a pocket across — it dispenses the initial charge then dead-heads. The stepper's continuous spin is what makes the rotary valve actually work, and it makes the portion-control claim literally true. (The geared 28BYJ-48 also has strong low-speed torque, which resists kibble jams.)
16	
17	## Bill of materials
18	
19	| Item | Notes |
20	|---|---|
21	| **28BYJ-48 stepper + ULN2003 driver** (5 V bundle) | The **5 V** version — runs off the same 5 V supply below. Get the motor+driver bundle. |
22	| **5 V supply, ≥2 A** | Powers the ULN2003/motor. Common **ground** with the ESP32; never tie the 5 V rails together. |
23	| Female–female jumpers | 4 signal lines (IN1–IN4) + 5 V + GND to the ULN2003. |
24	| PLA / PETG (or JLC nylon) | PLA is fine for dry kibble; PETG/nylon if you want to wash the parts. |
25	
26	The **ULN2003 board is the driver** — no separate PWM chip; the ESP32-S3 just toggles 4 GPIOs through the half-step sequence. (No servo → the 470 µF servo-inrush cap is no longer needed.)
27	
28	## Wiring
29	
30	```
31	  ESP32-S3 (3.3 V logic)            ULN2003 driver board          28BYJ-48
32	    GPIO9  ─────────────────────────> IN1
33	    GPIO10 ─────────────────────────> IN2                         (5-pin
34	    GPIO11 ─────────────────────────> IN3            motor  ────►  connector)
35	    GPIO43 ─────────────────────────> IN4
36	                                      +   ◄── 5 V PSU +
37	                                      −   ◄──┬─ 5 V PSU −
38	  board GND ───────────────────────────────┘   ← COMMON GROUND, mandatory
39	```
40	
41	- **IN1–IN3 = GPIO9/10/11** (header J8 pins 14/12/10), shared with the unused microSD slot (its CS is on expander EXIO3 and stays deasserted, so it's safe to drive). **Never put these on GPIO12/13/14/15/16** — those are the ES8311 audio codec's private I²S bus, not routed to any header at all, and VelaPaw now uses them for voice-settable meal schedules (onboard mic + speaker). Putting the stepper there would silently short-circuit the coil drive against the audio path — this used to be write-up guidance from before audio bring-up and is now out of date.
42	- **IN4 = GPIO43** (U0TXD). This works because the console runs on the **USB-Serial/JTAG** port, not UART0, so U0TXD is free to drive. **Use GPIO43, not GPIO44** — GPIO44 (U0RXD) is clamped and the coil won't drive cleanly (this was the cause of the early "stepper buzzes but won't turn" during bring-up; it was the pin, not the coil order).
43	- Change any of these in the board file (`STEP_IN1..4`) if you ever need UART0.
44	- **Power the ULN2003 from the separate 5 V supply, not the board**, and share **ground only**. The 28BYJ-48 draws ~240 mA/phase — fine for a 2 A supply.
45	- The ULN2003's on-board LEDs show the coil sequence — handy for confirming it's stepping.
46	
47	## Printing
48	
49	All parts print without supports. PLA/PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 3 perimeters.
50	
51	```bash
52	openscad -D 'part="rotor"'         -o rotor.stl         velapaw_feeder.scad
53	openscad -D 'part="housing"'       -o housing.stl       velapaw_feeder.scad
54	openscad -D 'part="plate_stepper"' -o plate_stepper.stl velapaw_feeder.scad   # drive end (28BYJ-48)
55	openscad -D 'part="plate_idle"'    -o plate_idle.stl    velapaw_feeder.scad
56	openscad -D 'part="hopper"'        -o hopper.stl        velapaw_feeder.scad
57	openscad -D 'part="cam_pod"'       -o cam_pod.stl       velapaw_feeder.scad   # relocated OV5640 enclosure
58	openscad -D 'part="cam_mast"'      -o cam_mast.stl      velapaw_feeder.scad   # drum-front camera yoke
59	```
60	
61	`plate_servo` still exists as legacy reference but is **not** printed — the drive
62	end is the stepper (`plate_stepper`). The pre-batched print/order set for the
63	structural parts (base, pedestal, chute, cradle, cam pod + mast) lives in
64	[`stl_jlcpcb/`](stl_jlcpcb/) with an [`ORDER.md`](stl_jlcpcb/ORDER.md).
65	
66	Open the file with no `-D` (`part="product"`) to preview the whole assembly.
67	
68	## Board cradle (mounting the ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C)
69	
70	`board_cradle` holds the Waveshare board so the **screen faces the owner** (the
71	board is now un-rotated — the front-eye layout). The board drops into the tray and
72	is fixed with four **M2.00** self-tapping screws through its corner mounting holes,
73	cutting into the posts' printed pilot holes; the bottom GPIO header (and the
74	stepper **IN4 wire on GPIO43**) exits through the header slot.
75	
76	The OV5640 **no longer looks down through a window in the cradle** — it has been
77	**decoupled from the board and relocated** (see *Camera relocation* below), so the
78	screen can face the owner while the camera watches the bowl from its own mount.
79	
80	Dimensions are taken from the Waveshare -C outline drawing (95.11 × 63.67 × 14.1 mm,
81	corner R7.3, mounting holes 72.00 × 48.50 mm apart, camera centred). `BM_SCREW_D`
82	(a 1.7 mm self-tap pilot bore for **M2.00** screws — the bare-board drawing labels
83	the mounting holes M2.00, not M2.5 as earlier assumed) is confirmed from the
84	drawing. **One value is still not on the drawing and remains assumed — verify on
85	the real board before printing:** `BM_CAM_WIN` (camera lens-barrel diameter,
86	assumed Ø14). Both constants are near the bottom of the `.scad`.
87	
88	> ### Stepper mechanical parts — done (verify two dimensions)
89	> The drive end is now built for the **28BYJ-48**: print **`plate_stepper`** (its
90	> Ø28 body clears the central bore; it bolts on through the two 35 mm flange
91	> holes) — *not* `plate_servo`, which is kept only as legacy reference. The
92	> **rotor** now has a **5 mm double-D socket** in its driven face that presses
93	> straight onto the stepper shaft (no horn/spline). Body Ø is confirmed 28 mm;
94	> two values are nominal — **caliper before printing** and adjust at the top of
95	> the `.scad`: `STEP_SHAFT_FLAT` (shaft width across the flats) and
96	> `STEP_SHAFT_LEN` (shaft length). `housing`, `plate_idle`, `hopper` and
97	> `board_cradle` are unchanged.
98	
99	## Camera relocation (OV5640 on a 30 cm FFC)
100	
101	The OV5640 plugs into the board's 24-pin 0.5 mm DVP connector (schematic **J2**,
102	"0.5-24pin-cam"). Unplugging it and running a **30 cm FFC + a 1:1 coupler** lets
103	the camera live on its own mount instead of riding the board, so the screen can
104	face the owner while the lens watches the bowl. The camera sits in **`cam_pod`**
105	(open-back OV5640 enclosure) carried by **`cam_mast`** — a two-leg yoke that
106	straddles the chute and holds the pod just in front of the drum, aimed steeply
107	down-and-forward at the pet (the sightline passes *under* the owner-facing
108	screen's bottom edge). `cam_mast` bolts to `base_front` with 2× M3.
109	
110	> **⚠️ A reversed FFC is FATAL on first power-on** — board pin *N* would meet
111	> camera pin *25−N*, dead-shorting a power rail into a data/ground pin. **Verify
112	> orientation with a meter before powering.** Verified-good chain (2026-07-30):
113	>
114	> ```
115	> camera pin 1 → pigtail "1" → coupler P1.1 (left) → P2.1 (left)
116	>              → 30 cm cable pin-1 (dotted edge) → J2 pin 1 (BOTTOM end of J2)
117	> ```
118	>
119	> Key facts for this module: the **coupler is a straight 1:1 extender** (silk
120	> `1`-left / `24`-right on both ports), **J2 pin 1 = the bottom end** (board silk
121	> prints `24` at the top), and the camera's **grounds are not bonded internally**
122	> — so you can't confirm orientation by probing *through* the camera; trust the
123	> silkscreen `1`/`24` marks and bare-copper (`000.x`) continuity only. Keep the
124	> ~30 cm run in a small **service loop** at the yoke foot for strain relief, and
125	> route it away from the stepper leads to keep noise off the DVP clock/data lines.
126	
127	## Assembly
128	
129	1. Mount the **28BYJ-48** to `plate_stepper` (flange screws).
130	2. Press the rotor's **D-socket** onto the stepper shaft.
131	3. Drop the rotor into the `housing` bore.
132	4. Fit `plate_idle` on the far end — its boss is the rotor's stub axle.
133	5. Bolt both plates to the housing (4 × M3).
134	6. Plug the `hopper` spigot into the inlet; put a bowl under the outlet.
135	
136	## Calibration — do this once
137	
138	1. Fill the hopper.
139	2. Dispense a single pocket.
140	3. Weigh what lands in the bowl.
141	4. Put that number in `GRAMS_PER_POCKET` in `board/esp32s3_st7789.c` and rebuild.
142	
143	Portions are then correct at any hopper level, for the life of the machine. If you want a different dose granularity, change `WIDTH` in the `.scad` (pocket volume scales linearly with it) and re-calibrate.
144	
145	`POCKETS` in the `.scad` must always equal `ROTOR_POCKETS` in the board file.

output: English | 中文 # VelaPaw —— 端侧 AI 多宠智能喂食器 **队伍：** CircuitForge（`contest2026_043`） · **赛道：** AI 硬件产品创新 **平台：** openVela（NuttX），运行于 Waveshare **ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C** **代码仓库：** [github.com/open-vela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge](https://github.com/open-vela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge) —— 源码已提交至大赛专属分支 **`dev-ai-contest-2026`** --- ## 演示视频 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41dbdc26-3da1-4739-bab1-6db7f95bbd13 ▶ 如果上方的嵌入视频无法加载，可以[直接下载](VelaPaw_Demo.mp4)（58MB，MP4）。建议您下载视频以获得更好的画质。 --- ## 一、作品简介 **VelaPaw 是一款智能宠物喂食器：它能识别出正站在食盆前的是*哪一只*宠物，并只投喂这只宠物当前应吃的那一餐——而所有 AI 全部在设备端本地运行。无需云端、无需手机、无需账号。** 在多宠家庭里，普通的定时喂食器分不清是哪只猫，结果往往是最贪吃的那只把大家的粮都吃了，定量管理根本无从谈起。VelaPaw 用和人一样的方式解决它：先"看"一眼动物、认出是谁，再只投喂它自己的那份口粮，并按它自己的时间表。由于摄像头、神经网络、时钟和投料机构全部自成一体，它在断网时照常工作，也绝不会把家里的画面上传到任何地方。 **核心亮点** - 🐾 **逐只宠物识别** —— 端侧 INT8 神经网络凭面部识别每一只已登记的宠物，无需项圈或标签。 - 🍽️ **识别门控投喂** —— 只有当"识别到正确的宠物在食盆前"**且**"它的某一餐已到时间且未被跳过"时才投喂，且每餐每天至多一次。每一餐都可单独设置**跳过（skip-meal）**开关。 - 🗣️ **语音设置时间表** —— 投喂时间也可以直接说出来：由端侧关键词识别模型驱动的 MEAL→HOUR→CONFIRM 语音对话，可免触摸设置某只宠物的投喂时间。**没有唤醒词** —— 需先在编辑宠物页面点击开始，再用语音依次回答。VelaPaw 不含常驻语音唤醒功能，因此大赛"参赛须知与规则"中关于统一唤醒词的要求不适用于本项目。 - ⚖️ **份量与每日上限** —— 每只宠物可设定克数份量，并有每日投喂硬上限。 - 🩺 **健康监测** —— 第二个端侧网络估计体况（偏瘦 / 理想 / 偏胖），进食历史分析还会发出**食欲骤降告警**，这是疾病的早期信号。 - 🕑 **真实计时** —— 硬件实时时钟（RTC）让投喂时间表在断电后依然准确。 - 🌐 **中英双语界面** —— 支持中文/英文，应用内可实时切换语言。 - 💾 **数据持久化** —— 已登记的宠物、时间表与宠物头像都能在断电后保留。 - 🖥️ **即开即用的家电体验** —— 上电直接进入触摸屏界面，无需连接串口控制台。 **为什么是现在：** 2026 年 3 月，小米推出了米家智能宠物喂食器 2 视觉版——一款面向大众市场的量产产品（众筹价 ¥449，零售价 ¥549），专门加入摄像头把 AI 视觉带进喂食场景。这等于是最懂宠物主人会为什么买单的公司，用真金白银的量产产品独立验证了 VelaPaw 立项时的核心判断——摄像头理应长在喂食器上。VelaPaw 在此基础上更进一步：从"看到食盆"到"认出是哪只宠物"，凭面部识别、完全端侧运行，无需 App、账号或云端。完整对比见项目介绍文档[§06 市场与价值](VelaPaw_Project_Intro_zh.pdf)。 --- ## 二、端侧 AI（项目的核心） 识别采用的是**开集度量学习（open-set metric learning）**，而非固定类别的分类器。模型是一个通用的宠物特征提取器（MobileNetV3-Small 主干 + 空间注意力 TSFM 模块），它把一帧摄像头画面转换成一个经 L2 归一化的 128 维**嵌入向量**。登记一只宠物即保存其若干张照片的平均嵌入；识别就是用余弦相似度与已登记宠物做匹配。正因如此，**新增一只宠物无需重新训练**——登记本身就是一等公民的功能，识别质量取决于登记照片的质量，而不是被冻结的类别集合。 | | | |---|---| | **身份识别模型** | MobileNetV3-Small + TSFM 注意力，INT8，128 维嵌入，128×128 输入 | | **体况评估模型** | 三分类（偏瘦/理想/偏胖）INT8 CNN | | **推理运行时** | TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers（`apps/mlearning/tflite-micro`） | | **加速** | 在 Xtensa LX7 上使用 ESP-NN SIMD 算子 → **约 1.3 秒/次推理**（参考算子约 6.75 秒） | | **模型存放** | 运行时从闪存加载（1.4 MB 身份模型 @ `0x600000`，626 KB 体况模型 @ `0x760000`）——因体积过大无法内存映射，开机时读入 PSRAM | 两个模型均在设备外训练，训练/导出流程见 [`host/`](host/)（TensorFlow/Keras → INT8 训练后量化 → `.tflite`）。 --- ## 三、工作原理 —— 从摄像头到猫粮 Shell cwd was reset to c:\Users\VICTUS\openVela

## 三、工作原理 —— 从摄像头到猫粮

```
   摄像头画面 ──► 嵌入向量（TFLM，INT8）──► 与已登记宠物做余弦匹配
                                                    │
                                          识别出的宠物 + 分数
                                                    │
                                    这只宠物今天是否有某一餐已到时间且尚未投喂？
                                               │是             │否
                                          投喂 N 克         提示"下一餐 18:00"
                                   （28BYJ-48 步进电机驱动叶轮）
                                               │
                                    记入历史 · 更新趋势 · 体况检测
```

中间的那道"门控"正是本作品的核心：只靠识别，会把贪吃的宠物喂上一整天；只靠定时，又会喂到碰巧站在旁边的那只。**两者必须同时满足。**

**软件架构**（清晰的 HAL 分层，位于 [`app/velapaw/`](app/velapaw/)）：

- `ui/` —— LVGL 触摸屏界面（登记 · 识别 · 我的宠物 · 趋势）
- `infer/` —— 推理接口 + TFLite-Micro 后端 + 训练好的模型
- `identity/` —— 登记存储、余弦匹配器、逐宠物闪存持久化、宠物头像
- `store/` —— 进食历史与行为分析
- `hal/` —— 摄像头（OV5640）与投料机构（28BYJ-48 步进电机）的硬件抽象

**板级支持**（[`board/`](board/)）—— 自定义板文件驱动显示屏、通过 ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM 外设驱动 OV5640 摄像头、通过 I²C 驱动 PCF85063 RTC，并经 ULN2003 用四个 GPIO 驱动投料的 **28BYJ-48 步进电机**（IN1–IN3/IN4 用 GPIO9/10/11/**43**）。显示屏运行于 **40 MHz 硬件 SPI + DMA**。ES8311 音频编解码器独占的 I²S 总线（GPIO12–16，未接到任何排针）驱动板载麦克风与扬声器，用于语音设置时间表。

---

## 四、端侧 AI Agent（唯一需要联网的部分）

openVela **`ai_agent`** 框架运行在同一颗 ESP32-S3 上，作为叠加在已完成的喂食器**之上**的一层。它让 VelaPaw 多了一种有用的方式：不必主人走到屏幕前查看，设备会自己读取喂食记录，在情况不对时主动开口。

**设备上实际运行的内容**

| | |
|---|---|
| **自定义 Skill** | 位于 `/data/ai_agent/skills/` 的喂食简报 Skill —— 读取 VelaPaw 每次投喂时写入闪存的喂食记录，生成逐只宠物的摘要：克数、餐次，以及相对该宠物自身基线的食欲变化。 |
| **CLI 提问** | `ask how much did bob eat today` —— Agent 从设备闪存中读取实时记录并据此作答，而不是返回预设的固定回复。 |
| **主动推送** | 心跳任务按固定间隔重新读取记录，**仅在某只宠物越过预警阈值时**才推送提醒 —— 设备不出声，就说明一切正常。它无人值守自动触发，无需有人守在控制台前。（演示固件使用 3 分钟的短间隔，以便在一次演示中就能看到推送触发；量产产品会采用小时级间隔。） |

**离线与联网 —— 边界在哪里**

> **喂食器本体从不需要联网。** 识别、投喂时间表、份量与每日上限控制、体况评估、进食历史与趋势、语音对话以及整个界面，全部在 ESP32-S3 端侧运行，不依赖任何网络。拔掉网络，VelaPaw 照常识别宠物并按时投喂，与之前完全一样。
>
> **Agent 层是唯一需要联网的部分**，因为它要通过设备的 USB 网络接口（CDC-NCM）访问云端大模型。断网时，`ask` 与主动推送会停止 —— 而其他一切都不会。任何投喂决策都不会在云端做出，也没有任何图像离开设备。

完整说明 —— 架构、Skill、框架补丁，以及已捕获的主动推送记录：**[docs/AI_AGENT_zh.md](docs/AI_AGENT_zh.md)**（[English](docs/AI_AGENT.md)）。设备端源码与补丁位于 [`agent/`](agent/)。

---

## 五、硬件

- **Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C** —— ESP32-S3，8 MB PSRAM，16 MB 闪存，320×480 ST7796 触摸屏，OV5640 摄像头，PCF85063 RTC。

> **为什么选这块板——同一颗 SoC，更合适的外设。** 这块板搭载的是与大赛提供的 ESP32-S3-EYE **完全相同的 ESP32-S3**，因此 openVela 移植、端侧推理和所有驱动都是在同一颗芯片上的工作。VelaPaw 额外需要的是一块**电容触摸屏**——登记宠物、编辑投喂时间、查看趋势都在屏上完成——以及一个**实时时钟**，让投喂时间表在断电后依然有效。ESP32-S3-EYE 是一块面向视觉/语音的开发板，屏幕小且不支持触摸，也没有 RTC；而 Waveshare Touch-LCD-3.5-C 把产品所依赖的 3.5″ 触摸屏、OV5640 摄像头与 PCF85063 RTC 集成在同一块板上。同一平台，选用了更合适的载板。

- **投料机构** —— **28BYJ-48 步进电机**（经 ULN2003 驱动）驱动的**叶轮（paddle-rotor）**投料器：叶轮每转过一格就量出一"兜"固定体积的粮，因此份量取决于转动格数，而与料斗内余量多少无关。完整参数化 3D 模型、可打印 STL 与物料清单见 [`hardware/`](hardware/)。
- **摄像头走 30 cm 排线** —— OV5640 从主板拔下，用 30 cm 排线 + 1:1 转接板引到位于食盆前方的独立 **`cam_mast`** 支架，从而屏幕朝向主人、镜头对准宠物。（排线反插在上电瞬间是致命的——已用万用表核对方向，见 [`hardware/README.md`](hardware/README.md)。）

## 七、编译与运行（真机）

```bash
# 1. 拉取 openVela 与本队仓库
repo init -u https://github.com/open-vela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge \
  -b dev-ai-contest-2026 -m contest2026_043_CircuitForge.xml
repo sync -c -j8

# 2. 将板文件放入 ESP32-S3 板级目录
BOARD=nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit
cp contest2026_043_CircuitForge/board/esp32s3_st7789.c   $BOARD/src/
cp contest2026_043_CircuitForge/board/esp32s3_appinit.c  $BOARD/src/
cp contest2026_043_CircuitForge/board/esp32s3_bringup.c  $BOARD/src/
cp contest2026_043_CircuitForge/board/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig \
   $BOARD/configs/waveshare_lcd/defconfig

# 3. 编译（在 openVela 工作区根目录执行）
./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j8

# 4. 烧录固件 + 两个端侧模型

  0x0        nuttx/nuttx.bin \
  0x600000   contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/infer/model/velapaw.tflite \
  0x760000   contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/infer/model/bcs.tflite
```

本项目全程采用 AI 辅助（AI Coding）开发，完整会话日志已按要求提交于 [`logs/`](logs/)。AI 贯穿了整个开发生命周期：

三、技术报告

3.1 绪论

3.1.1 背景与问题定义

多宠家庭里，普通定时喂食器有一个结构性缺陷：它不知道站在食盆前的是哪一只宠物。到点开盖，先到的那只把所有粮都吃掉，慢的那只挨饿——按只定量、按只控重、按只观察食欲，全部无从谈起。而"按只定量"恰恰是宠物医生给出减重、控病、术后恢复方案时的第一条要求。

市面上已有的"视觉款"喂食器（例如 2026 年 3 月上市的小米米家智能宠物喂食器 2 视觉版，众筹 ¥449 / 零售 ¥549）解决的是"让主人看得见食盆"，摄像头的产物是一路视频流；它并不解决"认出是哪一只"。这类产品同时把摄像头画面与账号绑定上云——这是宠物主人对家庭摄像头最主要的顾虑来源。

因此 VelaPaw 定义的问题是：

在一台 MCU 级设备上，不联网、不上云、不用手机 App，仅凭一颗摄像头就分辨出食盆前是哪一只宠物，并只投喂"这一只、此时此刻该吃的那一餐"；同时把每只宠物的进食量长期记录下来，在食欲异常时主动告知主人。

"主动告知"这一层由 openVela 的 ai_agent 框架承担，是全系统唯一需要联网的部分；喂食器本体在断网状态下功能完全不变。

3.1.2 技术难点

难点具体表现
①端侧细粒度识别的算力** 宠物个体识别属于细粒度识别，需要 MobileNet 级主干 + 度量学习头。在 Xtensa LX7 上用 TFLite-Micro 参考算子跑该模型需 ≈6.75 s/次，完全不可用。前期 TFLM 摸底（docs/TFLM_SPIKE_REPORT.md）用 profiler 定量确认：CONV_2D 占单次推理 84% 的时钟（643 819 / 768 105 ticks），即延迟几乎完全由 INT8 卷积核决定，而 openVela 树内只有 cmsis-nn(ARM) 与 nnlib-hifi4(HiFi DSP)，没有面向 LX7 的算子库。
②"新增一只宠物"不能重训 消费产品不可能让用户为了加一只猫去训练模型。必须放弃 N 分类，改用开集度量学习，且阈值要在真实光照下站得住。
③大模型放不进 MCU 的内存映射 1.44 MB 的身份模型无法作为 const 数组内存映射——ESP32-S3 的 DROM0 MMU 窗口远在此之前就饱和。必须从裸 Flash 读入 PSRAM；而 Flash 读会挂起 CPU cache，而 PSRAM 正是经该 cache 访问的，读模型的线程栈若落在 PSRAM 会直接死锁整颗 SoC。
④硬件 SPI 屏幕"渲染不出来" 全屏写正常，任何局部窗口（CASET/RASET 子矩形 + RAMWR）永不出图，而同样的字节序列走 GPIO 位翻转完全正常。该问题历经约 60 轮盲目编译未能解决。
⑤ai_agent 在 MCU 上的请求体 vs. 网络缓冲 ai_agent 默认注册 36 个工具，其 JSON schema 使单次 LLM 请求体达 19 391 B，其中 9 946 B 是工具 schema；而 NuttX 的 IOB 池仅 NBUFFERS(64) × BUFSIZE(196) = 12 544 B，扣除 THROTTLE(24) 后可用约 7 840 B。请求体远大于可用缓冲，表现为"时好时坏"的挂死，且无超时返回。
⑥Agent 答案"看起来对"但其实是假的 心跳任务会重放自己的历史、list_dir 的前缀匹配与本地工具短路会把 (no files found) 直接当成最终答案交给用户、ask 在第 7 个词处被 MAX_ARGS 截断。这些缺陷都不会报错，只会让回答变得流畅而错误。

3.1.3 创新点

  1. "识别 × 排程"双条件门控投喂——只有"认出的是这只宠物"且"它的某一餐已到点且今天未投"两个条件同时成立才投料，每餐每天至多一次，且每餐可单独跳过。只靠识别会把贪吃的那只喂一整天；只靠定时又会喂到碰巧路过的那只。这个"与"门是整个产品的核心逻辑，也是"按只定量"能成立的前提。
  2. 开集度量学习替代分类器——模型只做"通用宠物特征提取器"，把 128×128 帧映射成 L2 归一化的 128 维嵌入；登记 = 存若干张照片的平均嵌入；识别 = 余弦相似度匹配。新增宠物是纯运行时操作，无需重训、无需固件更新。
  3. 把一个卡了 60 轮的 bug 变成 4× 提速——用逻辑分析仪把"软件问题"证伪为"面板位同步问题"（详见 3.4.3），修复后顺势把显示从位翻转升级为 40 MHz 硬件 SPI + GDMA，全屏重绘 246 ms → 61 ms。
  4. ai_agent 作为"沉默的健康监护"，而不是聊天机器人——心跳任务定期读取喂食器自己写在 Flash 上的记录，只在越过阈值时才开口；一切正常时设备完全沉默。自定义 Skill 明确规定"只能使用文件里的数字，绝不臆造"。
  5. "离线为主、联网为辅"的清晰边界——所有投喂决策与全部图像处理都在端侧完成，没有任何图像离开设备；拔掉网线，喂食器行为完全不变，只是 Agent 层停止工作。这既是隐私主张，也是可靠性主张。
  6. 逐"兜"定量的机械设计——用连续单向旋转的叶轮转子取代翻板：翻板的投放量随料斗余量漂移，而转子每格容积固定，克数 = 格数 × 每格克数，使"按只定量"在机械层面也成立。

3.2.2 方案论证与选型

决策点最终选型论证 / 被否方案
识别范式开集度量学习（余弦匹配）否决 N 分类：每加一只宠物都要重训并 OTA，消费产品不可接受。度量学习把"加宠物"降级为写一条 Flash 记录。代价是对"非宠物物体"的拒识天然较弱，因此把杠杆放在登记质量（近距、光照良好的正脸）而非阈值本身。
推理运行时TFLite-Micro + ESP-NN前期用树内 tflm_benchmark 在模拟器上摸底，确认 集成可行、算子全覆盖、张量竞技场仅 84 420 B（8 MB PSRAM 下可忽略），并定位延迟瓶颈在 CONV_2D（84%）。据此判定必须引入 LX7 SIMD 算子（ESP-NN），否则方案不成立。
模型存放裸 Flash 分区 + 开机读入 PSRAM否决 const 数组内存映射：1.44 MB 远超 DROM0 MMU 窗口。改用 spi_flash_read；因 Flash 读会挂起 cache，读取线程的栈必须放在内部 SRAM（.bss）而非 PSRAM。
投料机构28BYJ-48 步进 + 叶轮转子否决 MG90S 舵机 + 翻板：舵机只能往复摆动，进出料口相隔 180° 时净转角为零的摆动永远无法把一"兜"粮送过去，只会投出初始装载量后空转；翻板的投放量还随料斗余量漂移，直接摧毁"按只定量"的产品主张。步进电机连续单向旋转使 克数 = 格数 × 每格克数 严格成立，且减速箱低速扭矩大，抗卡粮。
载板Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C与官方 ESP32-S3-EYE 同一颗 SoC，openVela 移植与推理工作完全共通；但产品需要电容触摸屏（登记 / 编辑排程 / 看趋势）与硬件 RTC（断电后排程仍准），EYE 二者皆无。同平台，换更合适的载板。
板载网络USB CDC-NCM 复合设备否决 RNDIS：Windows 的 rndismp6.sys 硬性要求 RNDIS 位于接口 0，与 CDC-ACM 控制台冲突，实测 Code-10 无法规避。CDC-NCM 使控制台（COM 口）与网卡（eth0）在一根 USB 线上同时可用。否决板载 Wi-Fi 作为演示链路：Wi-Fi 已打通并保留在配置中，但演示环境下 USB 复合链路的可复现性更高。
Agent 数据桥喂食器写 Markdown，Agent 用 read_file 读否决自定义工具 / IPC / 共享内存：VelaPaw C 应用每次投喂后把纯文本 Markdown 写到 /data/ai_agent/velapaw/{status,feed_log}.md，Agent 用框架原生的 read_file 读取。零新增工具、零新增协议、零耦合；对 Agent 而言它就是一个普通文件，对 C 应用而言它就是一次 fprintf。
Agent 持久化littlefs @ 0x180000 挂载 /data否决 tmpfs：API Key、会话历史、Skill 文件每次重启都要重新灌入。littlefs 分区起始于 0x180000，而 write-flash 0x0 nuttx.bin 只写到约 0x17ec80，因此 /data 能跨重启、也跨重新烧录固件保留。
云端模型DeepSeek deepseek-chatOpenAI 兼容接口，框架原生支持 function-calling；国内可直连、时延与费用可控。

3.2.3 断网 / 弱网降级策略

这是本作品在方案层刻意设计的一条边界，也是"AI 硬件"与"联网硬件"的分水岭。

功能断网说明
宠物识别（INT8 推理）✅ 正常模型在 Flash / PSRAM 本地，无任何网络依赖。
识别门控投喂 / 每日上限✅ 正常纯本地状态机 + RTC。
体况评估、进食历史与趋势✅ 正常第二个端侧模型 + littlefs 本地历史。
语音排程对话（KWS）✅ 正常端侧关键词模型，不走网络。
触摸界面全部功能✅ 正常LVGL 本地渲染。
Agent ask 问答⛔ 停止需访问云端 LLM。失败时在控制台给出明确的 [llm] API error 行，不产生虚构回答。
Agent 主动健康推送⛔ 静默心跳任务照常触发、照常读取本地文件，仅 LLM 调用失败；不会误报，也不会丢数据——恢复联网后下一次心跳即可基于完整历史给出结论。

弱网处理分三层：（1）传输层——vela_tls 维护到 api.deepseek.com:443 的连接池并复用（控制台可见 [vela_tls] Reusing pooled connection）；空闲 keep-alive 被服务端关闭时会出现零字节响应，框架在带内自动重连，实测 3/3 恢复，该现象不是缺陷。（2）超时层——针对 MCU 上的真实往返，把 AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SEC 放宽到 420 s、socket 超时 480 s；此前 60 s 的默认值会把一个已经成功返回的 62.6 s 回答直接丢弃。（3）请求体层——见 3.3.3 的工具裁剪，把请求体压到 IOB 池能承载的范围，这是弱网下最有效的一条。

3.3 核心算法与技术原理

3.3.1 端侧模型

项身份识别模型体况评估模型 / KWS
任务宠物个体识别（开集）体况三分类（偏瘦/理想/偏胖）；语音关键词识别
结构MobileNetV3-Small 主干 + 空间注意力 TSFM 模块 + ArcFace 度量学习头紧凑 3 类 CNN；14 标签 KWS 卷积网络
输入 / 输出128×128 → L2 归一化 128 维嵌入体况：3 类 logits；KWS：14 类 softmax
框架训练：TensorFlow / Keras（host/）；推理：TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers（apps/mlearning/tflite-micro）
量化INT8 训练后量化（PTQ），算子全部为 TFLM 内置算子
模型体积1.44 MB（Flash 0x600000）626 KB（Flash 0x760000）；KWS 模型内嵌在固件 rodata
算子集ADD, CONV_2D, DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D, FULLY_CONNECTED, L2_NORMALIZATION, LOGISTIC, MEAN, MUL, PAD（9 个，均为默认 resolver 支持）
算力占用单次推理 ≈1.3 s（ESP-NN SIMD 算子）／ ≈6.75 s（TFLM 参考算子），加速比 ≈5×。张量竞技场实测 84 420 B（非持久 55 296 B + 持久 29 124 B），在 8 MB PSRAM 下占比可忽略。计算分布：CONV_2D 约 84%、DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D 约 16%。
内存放置两个 .tflite 以裸块写入 Flash，开机由 spi_flash_read 读入 PSRAM 缓冲；读取线程的栈必须位于内部 SRAM（.bss），因为 Flash 读会挂起 PSRAM 所依赖的 cache。

ESP-NN 集成方式与合规说明。1.3 s 这一数字依赖 Espressif 的 ESP-NN（Apache-2.0）SIMD 算子，而该集成修改的是公共仓 apps/mlearning/tflite-micro。按大赛规则，公共仓改动以 fork + PR 形式提交到 dev-ai-contest-2026，不并入队伍仓。因此本队仓开箱即用时跑的是参考算子（≈6.75 s），套用 ESP-NN fork 后为 ≈1.3 s。集成由三部分组成：（1）apps/mlearning/esp-nn/ 引入库本体；（2）7 个算子包装（conv / depthwise_conv / fully_connected / pooling / add / mul / softmax）放入 .../micro/kernels/esp_nn/；（3）Makefile 块以 -DESP_NN=1 -DCONFIG_NN_OPTIMIZED -mlongcalls 编译并过滤掉对应的参考算子以避免符号重复。完整包装代码与复现步骤见 docs/esp-nn/。

3.3.3 关键机制

（1）识别门控投喂状态机。

if  匹配分数 ≥ 0.45  且  匹配到的是宠物 P
and 存在一餐 M 属于 P，其时刻已到、今日未投、未被跳过
and P 今日累计克数 + 本餐克数 ≤ P 的每日上限
then 投料 (克数 / 每格克数) 格 → 记录 feed 事件 → 更新 status.md / feed_log.md
else 界面提示"下一餐 18:00"，不投料

（2）工具注册表裁剪——本项目单点收益最大的一处改动。问题的量化形态见 3.1.2⑥。做法是在 tool_registry.c 的 s_excluded_tools 中排除 20 个与喂食器无关的工具（4 个可穿戴 + 6 个飞书 + 8 个音乐 + 2 个快应用），工具数 36 → 16，工具 JSON 4 706 B。效果：可靠性从"时好时坏"变为 8/8 全通，端到端时延从 150–300 s 降到 3.6–35.6 s。

连带缺陷（值得写进报告的工程教训）：裁掉工具会留下调用方。这次裁剪孤立了 5 条自然语言快捷路径、1 段手写的 music_search 分支，以及每份系统提示里的飞书文案；而 handle_nl_fast_path() 运行在 LLM 之前，因此指向未注册工具的快捷路径会把空白/错误结果当作最终答案返回给用户。检查方法固定为改动 s_excluded_tools 后 grep 一次被裁工具名，要求返回为空。

（3）三类"静默错误"的修复。它们的共同特征是答案读起来很通顺，但不是从数据来的：

  • 心跳重放自己的历史——持久化的会话历史跨重启存活，导致第 2 次以后的心跳在"复读"。history_json 在循环外只 calloc 一次，因此需要显式写入 '\0'。
  • list_dir 前缀匹配 + 本地工具短路——前缀是按绝对路径匹配的，而模型传的是相对路径；又因该工具位于本地短路集合中，(no files found) 被直接当成最终答案交给了主人。修法是同时接受两种路径写法（模型实际会用三种）。
  • 陈旧的控制台历史抑制工具调用——修法不是裁剪历史，而是在消息数组中部插入一条 system 消息强制重新读取；磁盘上的旧历史原样保留，结果仍为 iters=3 tools=2 且答案正确。
  • ask 在第 7 个词处截断——根因是 nsh_commands.c 的 MAX_ARGS 8，已提升到 32。

（4）验证方法论。本项目对"看起来能用"保持高度不信任，固化了三条判据：END status=ok iters=N tools=M 才是真信号（iters=1 tools=0 的完美回答等于历史重放）；[skills] Skills summary: NNN bytes 才证明 Skill 加载成功（Skills system ready (N built-in) 是编译期常量，什么也不证明）；判断回答是否真的来自远端，用 在运行中途登记一只新宠物——若下一次触发能发现它，就排除了 RAM 内 llm_cache 重放的可能。

3.3.4 openVela 系统能力的深度运用

VelaPaw 不是"跑在 BSP 上的一个薄应用"，而是纵向贯穿了 openVela 的图形、AI、多媒体、文件系统、USB 与网络子系统。三大能力方向全部落地：

3.3.5 对 openVela 的改进建议

以下 6 条均来自本项目真机踩坑，按"对下一位开发者的价值"排序：

  1. 为 Xtensa LX7 提供官方的 TFLM 优化算子路径（ESP-NN）。树内现有 cmsis-nn（ARM）与 nnlib-hifi4（HiFi DSP），唯独缺少 LX7；而 ESP32-S3 是本届大赛的主力芯片。差距是 6.75 s → 1.3 s（5×），直接决定"端侧视觉 AI 在 openVela 上是否可用"。建议以 Kconfig 开关的形式内置，而非让每支队伍各自 fork。
  2. mallinfo() / free / memdump 在刚启动的板子上会持锁挂死整颗芯片。本项目中 ai_agent 恰好把堆遍历放在 agent 任务的第一条语句，于是每一次 ask 都冻结全机（曾一度被误判为 PSRAM 问题）。建议：堆遍历接口增加非阻塞/超时形态，或至少在文档中标注其持锁语义。
  3. ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS 是 select 符号，永远不出现在 defconfig 中。而它恰恰是"任务栈不落在 PSRAM"的三个必要符号之一，缺一个就在首次 ask 时死锁。建议在 XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP 的帮助文本中显式提示这一依赖。
  4. IOB 池默认容量与 ai_agent 的默认请求体不匹配。默认 36 个工具产生 19 KB 请求体，而默认 IOB 可用约 7.8 KB，症状是无超时的间歇挂死——最难排查的一类故障。建议：ai_agent 默认精简工具集，或在 MCU 目标上对请求体大小做启动期断言。
  5. ai_agent 的"本地工具短路"应保证与工具注册表一致。handle_nl_fast_path() 早于 LLM 执行，一旦其目标工具被排除，错误结果会作为最终答案返回用户，且无任何告警。建议编译期校验短路表 ⊆ 已注册工具集。
  6. 几处"会静默毁掉整机"的配置项值得在 Kconfig 帮助文本中警示：CONFIG_RTC（在本板上会杀死 USB 控制台）、CONFIG_NETINIT_THREAD（挂死整机）、CONFIG_DEBUG_USB_INFO（塞死控制台）；以及 CONFIG_NSH_LINELEN 会在约 80 字符处静默截断输入行，用 echo … >> /long/path provision 文件时会写出损坏内容而不报错。

3.4.3 硬件设计与适配

是否完成全新硬件平台适配 / 驱动开发：是。Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C 在 openVela 中没有现成板级支持。本项目在 esp32s3-devkit 基础上新增了一份完整的板级实现（board/，共 1 903 行 C 代码 + 205 行 defconfig），从零驱动了以下四类外设：

外设接法驱动实现要点
ST7796 触摸屏
320×480		硬件 SPI2 + GDMA，40 MHz；CLK=GPIO5, MOSI=GPIO1, CS=GPIO4；触摸 FT5x06 走 I²C0(SCL=7/SDA=8)见下方"最硬的一处调试"。像素行需经内部 SRAM 中转缓冲——SPI DMA 无法 cache 一致地读 PSRAM；地址窗口设置从 11 次 SPI 调用合并为 5 次（LVGL 每次 putarea 都会重设窗口）。
OV5640 摄像头ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM 外设 + GDMA 接收通道，SCCB/I²C 配置；经 30 cm FFC + 1:1 转接板外引预览曾出现90° 转置 + 紫色偏色，两个独立根因：（a）翻转/镜像位——须清除 0x3820/0x3821 的 bit1+bit2，转置本身只能在软件重采样中修正，寄存器结构上做不到；（b）BLC pattern 寄存器 0x4514 须置 0x88。判别方法是一条可复用的规律：整帧色相是决定性判据——翻转/Bayer 相位错误只会红蓝互换、绝不可能丢掉绿色，因此"紫色（R+B 无 G）"必然是 0x4514，不是翻转位。
PCF85063 RTCI²C0，裸寄存器读写刻意不使用 CONFIG_RTC——在本板上它会杀死 USB-CDC 控制台。开机时间种子设计为以构建日期为下限的地板值而非"早于 2017 即视为无效"的合理性判断：后者会把板子永久钉在某一天且无法纠正（wall_set_min 只改时分，nsh 没有 date）。
28BYJ-48 步进投料ULN2003 驱动板，IN1–IN4 = GPIO9 / 10 / 11 / 43；5 V 独立供电，仅共地软件走全步序列。IN4 必须用 GPIO43（U0TXD）而不是 GPIO44（U0RXD）——GPIO44 被钳位，线圈驱动不干净，这正是早期"电机嗡嗡响但不转"的根因（是引脚问题，不是相序问题）。GPIO43 可用是因为控制台走 USB-Serial/JTAG 而非 UART0。严禁把步进放在 GPIO12–16——那是 ES8311 编解码器独占的 I²S 总线（未引到任何排针），已被语音功能占用。
ES8311 音频I²S0：MCLK=12, BCLK=13, DIN=14, WS=15, DOUT=16；16 kHz为打通麦克风采集，定位并修复了驱动层缺陷：从未编程 RX 的 TDM slot map（RX 通道卡死的真正根因）。另有 PSRAM cache 陷阱迫使采用 18 缓冲池的双 slot 流（活动 slot 每次采集翻转）。

最硬的一处调试：硬件 SPI 屏幕。症状是全屏写正常、任何局部窗口永不出图，而完全相同的字节序列走位翻转却正常；该问题熬过了约 60 轮编译（帧缓冲镜像、DMA 开关、软件 CS、PSRAM 一致性、引脚强制路由等全部无效）。

  • 方法——测量，而不是猜。SPI 引脚没有引到排针，无法直接探测，于是让板级固件通过 GPIO 矩阵把 FSPID_OUT/FSPICLK_OUT 镜像到空闲排针，另加一路触发标记，用逻辑分析仪（sigrok/PulseView + FX2）抓取。决定性的第一步是"地面真值"测试：先在探针脚上输出 4 路已知方波，读不干净就绝不相信任何采集——这一步立刻暴露了一个接线/接地问题，此前的"乱码"全部源于此；只有在此之后，真正的采集才是可信的。
  • 发现。解码结果显示 ESP32 发出的是逐字节完全正确的 CASET 00 28 00 8B / RASET 00 28 00 8B / RAMWR / pixels，DC 对齐正确、每字节恰好 8 个干净时钟沿、零毛刺。外设自始至终是清白的。
  • 根因。该面板的片选被硬件拉低，因此它永远无法借助 CS 边沿重新同步位计数器——它只会一直数时钟沿。固件先用位翻转完成面板初始化，之后才把引脚交给 SPI 外设；这次引脚交接会让时钟多出/少掉一个沿，从那一刻起面板就错开了一位。此后每条命令都被解码成垃圾，RAMWR 永不被识别，没有像素进入 GRAM，屏幕就一直显示位翻转最后画上去的内容——看起来正好像"硬件 SPI 什么都没画"。
  • 修复。先把引脚交给 SPI 外设，再硬件复位面板（软件复位不行——复位命令自己就会被读错），然后整套初始化全部走 SPI。面板在 SPI 所有权下重新同步之后，局部窗口即正常渲染。
  • 收益。路径打通后，显示彻底脱离位翻转，改用 40 MHz 硬件 SPI2 + GDMA：全屏 480×320 重绘 ≈246 ms → ≈61 ms（4×）。一个看似死路的 bug 变成了性能提升。

机械设计（hardware/）。重力料斗 → 叶轮转子 → 落料槽 → 食盆。全部零件为参数化 OpenSCAD 源码 + 可直接打印的 STL（PLA/PETG，0.2 mm 层高，3 圈外壁，无支撑），含 JLC 代打件清单。摄像头从主板拔下，经 30 cm FFC + 1:1 转接板装在跨过落料槽的 cam_mast 双腿支架上的 cam_pod 内，使屏幕朝向主人、镜头朝向宠物。安全警示：FFC 反插在上电瞬间是致命的——板端第 N 脚会对上相机第 25−N 脚，把电源轨直接短到数据/地脚；且该相机模组内部地未共通，无法"穿过相机"用万用表确认方向，只能依据丝印 1/24 与裸铜连通性核对（已在 2026-07-30 逐点验证）。

3.4.4 应用 / 交互端设计

本产品没有配套 App、没有账号、没有云端控制台——这是产品定位的一部分，而不是功能缺失。交互全部发生在设备本体上：

交互面设计
触摸屏（主交互）四页 LVGL 界面：登记（拍几张近距正脸照 → 存平均嵌入）· 识别（实时预览 + 匹配结果 + 投喂）· 我的宠物（编辑姓名/餐次/克数/每日上限/单餐跳过，删除，头像）· 趋势（摄入柱状图、食欲折线、体况仪表）。上电直接进入界面（board_app_initialize() 自启），无需连接串口——它的行为像一台家电，而不是一块开发板。
语音（免触摸）MEAL→HOUR→CONFIRM 三步对话，在"编辑宠物"页点击开始后进行，用端侧 KWS 模型识别受限词表。真机端到端验证通过（例：COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00）。
双语中 / EN 应用内实时切换，含自制 Noto Sans SC 子集字库；全部界面文案、文档与 README 均为中英双语。
Agent 对话（控制台）ask <自然语言>，例：ask how much did bob eat today。回答来自设备本地记录，非预置文案。
Agent 主动推送心跳触发，无人值守；只在越阈值时开口。这是"不需要主人走到屏幕前"的那一层。

3.4.5 自定义 Skill（AI 硬件产品创新赛道硬性要求）

Skill 文件：velapaw-feeding-digest.md（喂食简报）
仓库位置：agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md
运行时路径：/data/ai_agent/skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md

路径说明：赛道指南给出的运行时 Skill 目录为 /data/agent/skills/；本实现使用的是 /data/ai_agent/skills/，因为这是当前 packages/ai_agent 框架在设备上实际扫描的目录（控制台日志 [skills] Skill exists: /data/ai_agent/skills/… 可证）。二者语义等价，如需对齐规范目录，只是一次挂载点重命名。

Skill 定义（全文）：

# VelaPaw Feeding Digest
Report pet feeding, appetite and body condition.

## When to use
When asked about a pet, feeding, how much a pet ate, appetite,
body condition or feeder status. Also used by the periodic heartbeat check.

## How to use
1. read_file /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md
   Per pet it gives grams today, meal count, 7-day total, baseline,
   appetite percent, body condition, daily limit.
2. read_file /data/ai_agent/velapaw/feed_log.md
   Recent feed events with timestamps and match score.
3. Report per pet: grams today vs the daily limit, appetite vs baseline,
   and body condition.
4. Flag a concern ONLY if any of these is true:
   - appetite below 50 percent of baseline
   - grams today reached the owner daily limit
   - body condition is not ideal
   - no feed event today in the log
5. Otherwise say the pet is on track, one sentence.
6. Use only numbers from those files. Never invent.

触发场景（两条，均已在真机上验证）：

  1. 被动触发 —— 主人提问。控制台输入 ask how is jay doing today 一类问题时命中 When to use，Agent 依次 list_dir → read_file(status.md) → read_file(feed_log.md)，据实际数字作答。真机实录：[llm] OpenAI API with tools (model: deepseek-chat, 11559 bytes) → END status=ok iters=3 tools=2 llm_ms=4340 elapsed=5s，回答内容为"Today: 15 g in 1 meal / Appetite: 34% of baseline (44 g/day) / Owner daily limit: 60 g/day"。
  2. 主动触发 —— 心跳健康巡检（本赛道要求的"主动 + 执行"场景）。/data/ai_agent/HEARTBEAT.md 中的任务项为："Run the VelaPaw Feeding Digest skill. If it finds a concern, notify the owner with numbers. If all is on track, reply HEARTBEAT_OK only." 心跳服务（用的是 heartbeat 服务，而非 cron）按固定间隔把该文件作为一条 system 消息注入会话并触发一轮完整的 agent loop。沉默是正常状态——只有越过 Skill 第 4 条的四个阈值之一才会推送。已捕获的无人值守实录：iters=4 tools=3，4 次 read_file，请求体依次 15 592 → 16 209 → 17 697 → 18 760 B。

为证明"这是真的在跑，而不是重放"，采用了一条可复现的判据：在心跳运行过程中登记一只新宠物，若下一次触发能够发现它，则排除 RAM 内 llm_cache 重放的可能。该测试已通过——每一次触发都是真实的远端调用。（此前确实存在"第 2 次以后的触发被缓存重放"的缺陷，已通过按 chat_id 绕过缓存修复。）

四项平台级修复（agent/patches/，3 个补丁 / 18 个文件 / +570 −190 行）——没有它们，ai_agent 在这块板子上根本跑不起来：

#问题修复
1ask 第一次调用即冻结整颗芯片根因：agent_loop 的 pthread 栈落在 PSRAM（0x3c…），而 littlefs 的 Flash 读会关闭 PSRAM 所依赖的 cache。修复为三个 Kconfig 符号：XTENSA_IMEM_USE_SEPARATE_HEAP + XTENSA_IMEM_REGION_SIZE=0x48000 + 极易遗漏的 ARCH_HAVE_EXTRA_HEAPS。0x30000 只够止住冻结但不够实际出货——所有任务与 pthread 栈都从这个堆里切，ai_agent 的任务加 6 个 pthread 再叠上 velapaw 的 48 KB 栈会让 pthread_create 返回 ENOMEM。
2堆遍历杀死刚启动的板子agent_loop_task 的第一条语句就是 mallinfo()，而 free/memdump/mallinfo 在刚启动的板子上会持堆锁挂死整机。改为不遍历堆的状态上报。（那个"676 MB 幽灵节点"是坏掉的遍历本身，不是内存损坏。）
3IOB 耗尽导致请求无声挂死IOB_NBUFFERS / IOB_NCHAINS = 64、IOB_THROTTLE = 24（160 条链虽然更大但无法启动），并需主机先 ping 板子把 ARP 打通。1420 vs 1514 的 MTU 差异真实存在但不是本故障的原因，不应去"修" PKTSIZE。
4LLM 超时把成功的回答丢掉AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SEC=420、socket 480。原 60 s 默认值会丢弃一次已成功返回的 62.6 s 回答，表面症状却是"请求超时"。

选用 accurate 模型的依据是可分间距（0.324 vs 0.243）与更低的 EER，代价是 +91 KB 体积与 +1 个算子——在 16 MB Flash / 8 MB PSRAM 的预算下这个代价可以忽略。

对该结果的诚实解读：EER 0.291 是在公开宠物数据集的 39 个个体、开集条件下测得的下界式指标，它衡量的是"任取两张图判断是否同一只"的难度，而不是产品实际场景的准确率。真实场景要容易得多：家庭中通常只有 2–4 只宠物、登记照由主人近距离正脸拍摄、匹配阈值取 0.45（高于 EER 阈值，偏向"宁可拒识、不可误投"）。误报/漏报的主导因素不是阈值，而是登记质量——这是开集度量学习的结构性特征：通用特征提取器天然难以拒绝任意非宠物物体，因此产品把杠杆放在引导用户拍出紧凑、光照良好的正脸照。尚未完成的量化工作：在最终相机姿态（cam_mast 支架、当前色彩标定）下针对自家 3 只宠物的误报率 / 漏报率长期统计。当前 3 只宠物的嵌入是在存在紫色偏色的固件版本下采集的，0x4514 修复后需要重新登记，此前的现场准确率数据不具备可比性，因此本报告不给出该数字，而不是给一个不可信的数字。

  • 断电恢复：硬件 RTC 保时间，littlefs 保宠物 / 排程 / 头像 / 进食历史 / Agent 会话与 Key。/data 起始于 0x180000，而固件只写到约 0x17ec80，因此重新烧录固件也不会丢数据。
  • 网络异常：见 3.2.3 降级表。LLM 失败时输出明确的 [llm] API error NNN:，不产生虚构回答。
  • 内存波动：本项目刻意不报告运行时堆余量数字——原因见 3.4.5 修复 #2：在这块板子上堆遍历接口会持锁杀死整机，修复方式是改为不遍历堆的状态上报，因此固件打印的堆数值是假定值而非实测值，作为量化指标引用会构成误导。真正约束内存的是编译期的 XTENSA_IMEM_REGION_SIZE：0x30000 时 pthread_create 返回 ENOMEM，0x48000 可稳定承载 ai_agent 任务 + 6 个 pthread + velapaw 的 48 KB 栈——这个"能/不能创建线程"的二值结果，比一个不可信的堆余量数字更有信息量。
  • 连续运行时长：已完成的最长受控观测为演示录制中的 600 s（sleep 600） 无人值守区间，期间心跳按期触发、控制台无异常、Agent 正常应答。更长时间的老化测试（24 h / 7 d）尚未进行，列入 3.7.3 的后续工作，本报告不做外推。
  • 功耗：尚未使用功率分析仪做逐工况测量，因此不给出数字。设计上的低功耗依据是"识别按需触发而非常开推理"（避免 1.3 s 级推理连续占用双核）与"投料仅在门控通过时短时驱动步进"；步进电机 ≈240 mA/相由独立 5 V 供电承担，不经过主板。定量测量列入后续工作。

3.5.5 结果分析

把测试结果放回 3.1.2 的六个难点：

  1. 难点①（算力）已解决且量化：6.75 s → 1.31 s。关键在于前期用 profiler 先确定"84% 的时间在 CONV_2D"，才把全部工程投入压在算子库上，而不是四处调参。先测量、后优化是本项目最有回报的一条方法论。
  2. 难点②（不重训）已解决：登记是纯运行时操作，真机验证通过。代价是拒识能力弱于闭集分类器，这一点在 3.5.4 中如实披露而非回避。
  3. 难点③（大模型加载）已解决：裸 Flash + PSRAM，附带产出了"Flash 读会挂 cache"这条对任何 ESP32-S3 + PSRAM + 大模型项目都通用的经验。
  4. 难点④（SPI 屏幕）已解决并转化为 4× 收益：60 轮盲试的失败与一次逻辑分析仪测量的成功，其差别不在努力程度，而在于是否把猜测换成了观测。
  5. 难点⑤（请求体 vs IOB）已解决且是单点收益最大项：可靠性"时好时坏 → 8/8"，时延 150–300 s → 3.6–35.6 s，仅靠删掉 20 个用不上的工具。这条经验对所有在 MCU 上跑 ai_agent 的团队都适用。
  6. 难点⑥（静默错误）已解决，并沉淀为判据：本项目最重要的产出之一是三条"读日志而不是读文案"的验收判据（END status= / Skills summary: NNN bytes / 运行中途注入新数据）。它们是把"看起来能用"和"确实在用"分开的工具。
